## Solar arrays on the graph (system_graph/graph_solar_arrays.gd, 2026-10-27)

Every solar array is ONE model, whatever made it: "array" (imported OSM,
the placed `pv_array` rack via `bind_pv_array_prop`, Make array) and
"pv_design" (an MPPT input of a Solar designer array, GraphPvLabArrays).
`GraphSolarArrays` owns what an array is.
- **Outside: one card**, the array branch of `GraphCardSpecs._group` for
  both kinds (topology chip, live watts summed from its panels through the
  card ctx `array_live_w` / `array_peak_w`, "Packed · " / "Stowed · "),
  ONE + / − pair on the bottom edge with **+ on the left**
  (`GraphArrayLayout.default_handles`, rx 0.33 / 0.67, the DC terminal
  convention; the old array bus had + on the right). Its picture is the
  real layout: `specs.array_cells` = {w_m, h_m, cells: [[x, y, w, h, idx,
  string]]} in METRES, face-on, north up (`cells_for_design` from the
  solved PvLab layout with tables a short gap apart, `cells_for_specs` from
  the placed rack's `array_cols` / `array_rows` or series × parallel).
  `canvas.draw_array_cells` draws it (card media, the pre-card body, the
  Site Plan chip): each cell tinted by its panel's live output, edged in its
  string's colour (`STRING_COLORS`). The card size frames that picture
  (`card_size`); `GraphArrayLayout.legacy_compound_size` is the old tiles.
- **Inside: the real panels**, placed at their cells (`interior_rects`: one
  scale, a node takes its cell's shape, the shortest side NODE_MIN_SIDE),
  so the inside has the picture's aspect and the existing zoom-through
  (`_view_for_bbox_in_rect`) grows the panels out of the picture.
  `build_interior` is shared by both kinds: series links are − → + between
  neighbours (short hops; the string's + is its first panel's, its − its
  last's), strings joined in parallel at the first string's ends, the
  compound's ports promoted from them. `strings_from_model` reads any + / −
  link as source-before-target (older saves wired + → −).
- **Hollow arrays are gone.** `materialize` gives an "array" its panels
  (`array_interior` "panels", `array_generated` true, `array_owner` on each
  panel) or, above `MATERIALIZE_MAX_PANELS` (120), one STRING-PROXY panel
  per string (`string_proxy`, `panel_count` = the string, voc / vmp / wmp
  × the string). `GraphNesting.is_transparent_compound` treats a
  materialized array as transparent, so flow, PvElectrical and the energy
  sum walk its panels; `is_aggregate_array` (a hollow one) is what the old
  `== "array"` sim readers check now (PvElectrical source / Voc / Vmp,
  `_collect_root_array_aggregate`'s compound branch, the cost sum).
  `_sync_array_compound_layouts` migrates on load (idempotent), renames
  legacy outer port ids to positive / negative and resizes the card round
  its centre; `_upgrade_designed_array_layouts` (after the map load, needs
  the props) gives older designed arrays their picture and moves their
  panels onto the rack without touching wires. A Make-array group is
  ADOPTED: panels that each left through the same port are joined in
  parallel inside, duplicate outside wires collapse.
- **Parity is pinned**: the selftest checks peak W, string Voc and
  controller sources before / after; `solar_array_parity_probe.gd` on Mount
  Vernon matched everything but 7 am solar, which FELL from 0.237 to 0.069
  kW because the old DC topology counted a STOWED 6 kW Linkage array in
  `total_wmp` (`_pv_item_wmp` ignored `array_stowed`) and so diluted the
  morning tree shade on the placed panel 3×. Panels of a packed / stowed
  array carry the flag (`propagate_state`, also the rack's tilt / azimuth)
  and `GraphSolarArrays.panel_off` zeroes them in `_pv_item_wmp`,
  `_pv_sun_factor` and the aggregate. Child panels carry no site coords, so
  they are not shade receivers (a follow-up).
- **Zoom in**: `GraphSolarArrays.zoom_enterable` replaced the
  `compound_kind != ""` gate in `_maybe_zoom_drill_in` /
  `prepare_and_try_zoom_drill` — that gate (there since July) is why arrays
  never opened on the wheel. Generic groups as before; arrays when they hold
  something; battery banks / load groups still do not. A touch double tap
  opens a compound like a double click. Inspector: "Expand → Panels" for both
  kinds, "Reset panels to layout" (`SystemGraphView.rebuild_array_interior`:
  regenerates a generated array, re-lays a designed / grouped one), and
  Retile rebuilds a generated array's panels.
- ⚠ Heredoc trap again: a `\\` line continuation inside a Python heredoc
  edit came out as a JOINED line in GDScript (two places this pass). Write
  edit scripts with the Write tool.

## Flow visualization: Sankey wires, the Flows lens (2026-11-12)

Plan + the catalog of further visualizations: `plans/FLOW_VIZ_PLAN.md`.
- **One width rule** (`GraphFlowStyle`, `system_graph/data/graph_flow_style.gd`,
  pure):
  - Inside ONE resource, a wire's width is proportional to what it carries
    (linear; sqrt / log optional). Each width is measured against the biggest
    flow of that resource on screen (`ref`), eased fast up / slowly down.
  - Resources are never compared: each keeps its own scale bar. The scale key
    is the resource kind, or "electricity".
  - `zoom_floor` (Sankey 0.55): a ribbon never shrinks below that share of its
    100 % width. `screen_space` (Bold) ignores the zoom.
  - Presets, two rows: width (Classic = the OLD renderer, untouched, Subtle,
    Sankey = default, Bold) and looks (Neon, Aurora, Ink, Ember). Anything
    changed on top reads as "Custom" (`to_sparse` keeps only the changes).
  - The look keys (`GraphFlowStyle.look`, ranges in `LOOK_RANGES`, clamped by
    `resolve`): glow + glow width, hot core + core width, dark rim, swell (a
    passing streak widens the ribbon), taper (ends narrow), saturation,
    brightness, colour mode (`COLOURS`: resource toward the end / resource /
    heat by flow / aurora shimmer / one accent + `accent`), idle opacity, and
    the pattern's spacing (`period`) and length (`duty`, `pattern_ex`). An old
    `gradient: false` save reads as colour "kind". The Flows lens has its own:
    layer gap, node width, return reach and opacity, label size.
  - Animation speed encodes the MAGNITUDE (log, capped at `MAX_ANIM_PX_S`
    140 px/s). The sim speed only decides whether anything moves. At ≥ 300×
    the pattern turns into long soft streaks (`blur`).
- **Graph-wide, per-wire override.**
  - The graph's style is saved with the graph as `flow_style` (sparse over its
    preset); new graphs default from ui_prefs.cfg `[graph_flow] style`.
  - Set it from View options ▾ → "Flow: <preset>" radios or "Flow style…"
    (`graph_flow_style_panel.gd`, live): an animated preview (`FlowPreview`,
    four flows drawn by GraphFlowRibbons), the two preset rows, folding
    sections Width / Motion / Light / Colour / Averaging and legend / Flows
    lens; a row changed from the preset turns amber with a revert;
    `pick_preset`, `set_knob`, `preview` for checks.
  - `SystemGraphView.set_flow_style / flow_style / open_flow_style_panel`.
  - Per wire: inspector "Flow width" (`conn.flow_width`: "" graph's /
    "plain" / "x2"). The old `sankey_scale: false` reads as plain
    (`GraphFlowStyle.wire_override`).
- **Ribbons** (`GraphFlowRibbons`): a wire is one triangle array, a glow strip
  under a three-lane body, coloured per vertex. The pattern (streaks / comets /
  beads / pulse) comes from `GraphFlowStyle.pattern` on a continuous seconds
  clock (`_flow_clock`), so it never jumps. No shader, no texture: it lands in
  the canvas's own draw order.
  - Idle wires are one plain polyline.
  - Zoomed far out the pattern becomes a pulse.
  - The canvas pre-pass `_prepare_flow_values` (one estimate per wire per draw,
    cached in `_flow_est_cache`) feeds `_render_connection`'s ribbon branch,
    the trunks (V2 `_draw_trunks_ribbon`: per resource, never W + L/h) and the
    scale legend (`_draw_flow_scale_legend`, top-left).
  - Freeform and the Flows lens only. The map lenses keep their own drawing.
  - The hit test widens to the ribbon (`_ribbon_w_cache`).
  - **Cost** (`tools/bench/flow_style_bench.gd`, 227 wires on the Closed Loop
    Ten world): ~10 ms for the wires and ~24 ms for the whole draw per redraw
    (was 44–54 / 58–70), the lens ~12 ms (was 39). What carries it:
    - flow estimates cached for `EST_TTL_MS` 150 ms on the graph's revisions
      (`invalidate_flow_estimates` from `request_sim_redraw`);
    - AC delivered watts through `GraphAcLoad.delivered_index` /
      `delivered_watts_indexed` (one adjacency, memoised draws; the plain form
      was ~130 µs a wire), exact to the watt (the bench checks parity);
    - wire ends kept across draws on one geometry key
      (`_geometry_cache_key`: view, card positions, revisions, a 1 s bucket);
    - ribbon geometry cached per path (`_ribbon_geo`, `GraphFlowRibbons
      .geometry` / `geo_key`), so an animation frame only recolours; the
      lens caches its paths the same way.
- **The Flows lens** (`GraphSiteLayout.VIEW_FLOWS`, lens chip "Flows",
  `GraphFlowLens` + `LoopSankeyLayout`):
  - The current scope's REAL nodes laid out as a Sankey that can loop. The lens
    never writes x/y.
  - `LoopSankeyLayout` (pure):
    - Tarjan SCCs, with a weighted Eades–Lin–Smyth feedback arc set per loop:
      the LIGHTEST flows that close each cycle become the **returns**.
    - Longest-path layers with dummy nodes; barycenter ordering; slot ordering
      by partner.
    - Returns routed as field lines outside the column, nested by span.
    - Boundary flows enter from above (made / from store) and leave below
      (used / into store), read off each node's imbalance per resource.
    - Finn's Cycling Index per resource (Finn 1976; `cycling_metrics`).
  - The canvas draws it in its own pass (`_draw_flows_lens`, early in `_draw`;
    V2's overlays return early). Input goes through `_handle_flows_input`:
    - wheel / drag: zoom and pan;
    - click a node: select; double-click a group: go inside;
    - hover a ribbon: light its loop;
    - header chips: one resource, or Now / 24 h / 7 days.
  - Relayout at most every 0.9 s, only when topology or a flow moves ~25 %,
    with a cross-fade.
  - Windows come from `FlowHistory` (`core/flow/flow_history.gd`, hourly bins
    per CONNECTION id, held readings integrated exactly). It is recorded by the
    view's `_tick_elements` through `canvas.flow_values_now()`. Session data.
- **Elsewhere:**
  - `scenes/ui/loop_sankey_view.gd` puts the same picture in a window.
  - "Where it goes…" draws Loops by default (`ElementSankey.loop_input`), with
    Columns kept.
  - A/B Compare has "Where it flowed": each version's own engine records a
    FlowHistory (`ExperimentWorld.flow_hist`, `flow_loop_input`).
  - The simkit compact report has a `flows` block: top wires, % cycled per
    resource, loops (`SimkitCompact.flows`, `SimkitYear.conn_tot`).
  - 3D conduits animate on `fx_time_lights` (paused with the sim), and their
    glow and scroll speed follow the graph's flow style
    (`ConduitManager.flow_glow_for` / `flow_measure`: each run against the
    biggest of its kind, amps for power, L/h for a resource). Classic keeps
    the old rule. The 3D ring view's connectors take `_ribbon_width`.
- **Run Sankeys (2026-11-12, second pass):**
  - `EnergyRunSankey` (`core/flow/`, pure) splits a run's energy series
    step by step: sun direct to the loads, into and out of the battery
    (gains read off the recorded charge, so losses are the series' own),
    the charge it started with or kept, what was never used. It feeds a
    one-way loop Sankey; boundary flows under 3 % are left out of the
    picture, but the summary line still lists them.
  - `ChallengeBakeEngine.energy_flows()` covers the run up to its end or
    breakpoint. It rides `run_succeeded` as `energy_flows`, and
    `ChallengeRunner.last_energy_flows()` serves a failed prebake.
  - The challenge result card shows it under "Where the energy went". So
    do the tutorial run cards: the card modal takes an `energy_flows` key
    and sizes the picture to the room above the LIVE bar,
    `HudLayout.timeline_height()`. ⚠ `UiScreenLayout.timeline_stack_height()`
    is a stale constant, and a corner card anchored on it ran under a tall
    timeline.
  - A/B Compare: both versions share one width scale per resource
    (`FlowCompare.shared_refs`). "Show B − A" is one Sankey of the
    difference (`FlowCompare.difference`): keys `more:<kind>` (green) and
    `less:<kind>` (red), each pair on one scale, wires matched by
    (from, to, kind).
  - Simkit runs write `flows.svg` (`LoopSankeySvg.render`, through
    `SimkitCompact.flows_svg`): the year's loop Sankey on the dark theme,
    with a legend and a hover title on each ribbon.
- **Patterns** (timeline 🗓, `TimelineUI.open_patterns`,
  `scenes/ui/patterns_modal.gd`) reads the recorded days (SolarUI's
  EnergyTimeline and the tank ResourceTimelines; it changes nothing).
  Windows: 3 / 7 / 14 days, midnight-aligned. Three views:
  - a carpet plot (battery, solar, load, net power, any store's fill);
  - a phase orbit of battery charge against a store or net power, with its

  - the window's energy budget as a waterfall beside the energy Sankey.
- **Kit charts** (`scenes/ui/kit/`):
  - `CarpetPlot`: a day × hour image built when the data is set (never in

  - `PhaseOrbit`: zooms to the data inside the given bounds, fades older

  - `WaterfallChart`: horizontal rows; start and total bars are neutral,

  - The data side is `PatternData` (pure): `hour_grid`, `orbit_drift` /

  - The Site Report keeps the year hour by hour (`hourly_pv_kw` /

## Flows lens: torus shape, moved nodes, wire styles, cadence (2026-11-14)

Plan: `plans/TOROID_SANKEY_PLAN.md`. The Flows lens (lens chip "Flows") has
two SHAPES, picked by chips in its header and saved with the graph
(`flows_shape`): **Column** (LoopSankeyLayout) and **Torus**
(`ToroidFlowLayout`, `system_graph/data/toroid_flow_layout.gd`, pure).
- **Torus rules (second design, 2026-11-15, after the user's concept
  images: a bold trunk with racetrack loops beside it; a diagram, not a
  strict Sankey).**
  - TRUNK: a node that only touches the axis resource (electricity) stands
    on the central line, layered source to load from the top. What is made
    comes in from the top edge; what is used leaves the bottom as heat
    (`heat: true` ribbons grade to red). The lens draws a yellow-to-red
    arrow behind it (notch on top, head below).
  - LOOPS: every other node sits on a RING on one of two lobes. A ring is a
    rounded rectangle round the lobe centre (`ring_pt(a, ring, frac)`, frac
    0 = top centre, 0.25 = beside the trunk; `nearest_on_ring`). Rings are
    parallel offsets of each other (`_ring_size`), smallest loop innermost.
    Round every ring the flow runs DOWN beside the trunk and UP the far side.
  - A flow from one node to the NEXT one round its ring is a BAND
    (`band: true`): one width for the whole ring (`_ring_band`, 12..38),
    with a chevron. Its amount is on the pill, not in the width.
  - THROUGH-FLOWS: nodes on no loop go on open rings outside the loops:
    the longest chains get a ring each (`_longest_chain`, `CHAIN_OWN_RING`),
    the rest share. An open ring runs from an arm over the top, down the
    trunk's side, to an arm under the bottom; what its nodes take in is its
    `tail` ribbon and what they give off its `arrow` ribbon.
  - Every other flow is a thin LINK (`link: true`, <= 4.5 wide, drawn
    first and dimmed until something is hovered or selected): the work from
    the trunk to a machine, a flow across a lobe, a flow between lobes
    (round an end of the trunk, never through it).
  - Loops are peeled from each strongly connected component
    (`_peel_loops`); loops from one component and the small chains that feed
    them stay on one lobe. A store filling / emptying is `store_flow` on
    the node. Boundary flows of ring nodes are only shown as tails / arrows.
  - Output is LoopSankeyLayout's shape plus `shape: "torus"`, `rings`,
    `guides` ([{path, width}], drawn as faint tracks), `axis`, node `shape`
    card | disc.
- **Sides.** The layout fills the left lobe first; the lens passes
  `opts.mirror` (its `mirror`, default TRUE at the user's request, saved as
  `flows_mirror`), which swaps the lobes, so the first loops sit RIGHT of the
  trunk. The header's "Swap sides" chip toggles it (and drops torus pins).
- No layout is applied while a node is being dragged (`lens.dragging`).
- **Moved nodes.** Drag a node in either shape; `LoopSankeyLayout.apply_pins`
  moves each ribbon point by a blend of its two ends' moves. Pins are the
  lens's (`pins_by_shape`, saved as `flows_pins`), never the model's x / y.
  Right-click a moved node or the "Reset positions" chip puts it back.
- **Wire styles.** The toolbar's Wire style reaches the column
  (`opts.wire`: bezier / orthogonal / metro; `wire_path`, `round_poly`).
  Bezier is ONE monotone curve through a ribbon's waypoints (it was one
  S-curve per layer, which is what made long ribbons wavy). Torus ribbons
  are field lines and ignore it.
- **Cadence.** `_flows_input` is cached `FLOWS_INPUT_MS` 700 (it ran on
  every draw); the lens lays out at most every `TOPO_MIN_S` 4 s when WHAT
  flows changes and `VALUE_MIN_S` 8 s when only amounts change, with no
  cross-fade for the latter; numbers follow between layouts
  (`_refresh_values`); a player's choice lays out at once (`force_next`).
  Measured on Closed Loop Ten at 60x: 6 layouts in 12 s before, 3 after;
  frame median in the lens 49 → 31 ms.
- **Nodes.** `input.visuals` {id: {kind store | battery, level, color}}:
  stores draw as vessels with their level, batteries in cells, machines
  glow while working.
- Gates: `system_graph/toroid_flow_layout_selftest.gd` (59) and
  `tools\harness.ps1 -World w6af22bac295d -RunScript res://tools/checks/flow_torus_check.gd -Label flow_torus -Timeout 900`
  (36, real clicks and drags; shot 10 is a synthetic closed site).
- The window Sankeys (`LoopSankeyView`: Where it goes…, run cards, Compare)
  carry their own Column / Torus chips in the top right corner.
- On the torus a dragged lobe node rides its ring (`snap_to_shell`,
  `SHELL_SNAP` 34); pulled further it comes free.
- Tour stop `20h_flow_torus` (mtvernon).
- **Between the lobes.** A flow from one lobe to the other goes round an END
  of the axis (over the top or under the arrow head, each in its own lane),
  never through the beam (selftest). To keep them few, loops cut from one
  component share a lobe and a refinement pass moves a loose node to the
  lobe most of its flow is on (`SIDE_MAX` 0.68 of the nodes a lobe).
  Closed Loop Ten over a week: 19 of 215 ribbons cross.
- **The per-wire ledger (engine).** `ResourceFlowEngine._conn_qty`: every
  LIVE step adds rate x dt per wire, and a batch's FRONTLOADED charge (taken
  from its tank in one step with no rate on the wire) is added whole;
  `take_conn_quantities()` drains it. The view's `_record_flow_history`
  feeds it to `FlowHistory.add_quantities` (spread over the time since the
  last record) and samples only electricity from the canvas. Before this
  the history was a once-a-second SAMPLE of the wires: a frontloaded charge
  was never seen, so a store feeding a batch machine (Pantry to Kitchen)
  read as a dead end and no loop through it could close. Pre-render steps
  are not counted. Simkit's `conn_tot` still misses frontloaded charges.
- On Closed Loop Ten the windows show 0 loops over a day and 1 over a week
  (digester, filter, reclaimed water, HomeBiogas); the Nutrient Store only
  fills in that week, so the food loop stays open there.

## Flows + Process lens improvement pass (2026-11-17)

- **Reading order (tiers).** `LoopSankeyLayout` nodes take `tier` (0
  sources, 1 converters, 2 stores; the canvas's `_flows_tier`: panels,
  arrays, wind / hydro turbines 0, controllers 1, batteries 2). A node sits
  under every lower-tier node it is wired to. A flow from a higher tier into
  a lower one one layer up is `KIND_UP` (battery top → inverter bottom, a
  short rising ribbon); further apart it is a return. Before, a discharging
  battery had no forward input and climbed to the panels' row.
- **One flow per DC pair.** `_flows_input_build` merges the second wire
  between the same two things (the − of a + / − pair) into the first edge's
  `conn_ids`. Every DC value used to be doubled.
- **Boundary flows say where they come from**: "sunlight" (with `sun`,
  drawn as a broad beam with a sun and moving streaks, `_draw_sun_bands`),
  "wind", "falling water", "losses" / "from other sources" at a controller.
  A store's own stock in / out has `hide` (counts in the metrics, takes no
  slot, draws nothing); its card says charging / giving instead.
- **Cards**: per-node `w` / `h`; input `info` {id: {value, media}}. An
  array (`compound_kind` array / pv_design) is a card sized to show every
  panel (`_flows_array_size`, `draw_array_cells` in its body); one panel is a
  drawn module (media "panel"); a node with a model gets the Process lens's
  picture (`_flows_icon_of`, the process lens's view per node, else side),
  else a pictogram. The value line: a controller with AC wired says
  "AC out X" (its DC side is the battery's to show), a battery "charging" /
  "giving", a generator "making", a load "using".
- **Freeform controller card**: ctx `ac_out_w` (`controller_ac_out_w`,
  -1 = no AC wire) makes the hero the AC output, chip INVERTER, sub "AC out ·
  solar in X", bar against `overload_watts`.
- **Multi-select in the lens**: Shift / Ctrl-click toggles, Shift / Ctrl-drag
  on the background is a selection box, dragging a selected node carries the
  others (`GraphFlowLens.set_pins`), a "Group N" chip in the header (and
  Ctrl+G) emits `group_selection_requested` → the view's
  `_on_group_selected_pressed`.
- **Estimator fixes** (freeform wires too): a battery ↔ controller wire's
  direction now accounts for which end the battery is on (Mount Vernon's
  battery is the source end, so charge and discharge were swapped); a hydro
  turbine's + / − leads carry its `live_power_w` (checked before the AC-load
  and AC-shed rules, which took a processor ↔ controller wire for an AC
  load); the published `battery_w` uses load 0 while the AC is shed.
- **Process lens top to bottom**: `MimicGraphSource.build(..., {"flow":
  "down"})` lays the picture out the "right" way with each thing's size
  swapped, then turns positions and line corners over the diagonal
  (`_tp`): lines leave a bottom and arrive at a top, returns run down the
  right side, things keep their shapes. Palette picker "Flow: left to right /
  top to bottom" (`set_flow_dir`, saved inside `icons_data` as `flow`);
  moved things are kept per direction (`_pin_scope`, "<scope>|down").
- Gates: `loop_sankey_layout_selftest` (41), `mimic_selftest` (128),
  `graph_card_specs_selftest` (47) and
  `tools\harness.ps1 -World mtvernon -RunScript res://tools/checks/flows_lens_tiers_check.gd -Label flows_tiers -Timeout 900`
  (33, at noon / 18:00 / 23:00: rows, no doubled pairs, sunlight bands,
  AC out, the battery agreeing with SolarUI, REAL Shift-clicks + the Group
  chip, the Process lens turned top to bottom).

## Circle packing: nested things as zoomable circles (2026-11-12)

Anything nested on the site as circles inside circles you can fly through
(the user's reference: zoomable circle packing, in the dark theme).
- **`CirclePack`** (`core/viz/circle_pack.gd`, pure, 64-bit floats): a tree
  {id, name, value | children, color, unit, detail, data} → laid nodes
  {x, y, r, depth, parent, kids, …} in a frame with the root at (0, 0),
  radius `RADIUS` 1000. Siblings by the front-chain algorithm (Wang et al.
  2006), enclosed by Welzl's circle, both ported from d3-hierarchy v3
  (deterministic LCG shuffle); two passes like d3.pack so the padding is in
  final units; children sorted largest first. A leaf's AREA is its value.
  Leaves of 0 and emptied groups are dropped (`hidden`). Colours: a node's
  own, else its parent's; the root's children take `PALETTE` in order (the
  dataviz reference's eight dark-surface hues, validated on #0f1628:
  adjacent CVD ΔE ≥ 8.4, contrast ≥ 3:1). Circles of any two hues can touch,
  so every group circle carries its name too.
- **`CirclePackView`** (`scenes/ui/kit/circle_pack_view.gd`): click a
  group → a van Wijk & Nuij smooth zoom (d3.interpolateZoom's path) into it;
  click a leaf → selected; double-click → `activated`; right-click /
  Backspace → up; Home → whole; wheel zooms about the pointer; drag pans
  (the focus then follows the view). `set_tree` with the same root id
  GLIDES the circles to new values (live refresh); a new root grows in ring
  by ring. Drawing: groups a tinted disc + an anti-aliased rim, leaves a
  solid disc + a sheen; names on dark pills at a group's top, in the middle
  of a leaf (text colours, never the series colour), largest first, never
  overlapping. ⚠ Discs come from ONE mipmapped 512 px texture
  (`TEXTURE_FILTER_LINEAR_WITH_MIPMAPS` on the view) drawn at any size:
  GraphFastDraw's per-size discs built a new texture every frame of a zoom
  (one draw was 6 ms for 165 circles; now 1.5). Past 512 px a disc is a
  polygon. Off-screen and sub-pixel circles skip their subtree. PerfSpan
  `pack_draw`.
- **`CirclePackWindow`** (`scenes/ui/circle_pack_window.gd`, a ModalFrame,
  one instance under the root: `open_for(tree, spec)`, `current()`): source
  tabs, "Size by", breadcrumb, Home / Up, a side panel (name, value, share
  of the level above and of the whole, its actions, what is inside: rows
  that fly there). spec `sources: [{id, label, build(size_by) -> tree,
  sizes, size, actions(node) -> [[label, Callable]], live_s}]`. Harness:
  `view()`, `set_source`, `set_size_by`, `source_id`.
- **`CirclePackSources`** (`core/viz/circle_pack_sources.gd`): `graph`
  (groups, camps, vehicles; an array's panels in their strings; one each /
  rated power / shipping mass; leaves in their system's channel colour),
  `composition(kind, kg)` (components, each split into elements; water
  stays water), `stores` (by system → store → components),
  `built(records, by structure | material)` (BuiltStock; structures by their
  design's own name, numbered when repeated), `parts(rec)` (materials →
  the designer's parts, from `BuiltStock.parts_of_record`, which shares
  `_part_source` with `of_record`, so parts and material totals agree).
- **Where it opens:** graph View options ▾ → "Nesting as circles…"
  (`SystemGraphView.open_circle_pack(source, focus_id)`: Systems, What the
  stores hold, What it is built from; actions Show on the graph / Look at
  it in 3D / Its parts); a group's inspector "See inside as circles"
  (opens on that group); a store's "See its make-up as circles"
  (`open_composition_pack`); the dashboard's WATER & NUTRIENTS "What it is
  made of…"; the prop editor's "What it is made of…" (`open_parts_pack`).
- Gates: `core/viz/circle_pack_selftest.gd` (26: inside parents, padding,
  area ∝ value, enclose by hand, 3 equal circles exact, determinism, drops,
  2,500 nodes in ~150 ms, composition sums, graph nesting + strings, parts
  = built stock); `tools\harness.ps1 -World w6af22bac295d -RunScript
  res://tools/checks/circle_pack_check.gd -Label circle_pack -Timeout 900`
  (23, real clicks: fly in, hover, right-click out, tabs, Its parts, the
  inspector button; draw cost); tour stop `20g_circle_pack`.

## Graph view at speed (perf pass, 2026-10-27)

"The graph view moves very slowly at high speeds." Measured with
`graph_view_bench` on Mount Vernon (graph open, freeform). The median frame
was vsync-bound up to 1440× but ~7 % of frames ran 37–48 ms at every speed,
and at 7200× the median was 27.6 ms with the graph's sections summing to
32 ms. After the pass: 7200× median 16.7 ms, sections ~9.5 ms. Frames over
budget are mostly frames a few ms past 16.7 ms that wait a whole vsync, so
the fix was taking steady cost out. In order of size:
- **PV string walk.** `PvElectrical._pv_sources_reachable` rescanned every
  wire for every node it visited. It now builds `pv_adjacency(conns)` once
  per walk. On top of that:
  - `_collect_root_array_aggregate` is cached on (struct_rev, user_rev, wire
    count, sandbox); callers get a copy. It was 5.5 ms, computed twice in
    the 1 Hz flush and on every SolarUI sync.
  - The DC throttle's live circuit Voc reuses each controller's strings
    (`_circuit_strings`, cached with `_dc_topo_key`). It was a full flat
    walk per controller at 10 Hz.
  - Net: SolarUI sync 10.8 → 1.3 ms, telemetry 9.7 → 0.75 ms, throttle
    pass 4.9 → 0.3 ms.
- **Redraw cadence.**
  - Sim telemetry no longer `queue_redraw()`s every frame the clock runs. It
    calls `canvas.request_sim_redraw()`, drawn by the canvas tick at most
    every `SIM_REDRAW_INTERVAL` (0.1 s).
  - ⚠ The high-speed LOD could never engage: `_high_speed_lod` compared the
    flow multiple, which is clamped to 80, with `HIGH_SPEED_FLOW_MULT` 300.
    It now compares the real speed (sim_time_scale / REALTIME_SCALE_REF),
    and `REDRAW_INTERVAL_HIGH_SPEED` is 0.1 s.
- **Closure metrics.** `compute_closure_metrics` is memoised for
  `CLOSURE_MEMO_MS` (200 ms) at the same thousandth of a sim-hour. A
  challenge bake stepping minutes inside one frame still recomputes per
  step. The dashboard (5 Hz), the closure refresh and the timeline used to
  compute it separately, ~3 ms each.
- **High scores.** `HighScoreStore.load_scores` keeps parsed files in
  memory while the file's modified time is unchanged. The dashboard read
  and parsed the score file five times a second.
- **Dashboard projection.** The 24 h / 7 d projection evaluates SolarUI's
  solar once per WHOLE sim hour and interpolates (`_solar_hours`, dropped on
  a graph or array change or every 60 s). It used to make 192 fresh
  evaluations (~13 ms) every 0.25 sim-h, which is eight times a second at
  7200×.
- **Array card picture.** `draw_array_cells` draws straight off the
  snapshot: no per-cell dicts, `frac_by_idx` once per draw, outlines
  batched per string through `draw_multiline`. That took it 0.95 → 0.52 ms
  for 60 cells and dropped draw calls from 1115 to about 1000.
- **New spans.** `gv_process` (the view's whole frame), `gv_flush_tel` /
  `_solar` / `_inv`, and `gv_dash_power` / `closure` / `tick` / `slow` /
  `proj`. `canvas.draw_profile_on` times each card by type.
- **What remains** in slow frames is mostly outside graph code: the stream
  network's `water_*` (it runs while the graph hides the world), SolarUI at
  7200×, and engine time.

## Frame spikes: one heavy job a frame (perf pass, 2026-11-17)

Walton, first person, graph closed, ran ~19 ms frames with 25–140 ms spikes
several times a second. Measured with `tools/bench/frame_spike_bench.gd`
(`SPIKE_SPEEDS=1,60`; per frame its length, every F3 section and the frame's
PHASES; `SPIKE_PACER=0` turns the pacer off).
- **Frame phases** (`tools/bench/frame_phase_probe.gd`, two nodes at
  `process_priority` ±100000 plus `RenderingServer.frame_pre_draw` /
  `frame_post_draw`): `scripts` (every `_process`), `after_scripts` (the
  deferred-call flush, the delete queue, SceneTree timers, tweens),
  `render_main`, `physics`, `between`. ⚠ **A Control's `_draw()` runs in
  `after_scripts`**: `queue_redraw()` is a deferred call, so a slow `_draw`
  shows up in no `_process` section. `tools/bench/deferred_bisect_bench.gd`
  switches Main's children off one at a time (`BISECT_IN=UILayer` for
  UILayer's) and finds the node behind that window.
- **`FramePacer`** (`core/perf/frame_pacer.gd`, static, autoload-free):
  `claim(job, waited)`. At most one heavy periodic job runs a frame; a job
  that finds the frame taken waits for the next and asks again, and after
  `MAX_WAIT_FRAMES` (6) runs anyway. Only WHEN a job runs moves, never what it
  computes. Jobs on it:
  - the ambient tick's two halves (`SystemGraphView._tick_resource_flow_ambient`):
    the people tick runs on the frame the flow step falls due, and the flow
    step on a later frame (`_flow_step_due`, `_ambient_flow_step`). The flow
    engine counts the held frame's time (`ResourceFlowEngine.accumulate`), so
    the step still covers the clock up to when it runs;
  - the SCADA hub's 1 Hz tag gather, the element ledger, the timeline's needs
    strip;
  - the water network's hydraulics poll, now three phases a frame apart
    (`_step_hydraulics_poll`): erosion, then the rain history and basins,
    then the flow comparison, in the old order.
- **The timeline track.** It redraws at least every `TRACK_IDLE_REDRAW_MS`
  (500 ms), and its `_draw` had two slow parts:
  - The four weather lanes each read ~1,000 weather samples (~100 ms a lane),
    all together on their 10 s TTL: a ~480 ms frame. Weather bins are now
    made a slice at a time in `_process` (`_lane_bins_sliced`,
    `_run_lane_jobs`, `LANE_JOB_BUDGET_US` 3 ms). The lane draws its last bins
    until the new ones are done, and nothing on the very first draw. Bins on
    the anchored grid do not depend on each other, so the numbers are the
    same. Checks that read `_waveform_cache` wait on `lane_jobs_pending()`.
  - `_draw_set_spans` looped over every venue set in the window. Walton's
    saved window was 337,221 hours (~38 years): 42,156 sets, 113 ms to build
    and 28 ms to skip on every redraw. Past a day a pixel nothing there can
    draw, so it returns.
- **`SpaceRegistry.area_point_memo`**: an area target's interior point is a
  pure function of its outline (the concave fallback grid-samples 625
  points). The population tick resolved all 82 of Walton's areas every tick
  (~9 ms); memoized on the outline's hash, checked by value.
- **Water at load.** Every Walton load carved the stream channels twice. Other
  tile layers composing at load asked the network to rebuild before this
  load's OSM water had answered, so it resolved 0 features, wiped the 425
  cached channel tiles, and the next carve cut them all again. Each pass sent
  425 tiles through the height field at ~15 ms each. The loader now reports
  `osm_water_pending()` (`_osm_water_settled`, set when the OSM fetch answers,
  fails or the load ends), and `WaterNetwork._start_rebuild` holds the carve
  until then.
- **Erosion** walks only the stations that can erode (carved, open, ≥ 2 cm of
  water; `_erosion_candidates`, cached per flow-states array, which is always
  replaced and never edited), in the same order.
  - Second pass, same day: `_erosion_rates` keeps each stream's stations over
    the critical shear, with their rate, erosion bin and spacing, until the
    flow states, the carve's facts or the section change. Only re-meshed
    streams rebuild theirs, and the rebuild has `bed_shear_pa` /
    `erosion_rate_mps` written out. On Walton's 19,879 stations (old → new):

    | | dry day | 100 mm/h |
    |---|---|---|
    | a poll | 6.2 → 0.12 ms | 13.5 → 1.1 ms |
    | a poll after its stream re-meshed | 6.2 → 2.6 ms | 13.5 → 6.9 ms |

    `tools/diag/erosion_parity.gd` keeps the old loop and compares
    (bit-identical). ⚠ A change to the shear or rate formulas must be made in
    `StreamHydraulics` AND in `_erosion_rates`.
- **Result** (Walton, same session, before → after; flow_step_bench state
  hash unchanged on both worlds, `873bbca3849e25ca` / `c196d8df62f4dee6`):

  | | 1x | 60x |
  |---|---|---|
  | p90 | 46.9 → 25.0 ms | 39.1 → 27.5 ms |
  | p99 | 80.6 → 32.5 ms | 65.2 → 46.1 ms |
  | worst | 146.7 → 43.5 ms | 139.2 → 61.3 ms |
  | frames over 33 / 50 ms in 20 s | 195 / 46 → 8 / 0 | 135 / 50 → 35 / 4 |

  The median stays ~19 ms. flow_step_bench's own 60x median frame on Walton
  went 42.7 → 20.2 ms. Its "full specs digest" is NOT a pin: it holds live
  display stamps (panel output, battery SOC, `dc_*_w`) and differs between
  two runs of the same code; the state hash is the pin.
- **The basin phase** (second pass, same day) was ~25 ms once a sim-minute
  at speed, now ~7 ms, with results the same bit for bit:
  - `_refresh_basin_series` has `_q_at` and `step_volume` written out, with
    the per-basin constants worked out once (`_inflow_plan`) and the stage
    row found by halving: 17.5 → 4.9 ms on Walton's 8 basins.
  - The rain history is sampled by `rain_mmh_series` (lookups made once, the
    date once a day) and summed by `StreamRunoff.history_prefix_values`.
  - `WeatherService` reads the computer's date and hour at most every 200 ms
    (`_read_system_date`; sample() asked the OS up to five times a call).
  - Together the rain history went 4.4 → 1.7 ms.
  - Gate: `tools/diag/basin_series_parity.gd` keeps the plain loops and
    compares.
  - Walton frame-spike A/B:

    | | before | after |
    |---|---|---|
    | 60x p99 / max | 42.4 / 56.2 ms | 34.4 / 51.7 ms |
    | 60x frames over 33 ms | 36 | 13 |
    | 1x max | 51.0 ms | 37.8 ms |
    | 1x frames over 33 ms | 15 | 6 |

    The water poll's worst frame went 26.6 → 10.1 ms (now erosion). Both
    state hashes are unchanged.
- **The flow step** (fourth pass): 13.8 → 10.4 ms on Walton (378 items, 233
  tanks, 288 wires; `tools/diag/flow_step_profile.gd`). State hashes
  unchanged. The changes:
  - The culvert pass asked `ConduitKinds.uses_culvert_kit` for every wire,
    and that deep-copies the type's whole metadata (`type_meta`). It is now
    asked once per type per step: 1.27 → 0.24 ms.
  - `_tank_specs_view` reads a tank's specs in place when
    `_migrate_resource_specs_if_needed` would only fill its two false
    defaults. The timeline check (1.86 → 0.8 ms) and the tank loop use it.
    The deficit and make-up paths, which write, get `_tank_specs_copy`.
  - `_apply_tank_sample` collects the keys it writes and copies the specs
    only when a value moved. The tank loop went 3.7 → 2.6 ms.
  - Not changed: the habitats (~1.6 ms). Their working copy is most of it,
    but with ideal supply on (the author's prefs) their import rates move
    every step, so nearly every habitat writes and copies anyway. A
    read-in-place path saved 0.1 ms and was dropped.
  - Also not changed: Walton's one terraced field costs 0.8 ms a step.
  - Sixth pass (2026-11-18), 10.62 → 9.47 ms (state hashes unchanged):
    `_ensure_timelines_at` returns at once while struct_rev, user_rev,
    the item array and the timeline count are as last time (0.79 → 0.02
    ms); `_apply_tank_sample` reads into locals and builds its patch only
    when a value moved, in the old key order (tanks 2.62 → 2.26 ms); a
    terraced field's paddy losses are memoised per (crop, flooded,
    growing) within a step and its stores are read in place (0.76 → 0.64
    ms; `tools/diag/terrace_step_profile.gd` times its parts).
  - **Full tank histories.** Once a tank's `ResourceTimeline` held
    `MAX_SAMPLES` (14 sim-days, ~14 real minutes at 1440x), every step
    copied its three arrays to drop the oldest sample: 16.5 µs a step
    against 2.7 µs, ~3 ms of every flow step on Walton's 233 tanks. Now the
    trim moves `_head` (storage index of the first kept sample) and the
    dead samples are cut off every `COMPACT_AT` (2048) steps: 2.6 µs, full
    or not. Logical sample i is storage `_head + i`; anything new that
    indexes `_level` / `_inflow` / `_outflow` must add `_head` (appends at
    the end and the last element need not). Gate:
    `core/resource_timeline_selftest.gd`; a deliberately broken index
    fails it at op 282.
- **The two once-a-second jobs** (fifth pass, same day), with results the
  same tag for tag and row for row (`tools/diag/scada_ledger_parity.gd`,
  `tools/diag/kind_factor_parity.gd`; profiler
  `tools/diag/scada_elements_profile.gd`):
  - **Element ledger 9.9 → 6.0 ms.** Its stock pass asked the composition
    catalog ~15 times per tank, and each `canonical()` goes through
    ResourceKinds. `CompositionCatalog.kind_factors(kind)` keeps each kind's
    constants (material, known, kg per unit, element profile, lhv +
    sensible, water share, food MJ, clean water), cleared when
    `ResourceKinds.kinds_rev` moves (bumped wherever the user kinds
    change). `embodied` / `embodied_kg` multiply the same numbers in the
    same order.
  - `ResourceKinds.display_name / default_unit / wire_color /
    flow_ref_rate` read the kind's own entry (`_meta_ref`) instead of
    `kind_meta`, which deep-copies it on every call.
  - **SCADA refresh 7.3 → 5.3 ms** (graph tags 7.7 → 4.2, the book 2.3 →
    0.8): see `ScadaTags` in the SCADA section.
  - Walton, before → after:

    | | 60x | 1x |
    |---|---|---|
    | `gv_elements` worst | 10.3 → 7.3 ms | 10.8 → 7.0 ms |
    | `scada_hub` worst in a slow frame | 11.3 → 6.8 ms | 12.4 → none |
    | frames over 33 ms | 9 → 6 | 4 → 8 (other jobs; noise) |
    | worst frame | 44.0 → 38.2 ms | 42.2 → 44.7 ms |

    Neither job is in a 1x slow frame any more. Both state hashes are
    unchanged.
- **The timeline's lanes** (sixth pass, same day; pixel-identical,
  `tools/diag/timeline_lane_parity.gd`). The track redraws every 500 ms and
  on each half-pixel playhead move. Each redraw rebuilt every lane's
  triangle strips, value range and (imperial units) unit-mapped weather
  bins from bins that had not changed: ~6.4 ms a redraw on Walton's 8
  lanes × 503 bins. Now:
  - `TimelineWaveformDraw.draw_bins_cached` keeps a lane's draw operations
    (`bins_ops` → `replay`).
  - `_bins_range` keeps its value range.
  - The weather lane keeps its mapped bins.

  Each is held per track id in `_lane_draw` and keyed on the bins DICT
  itself (`is_same`) plus every other input. ⚠ So a bins dict must never
  change once a producer hands it over; every producer builds a fresh one
  through TimelineBinning.

  Walton, before → after: one track redraw 6.4 → 1.4 ms
  (`timeline_lane_profile.gd`), and the frame spike bench:

  | | 60x | 1x |
  |---|---|---|
  | worst frame | 42.6 → 34.7 ms | 42.0 → 34.5 ms |
  | frames over 25 ms | 56 → 37 | 51 → 30 |
  | frames over 33 ms | 6 → 3 | 5 → 5 |
  | `tl_draw` worst in a slow frame | 8.4 → 3.4 ms | 8.3 → 5.0 ms |

  What is left of a redraw is ~0.15 ms per weather lane, ~0.04 ms per power
  lane and 0.35 ms for the clips lane.
- Spans added: `npc_svc` / `_pos` / `_spots` / `_comfort` / `_nav`,
  `npc_walk`, `npc_full_tick` / `_post`, `tl_draw` / `_lanes` / `_mc` /
  `_clips` / `tl_draw_wave_<source>_<channel>`, `tl_clip_*`.
  `PerfMonitor.last_frame_ms` is the delta that goes with `last_frame`.
- **The nav re-bake spike** (2026-11-18). Placing a prop, repainting a camp
  or tagging a space restarts the people's nav grid reusing its ground
  (`NpcNavGrid.begin_bake_reusing`), and that copied every column's height
  and slope in a GDScript loop, and `begin_bake` filled the upper layers a
  byte at a time: 76 ms of `npc_svc_nav` in one frame on Walton's
  800 x 800 x 3 grid, now 10–11 ms (whole frame ~93 → 22–29 ms). The arrays
  are copied natively, and steepness is re-marked only on the columns
  `_write_slope` recorded within `STEEP_NEAR_DEG` of the limit
  (`_steep_near`), tested on the stored value as before. Gate:
  `tools/diag/nav_reuse_parity.gd` (offline, frozen copy of the old loops,
  byte for byte); in the world `tools/diag/nav_reuse_spike_probe.gd`.
- **Ground-height queries cost half** (2026-11-18): every one goes through
  `TerrainBuilder.sample_footing_height` → `sample_bilinear`, which built a
  4-element Array per call for its NaN fallback and sampled the coarse grid
  even deep inside the detail patch where only the detail height is
  returned. Now no Array (same first finite corner, same order) and each
  grid is sampled only where its height is returned: 3.22 → 1.62 µs a query,
  bit-identical on 240,000 queries incl. NaN corners and the crossfade band
  (`tools/diag/footing_sampler_parity.gd`). Walton's full nav bake (~600k
  queries, time-budgeted per frame) is ready 13 s sooner (76.8 → 63.5 s).
- **Still open:**
  - A terrain tile rebuild is ~15 ms on its own (the first build samples the
    base ground 67² times), more than the 6 ms budget. Each of those samples
    halved on 2026-11-18 (below), so roughly 9 ms now; not re-measured.
  - The load carve that recuts all 425 Walton tiles (~10 s on a worker) in
    the harness: the sandbox always starts from the player's real channel
    cache, saved 2026-10-31 by older code that computed other beds. The real
    game re-carves once after such a change and saves a fresh cache.
    (Separately, erosion made unrelated rebuilds re-carve in a loop: fixed,
    see "Erosion never makes an unrelated rebuild re-carve".)
  - The flow step (~8 ms) is most of Walton's remaining frames over 33 ms.

## One site, many power systems (system_graph/data/graph_systems.gd, 2026-11-04)

Plan: `plans/GRAPH_SYSTEMS_UX_PLAN.md` (Phase 0 landed; Phases 1–6 are the
navigation / seamless-zoom / festival-board / 3D-link / perf work).

**Power islands.** A living vehicle's node (`specs.vehicle_prop_id`) and a
festival camp's compound (`specs.camp_lot_id`) are power ISLANDS: their
contents are that system's, never the site's. `GraphSystems`:
- `is_power_island(item)`;
- `island_scopes(model)`: every scope inside an island, nested groups
  included, mapped to the island id; memoised on struct_rev + user_rev;
- `island_of(model, item)`;
- `walk_site_power(model)`;
- `list(model)`.

⚠ **Every site-energy aggregate walks `GraphSystems.walk_site_power`, never
`GraphNesting.walk_items(model, "root")`.** The plain walk descends into
vehicles (their compound has no `compound_kind`), and that leaked:
- vehicle panels into SolarUI's peak, which also turned SolarUI on for a site
  with no PV;
- vehicle batteries into the site bank, so the site SOC jumped on every vehicle
  add or rebuild;
- the site SOC written over every vehicle battery at 10 Hz;
- vehicle MPPTs as site controllers (`INVERTER_MAX_SOLAR_KW`, DC throttle
  entries);
- a destroyed vehicle controller shedding the site's AC.

The flow engine still walks INTO islands (tanks, habitats), so never make them
opaque in `GraphNesting`.

Other rules:
- `GraphAcLoad` seeds reach from non-island controllers only, and its loss pass
  skips wires inside an island.
- A destroyed controller inside a vehicle drops that vehicle's scope AC only
  (`_tick_vehicle_power`).
- Removing a camp or vehicle clears its own scope AC, never all of them.
- Camps and vehicles take their sun from `SolarUI.evaluate_yield_per_kwp_at`
  (the sky on 1 kWp: no site shade, caps or clamp). The site's delivered output
  over `PEAK` carried the player's clipping into every camp and was 0 on a site
  with no PV.
- Battery cards and wires inside an island read that island's own flow:
  `live_power_hint.islands`, through `graph_canvas.hint_battery_w`.
- A sim render steps and snapshots vehicle power with camp power.
- Dashboard stores and the ClosureMetrics battery fallback count the site's own
  system; the stores card says camps and vehicles keep their own.

**Placement and scope:**
- Camp compounds, their habitats, festival depots and festival-mode fallback
  habitats carry TOP-LEVEL `site_x_m` / `site_z_m`, which is what
  `GraphSiteLayout.has_site_coords` reads. The specs copy alone gave a camp no
  pin and no Locate / Watch, and then an invented spot from the Site Plan
  auto-seed. The camp sync rewrites a stale top-level value.
- New camp and vehicle cards go to `_free_system_card_pos(site)`: the site
  position × 4 px/m below the player's system, then the nearest free cell on a
  spiral.
- `_unstack_system_cards` (run by the camp sync) moves only a system card that
  overlaps another one.
- After every structural change the breadcrumb trail is checked at the end of
  the frame (`_queue_scope_validation`). A gone vehicle or camp scope follows
  its owner by identity (`_scope_owner_keys`); anything else falls back to the
  deepest scope still standing.
- PVLab arrays are never seeded inside an island scope.

Gates: `system_graph/graph_systems_selftest.gd` (offline, 22 checks) and
`tools\harness.ps1 -World walton -RunScript res://tools/checks/graph_systems_check.gd -Label graph_systems -Timeout 900`.
The Walton check covers:
- the site's peak, capacity, stored kWh and clamp unchanged by a placed tool
  bus;
- the vehicle card reading its own SOC;
- 40 camps with top-level coords and no overlapping system cards;
- a rebuilt vehicle keeping the player inside it, and a deleted one returning
  them to root.

**Finding your way (Phase 1, 2026-11-04):**
- **Systems outliner.** `GraphSystemsOutliner` (`system_graph/graph_systems_outliner.gd`)
  sits at the top of the left sidebar. It holds a tree:
  - Site ▸ Camps / Vehicles / Groups & structures / Nodes;
  - inside each compound, what is in it;
  - on each system row, a status (`GraphSystems.status`: ok / warn / crit /
    idle, from the stamped `camp_*` keys or `vehicle_power_states`).

  Filter chips: All · Attention · Camps · Vehicles. The search matches every
  word against name, type and the system the node is in, and lists results
  flat. Click = `focus_graph_item(id)`, which flies there and enters the
  scopes on the way; double-click = open it; Enter in the search = the first
  result; Down = into the tree. The tree is rebuilt only on struct_rev /
  user_rev / filter changes; the status column refreshes at 2 Hz.
  ⚠ A click on a row's fold arrow only expands it: harness clicks go on the
  row's text.
- **Keys** (graph open, not typing):
  - Ctrl+F = search (opens the left sidebar);
  - F = frame the selection, A = frame the scope (freeform;
    `fit_items_to_view`);
  - Home = the site;
  - Alt+Left / Esc = up one level.

  The Hints & shortcuts panel lists them all.
- **Breadcrumb.** Crumbs show the compound's own name with ⛺ / 🚐. A ▾ after
  a crumb lists its siblings of the same kind (`_breadcrumb_siblings`) and
  jumps camp to camp.
- **`_set_scope_trail(trail, focus_id)`** is THE way to move more than one
  level: breadcrumb jumps, sibling jumps, the outliner and search all go
  through it. It remembers the camera of the scope being left, fades, selects
  `focus_id`, and lands on the remembered camera framed on it, else frames
  it.
- **Per-scope camera.** The canvas keeps `_scope_cam["<lens>|<scope>"]`,
  captured on enter (`begin_enter_transition`) and on every trail move. A pop
  or jump up returns there, re-centred on the compound left if it would be
  off screen. Only parents are restored on a pop: a child's camera at the
  moment it is left is at the pop threshold.
- **Pop-out resists.** Content must be under `ZOOM_POP_COVER` 0.3 of the view
  (was 0.42) AND the wheel must push out `POP_PUSH_NOTCHES` 3 more times,
  each within 0.8 s. The hint "Keep scrolling out to leave <name> ●○○" shows
  above the bottom portal pills. At the zoom floor the wheel still pushes.
  Measured on a Walton camp: 11 notches to reach the floor, then 3.
- Gate: `tools\harness.ps1 -World walton -RunScript res://tools/checks/graph_navigation_check.gd -Label graph_nav -Timeout 900`
  (17 checks, REAL input: Ctrl+F, typing, Enter, F, a row double-click, Esc
  back to the same camera, the sibling menu, Home, Alt+Left, the wheel
  resistance); the selftest is now 28 checks (status rules).

**Festival to wire on one wheel (Phase 2, 2026-11-04):**
- **Tiles.** A camp or vehicle card narrower than `TILE_MAX_PX` (96 px) on
  screen is drawn as a festival tile (`graph_canvas_v2._draw_system_tile`):
  - a status ring, one quarter arc each for power, water, food and people
    (`GraphSystems.ring`, read from the stamped `camp_*` keys or the
    vehicle's power state and tank levels; the vehicles' power reaches the
    canvas as `live_power_hint.vehicles`);
  - the tent or truck icon;
  - a name under it.

  A tile grows to at least `TILE_MIN_R` but never past half the distance to
  its nearest neighbour (`_tile_room_for`). Names are placed after every item
  has drawn (`_draw_tile_labels`): the most urgent first, and none that would
  land on another name or tile.
- **Peek.** A group card at least `PEEK_MIN_PX` (340 px) wide (generic groups,
  camps and vehicles; not arrays, banks or banners; at most `PEEK_MAX_ITEMS`
  inside) keeps its header and draws its real interior in the body
  (`_draw_card_peek`): child cards through GraphCard at their true layout,
  with wires from the bottom edge to the top.
  - The mapping is `_view_for_bbox_in_rect(child bbox, card_peek_rect(rect))`.
  - `begin_enter_transition` starts the child canvas from that same rect
    (`draws_peek`), so entering is not a jump. The check measures the same
    pixel before and after.
- **Arrange by site** (Layout ▾, `arrange_systems_by_site`, one undo step):
  - every system card goes where its system stands, with the site's own nodes
    in the middle (`GraphSystems.arrange_by_site`: nearest the centre placed
    first, then pushed out on a spiral);
  - the scale comes from `auto_px_per_m`, so the median nearest neighbour is
    a card apart.
- **Lenses inside a system.**
  - An island's contents with no map place get one round the island
    (`GraphSystems.derived_child_sites`, radius `island_radius_m`), in their
    canvas shape, flagged `site_derived`, and they follow when it moves.
  - They are written as sim writes (`_derive_island_sites`, from the camp
    sync, the vehicle sync and `_apply_scope_to_canvas`).
  - A derived place is never a shade receiver.
  - In Site Plan, every scope change frames the map on where the items stand
    (`frame_site_items`). The freeform fits used to push graph coordinates
    into the map camera.
  - The Globe stays on the site marker, so a camp far from it is outside the
    sphere.
- **Inside cue.** Every lens draws a frame in the system's colour and
  "Inside <name>" low on the canvas (`_draw_inside_cue`).
- Gate: `tools\harness.ps1 -World walton -RunScript res://tools/checks/graph_festival_check.gd -Label graph_festival -Timeout 900`
  (12 checks: arrange with no overlaps and the map's east–west order, every
  camp a tile, the peek, the enter starting on the peek's pixel, a real wheel
  zoom through the peek into the camp, Site Plan inside with every item
  placed and on screen, Esc back out with the camp in view). The selftest is
  now 42 checks.

**What is wrong at my festival (Phase 3, 2026-11-04):**
- **One row per system.** `GraphSystemBoard.row(item, power, ledger, site)` is
  pure. It reads data already stamped or stepped:
  - the camp_* keys;
  - the camp or vehicle CampPowerModel state, which wins over the stamps;
  - CampLedger over the system's own scope.

  It gives battery, solar, load, hours left, people, morale, stores with days
  to empty (wastes: days to full), a level (ok / warn / crit / idle), the
  reasons in words, and an attention score.
  - An OPEN loop alone is not news: a camp living off a week of stored water
    is fine. Only a kind with no store at all warns ("no water here").
  - Water or food under 1 day is critical, under 3 days a warning; a waste
    tank filling up is judged the same way.
  - `SystemGraphView._refresh_system_board` rebuilds every row once a second
    (the closure block, `gv_board` span), the site's own row first. The
    board, the dashboard, the tile overlay, the alerts rail and the outliner's
    status all READ them (`system_board_rows / _row`, `active_system_id`).
  - Cost on Walton's 40 camps: 3.3 ms a second. It was 17 ms until
    `GraphNesting.scope_index` / `walk_in_index` (one pass for every camp's
    ledger; `CampLedger.compute` / `open_kinds` take the items) and the
    `ResourceKinds.normalize_kind` memo (it scanned every kind's alias list
    per call, which every ledger and the flow engine call per port). The camp
    card refresh got the same index.
- **The dashboard follows the active system** (`graph_dashboard_panel`
  tabs):
  - At the site level with camps or vehicles, the tabs are Whole festival
    (the default: decision #3), Your system (the old cards) and Board.
  - Inside a camp or vehicle, the tabs are that system (its battery, solar,
    load, time to empty / full, people, stores with days, what it brings in
    and keeps) and Board.
  - With no islands there are no tabs: the old cards, as before.
- **Festival board** (`GraphFestivalBoard`): filter chips, sortable columns,
  rows with a level stripe and the reasons; a click flies there, a double
  click goes inside (`board_fly_to`). The same widget sits in the Board tab
  and full screen over the canvas (View ▾ → Festival board, ⤢; Esc closes).
- **Colour systems by** (View ▾): battery, water days, morale, power margin.
  - Values come from `GraphSystemBoard.overlay_value`; there are four bins,
    and no data draws grey.
  - Tiles are tinted, big cards outlined, Site Plan gets a disc where each
    system stands.
  - The legend (bottom-left of the canvas) hides a bin on click.
  - The mode is saved in ui_prefs.cfg `[graph_systems] overlay`.
- **Alerts rail** (canvas top-right, `GraphSystemAlerts`, pure latch):
  - a system shows once it has been WORSE than its baseline for 2 s;
  - a level a system already has when first seen is its baseline, except
    critical, which is always news;
  - it leaves after 5 s fine; a dismissed entry returns only if it gets worse;
  - 6 shown, then "+N more on the board".
- ⚠ A button whose press rebuilds the panel it sits in (the legend bins, a
  rail entry's ×) must connect CONNECT_DEFERRED or defer the rebuild: freeing
  the emitter mid-signal is an engine error.
- Gates: `system_graph/graph_system_board_selftest.gd` (offline, 46) and
  `tools\harness.ps1 -World walton -RunScript res://tools/checks/graph_board_check.gd -Label graph_board -Timeout 900`
  (18, real clicks: a fine camp loses its power and reaches the rail, the
  click flies there, the system tab inside it, the Board tab and its filter
  and row, the full-screen board and Esc, battery colours and a legend bin,
  the cost). The Walton world as saved has 24 camps with no power at its
  hour, so those are on the rail from the start.

**Always know what a node is (Phase 4, 2026-11-04):**
- **Twin kind** (`GraphSystems.twin_kind(model, item)`, pure):
  - "3d": a prop, vehicle, scene device or OSM feature (`TWIN_KEYS`);
  - "map": only a place on the map (a `site_derived` place does not count);
  - "owner": no place of its own, but inside a camp or vehicle that has one
    (`owner_with_place`);
  - "none": graph only.

  `_item_world_xz_for_handoff` falls back to the owner, so Locate and Walk
  work for every node inside a camp or vehicle; `locate_item_in_world` now
  uses it too.
- **Twin badges:** every card at least `TWIN_BADGE_MIN_PX` (120 px) wide
  carries a small chip just outside its right edge at the header (the top and
  bottom edges carry the ports and their names; `_draw_twin_badge`,
  freeform): a box
  for 3D, a pin for the map or its owner's place, a struck circle for graph
  only. A click Locates (`twin_badge_pressed`); graph only explains how to
  place it.
- **Hover, both ways:**
  - The canvas emits `item_hovered` (cards, and pins in the lens views). The
    outliner rows do the same through `preview_item_hover`.
  - `_apply_embodiment_highlight` lights the twin while hovered and puts the
    selection's highlight back after. It gained camps: a camp compound lights
    its painted outline through `loader.set_camp_focus`
    (`_embodiment_camp_id`). Vehicles light through their `bound_prop_id`.
    The lens previews share the world, so they draw it.
- **Open in graph enters scopes:** `open_node_in_graph` goes into the
  node's camp or vehicle first (`focus_graph_item`). The camp Tune look (camp
  mode) has "Open its system in the graph" (`open_camp_in_graph(camp id)`:
  a painted camp or a lot's camp).
- **Pins that read** (`_draw_pin_labels`):
  - names at rest, at most `PIN_LABELS_MAX`, by priority: selected / hovered
    / dragged, then systems, then big machines, then the rest;
  - a name is drawn only where it lands on no other name or pin head
    (`pin_labels_drawn` for checks);
  - a system's pin is coloured by its board level (`system_status`, pushed
    with the overlay) and drawn a little larger.
  - Grouping pins per system needed nothing new: a camp's contents live in
    its scope, so at the site level a camp is already one pin.
- **The camp card says what the board says:** the canvas gets each
  system's level and reasons (`system_status`, `system_reasons`) and passes
  them to `GraphCardSpecs` as ctx `sys_level` / `sys_reason`. A camp living
  off its stores reads "Fine: its stores cover it" instead of a warning per
  open loop. Without the ctx (selftests) the old footer stays.
- **Freeform site inset** (`_draw_site_inset`, bottom right of the canvas,
  View ▾ → Site map inset, ui_prefs.cfg `[graph_systems] inset`): every
  system a dot where it stands, coloured by level, the site's own system at
  home in cyan, systems on screen ringed, the one you are inside (or have
  selected) ringed bright. A click flies there (`inset_system_pressed` →
  `board_fly_to`).
- Gate: `tools\harness.ps1 -World walton -RunScript res://tools/checks/graph_twin_check.gd -Label graph_twin -Timeout 900`
  (real input: hover lights and clears the camp outline, badge kinds, a badge
  click looks at the camp and Esc returns to it, Open in graph into a camp's
  scope, the camp's own Open in graph, Site Plan pin names, the inset's dots
  and a click on one, the View toggle). Selftests: graph_systems 47
  (`_test_twin_kind`), graph_card_specs 45.

**One visual language (Phase 5, 2026-11-05):**
- **Colour grammar** (`GraphTheme`): channels say WHAT flows (`CHANNELS`:
  electricity amber, water cyan, food green, fuel and heat orange, people
  violet; `channel_of_kind` through GraphDomainFilter), levels say HOW IT IS
  GOING (`LEVEL_OK` / `WARN` / `CRIT` / `IDLE`, `LEVELS`). The tiles, the
  pins, the site inset, the board, the overlay bins and the outliner all use
  them. Wires keep their per-kind ResourceKinds colours (finer than a
  channel).
- **Status motion** (`GraphTheme.level_motion`): ok and idle hold still;
  warn breathes about once a second; crit beats twice then rests. Tiles show
  it in their ring arcs: a calm arc wears its CHANNEL's colour, a troubled
  one its level's, moving. The ring has an inner arc for the battery, and a
  charging system swells slightly on its own beat (`system_live`, pushed with
  the board). Motion keeps the existing alert cadence (`_alert_phase`,
  `_alert_seen_this_draw`) and stops when the clock does unless "animate flow
  when paused" is on (`_sim_flow_mult`).
- **Festival trunks** (V2 `_plan_trunks` / `_draw_trunks`, hooked in the
  base `_draw_connections`): at the site level, when one node is wired to
  `TRUNK_MIN` (3) or more systems drawn as tiles, those wires draw as ONE
  trunk to the middle of the tiles (thickness ∝ log count) with thin
  branches from there. Per channel, in its colour, with a bead stream
  scaled by the total flow on the flow animation's phase. `trunks_drawn`
  for checks.
- **One camera path** (`graph_canvas._fly_view`; `_animate_view` calls it):
  a short move eases out as before. A long one (more than ~0.6 screen at the
  closer zoom) zooms out on the way and back in. This is the smooth-zoom of
  van Wijk & Nuij 2003, simplified: the centre moves in a straight line while
  the log-zoom dips by ln(distance / 0.6 screen), and the move takes longer
  the bigger the dip (`last_fly_dip`). It works in freeform and Site Plan
  alike (the centre is −pan / zoom in both). Entering a scope ends with a
  1.5 % lens settle (`FLY_SETTLE`).
  - Any mouse press, wheel, touch or gesture on the canvas stops a running
    fly (`stop_fly()`, top of `_gui_input`). A long fly runs up to 0.9 s and
    would otherwise pull the view back from under the player's own zoom.
    Code that sets `_zoom` / `_pan` directly (the checks) calls `stop_fly()`
    first.
- ⚠ A press an overlay takes (a twin badge, the site inset:
  `_consume_press`) clears any drag / marquee state an earlier press left
  and swallows its own release. Otherwise a stale `_item_dragging` from a
  lost release re-selected an old node or deselected on release, so the
  inset click only worked some of the time.
- **Hints & shortcuts**, rewritten in two columns: Find your way, Edit,
  Lenses, Festival, and a colour key (channels + levels). It fits above the
  timeline at every size.
- **Coach mark** at the site level the first time camps or vehicles exist:
  "Scroll into a camp or vehicle to see its own system". It goes away for
  good when the player enters one or clicks Got it (ui_prefs.cfg
  `[graph_systems] coach_seen`).
- **Tour stop** `20c_festival_systems` (Walton): tiles, into a camp, Esc
  out, the Festival board. UiAudit strict: 0 errors at 1080 and 720.
- Gate: `tools\harness.ps1 -World walton -RunScript res://tools/checks/graph_motion_check.gd -Label graph_motion -Timeout 900`
  (11: the coach mark and a real click on Got it, a depot wired to four
  camps as one trunk, critical tiles keeping the canvas beating and nothing
  moving with the clock and the pref off, a long fly-to zooming out on the
  way and a short one not, the hints panel inside the canvas with the
  festival tools and colour key). graph_system_board_selftest is now 50
  (`_test_grammar`).

**Festival scale (Phase 6, 2026-11-05).** Measured first with
`tools/bench/graph_festival_bench.gd`: the Walton graph at 60x in six views
(root framed, root zoomed in, Site Plan whole and zoomed, inside a camp) plus
an animated root Tidy. `GFBENCH_FESTIVAL=1` opens festival mode at the camps'
natural headcount (1,053 people; the sandbox's population target is a test
value of 60). `GFBENCH_ONLY=site,site_zoom` limits the views,
`GFBENCH_SPEED` sets the speed. It prints draw ms PER REDRAW (`gv_draw_all`,
the whole V2 draw, avg ÷ calls), cards drawn, people drawn / grouped, and
per-card-type draw cost. Sub-spans: `gv_d_*` (Site Plan passes),
`gv_ambient`, `gv_dcthrottle`, `gv_chrome`, `gv_closure_m`,
`gv_camp_cards`, `gv_cc_*`.
- **Site Plan** went from 55 ms a redraw (with 80 people) to ~15 ms (with
  1,053). What it took:
  - **Projections are cached while the view holds still.**
    `GraphSoiPreviewService.projection_key()` (the camera pose rounded,
    lens, viewport and container) and `canvas.proj_view_key()` (that key, or
    zoom/pan on the flat plan) key:
    - `world_to_canvas_cached` (pins, the SoI ring);
    - each space's outline (`_screen_ring`: projected ring, world-space
      triangulation, thinned closed line), 4,319 vertices on Walton;
    - streams (`_site_line_cache`, one polyline per run of one mode);
    - the ring runs (`_ring_runs_cache`);
    - the world anchors of pins (`_anchor_cache`, cleared on
      struct_rev / user_rev or after `ANCHOR_TTL_MS`).
  - **People.**
    - Culled per 8 m cell before any per-person work (`_cell_on_screen`).
    - Projected with `project_moving` (2 m ground grid, no cache).
    - Drawn as ONE textured triangle array (`_batch_disc`), with interp
      records as Arrays.
    - Zoomed out past `AGG_PX_PER_M` (2 px/m) with 250 or more people, they
      are count discs binned in world space (`_draw_agent_groups`).
    - The provider hands the canvas a new payload at most every
      `SITE_DOTS_MS` (150 ms).
  - Space markers' static parts (area interior points can grid-sample a
    concave outline) are cached per registry revision in
    `NpcPopulationBridge.space_markers`.
  - Spaces, pins and people draw through GraphFastDraw (no `draw_circle`).
- **Culling.** Cards (`_item_on_screen`) and wires (`_wire_on_screen`,
  the bezier's hull padded) off the canvas are not drawn (`CULL_PAD_PX` 90).
  The visible-items cache stays whole for hit-testing. `cards_drawn` is for
  checks. Root zoomed in: 25.7 → 11.5 ms a redraw.
- **Once-a-second work.**
  - `CampLedger.boundary_ports` scanned every wire per camp port; it now uses
    an index of wire ends (`_wired_ends`).
  - Camp cards compute each camp's ledger once and the system board reuses
    it (`_camp_ledgers`). Peak 32 ms → 3 ms.
  - The closure refresh no longer forces a full dashboard refresh.
- **Dashboard.**
  - Power numbers follow SolarUI's tick at most every 100 ms; the site
    balance stays on the 1 Hz path (it ran every SolarUI tick).
  - The closure card refreshes at 2 Hz.
- **Tidy.** Over `TIDY_SYNC_MAX` (24) cards, Tidy settles over frames
  (`TIDY_BUDGET_USEC` 6 ms each, `is_tidying()`), then glides. It lands
  exactly where the one-shot Tidy does (selftest). The festival root was one
  155 ms block; it is now about 25 frames.
- The "In the world" drawer: `GraphEmbodiment.find_item_by_bound_prop_id` is
  indexed (it copied the item list per prop), and the drawer rebuilds only
  when the graph, the props or the lights change (`_world_inventory_sig`).
- **What is left** is not graph code. On Walton's festival at 60x the frame
  median is ~45–70 ms: people (`npc_population`, `npc_host`, `npc_dots`), the
  water network, the nav bake, the timeline, and render. The plan's 60 fps
  target is not reachable from the graph alone. The camp tiles cost ~130 µs
  each (four AA arcs and an icon; 5 ms for 40 at the root).
- ⚠ The Bash tool joins a heredoc's `\` line continuation into one line with
  stray tabs. It still parses, but use the Write tool for patch scripts
  (`fix_joins` found five such lines, two from Phase 5).
- Gate: `tools\harness.ps1 -World walton -RunScript res://tools/bench/graph_festival_bench.gd -Timeout 900`
  (with `GFBENCH_FESTIVAL=1`); graph_force_layout_selftest is now 26
  (`_test_tidy_over_frames`).

## Video export + camera keyframes (core/climelapse/, 2026-10-22)

The timeline's 🎬 renders a range to an MP4: it steps the world one frame at a
time with the clock held, draws each instant through its own camera into an
off-screen SubViewport and streams the frames into ffmpeg.
- **Why every export was black.** The 3D SubViewport's `get_image()` is RGB8;
  the old timecode compositor built an RGBA8 frame, and `Image.blit_rect`
  refuses mismatched formats (an engine error, nothing copied), so every frame
  stayed all-zero. The user's `climelapse_2024_04_18.mp4` was 1350 frames of
  Y = 16. The timecode is now a Label on a CanvasLayer INSIDE the capture
  viewport, so a frame is one image straight off the GPU and nothing is
  composited on the CPU. The capture viewport also copies the root viewport's
  MSAA / TAA / scaling / shadow atlas and the player camera's `environment`,
  `attributes` and `cull_mask` (`ClimelapseCameraRig`); without them it drew
  far darker than the game.
- **Frames go through a pipe, not PNGs** (`ClimelapseFramePipe`): raw rgb24 on
  ffmpeg's stdin via `OS.execute_with_pipe(..., true)` (a writer thread, a
  6-frame queue). ⚠ The pipe must be BLOCKING: non-blocking dropped every
  write once the buffer filled and ffmpeg wrote a 262-byte file (measured).
  ffmpeg runs `-loglevel error` so its stderr cannot fill; it is read after
  exit. `store_buffer` returns false once ffmpeg dies.
- **The options dialog** (`scenes/ui/climelapse_export_dialog.gd`, a
  `ModalFrame`): range (pre-filled from the Ctrl-drag selection; none = the
  next 24 h from the playhead), speed in sim-hours per VIDEO second
  (`ClimelapseExportOptions.TIME_PRESETS`: the bar's speeds, "Max" = the bar's
  Max = 2 h/s, then a day / 3 days / a week / a month / a season / a year per
  second, or any value up to `MAX_RATE`; or type the VIDEO LENGTH and the
  speed follows, `speed_for_length`), folder +
  file name, size (presets, the game window, custom; rounded to even for
  yuv420p), fps, CRF, the date/time strip, and render settings for the export
  only (graphics + shadow preset, MSAA, TAA, settle frames per video frame).
  Choices persist in `user://climelapse_export.cfg`. Frame i is at
  `start + i × hours_per_second / fps`, both ends included (24 h at Max,
  30 fps = 361 frames, 12.03 s).
- **While it renders** the export holds an exclusive clock claim
  (`climelapse_export`: time_scale 0, analemma off unless the export is an
  analemma), sets the root viewport
  `disable_3d` (the world is drawn once per step, by the export) and shows
  the export's own picture in the progress window. `_restore_world` gives back
  the claim, the graphics / shadow presets it changed and `disable_3d` on
  every exit path. A cancel keeps nothing (the partial MP4 is deleted).
- **Camera keyframes** (`ClimelapseKeyframes`, replacing the untimed
  waypoint list): each key is pinned to an absolute hour, saved per world
  (WorldPaths kind `climelapse_keys`). Between keys the camera follows a cubic
  Hermite in TIME (Catmull-Rom tangents over uneven spacing, zero at the
  ends, so the shot eases in and out; "Smooth path" off = straight lines);
  yaw is unwrapped the short way; fov lerps. 0 keys = a STILL shot from the
  current view, whatever the camera (2026-10-23: the drone used to make up a
  near-full-circle sweep of its own; `ensure_default_hyperlapse_path` is
  gone), 1 key = locked on it. Editing on the timeline's CLIM lane: 📍 keys
  the current view at the playhead (a key at the same moment is replaced),
  drag a diamond to retime (a press that moves under 4 px is a CLICK and
  opens the camera-path editor on that key), double-click to jump the
  playhead to it, right-click for jump / preview from here / set to the
  current view / edit camera path / delete, or on empty lane: key here / key
  at playhead / preview / edit camera path / clear all.
- **Camera-path editor** (`scenes/ui/climelapse_path_editor.gd`,
  `UILayer/ClimelapsePathEditor`, made by `TerrainLoader.open_climelapse_
  path_editor(key, opts)`; also "Edit camera path…" in the export dialog,
  which hides while it is open). A right-edge dock in the TOOL-OVERLAY tier
  (prop-editor contract: free cursor, RMB looks, Esc steps out a drag, then
  Look through, then the editor). `ClimelapsePathView` draws the keys in the
  world, no depth test: the flown path (`ClimelapseKeyframes.sample_path`,
  the export's own sampling), view ticks along it, each key's marker, number
  + time and frustum wireframe at the export's aspect (`frustum_corners`,
  VERTICAL fov), the selected key amber, the playhead's camera white. A
  `LightGizmo` sits on the selected key in a YAW-ONLY frame with
  `hidden = ["rz"]` (the gizmo's new hidden-handles list): the green ring
  pans (yaw about world up), the red ring tilts (pitch about the key's side
  axis, clamped ±89°), arrows / squares move it. A ring seen edge-on (the
  tilt ring when the key faces along your view) cannot be grabbed — use the
  Tilt field or Look through. Fields: Pan = compass heading
  (`heading_deg` = −yaw, 0 north), Tilt, FOV, East / Up / South. Look
  through = a (non-exclusive) camera claim on an editor camera at the key;
  drag pans and tilts (from mouse POSITIONS — pushed / warped motions carry
  a wrong `relative`), the wheel zooms. Click a marker to select a key.
  Edits save on release (`set_climelapse_key_pose(..., save)`); Revert =
  `restore_climelapse_keys` with the keys as the editor opened; Preview
  plays from the selected key and the editor comes back after. Undo / redo
  (Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y in `_input`, ahead of the terrain's own undo; buttons
  too) over whole-key snapshots, held-spin / wheel edits coalesced;
  "Add at the playhead" (your view), "Move here" (the selected key to the
  playhead), PageUp / PageDown, and where the key lands in the video.
- **Sky options** (dialog "Sky" + "Aim"; `ClimelapseSkyDirector`, shared by
  the export and the preview so they match; everything restored by `end()`):
  - Analemma (sun / moon): the game's ∞, stepped by the export
    (`analemma_export_begin / _step / _end`, `analemma_external_step` stops
    `_process` stepping it). Its speed is `analemma_days_per_second` (any
    value; presets a day … a year per second, "60 days/s" = the game's ∞ at
    60 fps; the speed row switches unit). Frame i shows day
    `analemma_day_of_frame` = floor(i × dps / fps): below the frame rate a
    day is held, above it days are skipped in the VIDEO but the director
    still steps through each one (≤ 7 per call), so the figure on the sky
    gets every day, as in the game. A range under `ANALEMMA_MIN_DAYS` (30)
    becomes a year from its start day (`analemma_range`, 365 frames at one a
    day) — in the dialog, the path editor's preview and the lane menu's
    preview; the dialog also has a "One year" range button.
  - Clouds off = `main.clear_sky_override` (cloud layers, cloud shadows and
    the weather light factor, for the video only; data untouched).
  - Star trails "grow through the night": closed above −6° sun altitude,
    then the exposure arc grows at 15.04°/h (`trail_state`).
  - Aim: follow the sun / moon (look at it, horizon level, `look_basis`) or
    the stars (the camera turned with the sky since the first frame,
    `follow_stars_basis`: the stars hold still and the horizon rolls).
- **Keyframe timing** (`camera_timing` auto / pinned / spread,
  `ClimelapseExportOptions.key_timing`, `rig.key_timing`): PINNED = each key
  at its hour on the timeline; SPREAD = the path from the first key to the
  last fills the whole video (`ClimelapseKeyframes.sample_progress(t_norm)`,
  t_norm = VIDEO progress in both the capture and the preview), keys keeping
  their spacing. Auto pins when ≥ 2 keys are inside the range or their span
  covers half of it, and always spreads under an analemma. ⚠ Before this, a
  path keyed a few hours apart played in the first frames of a year-long
  analemma (or never, for a range elsewhere) and the camera then sat on the
  last key — "the preview has no camera movement". The dialog's camera note
  says which timing applies and why.
- **Preview** (`ClimelapsePreview`, the dialog's Preview button or the lane
  menu): plays the shot in the game window in real time at the export's
  speed, with an exclusive clock claim and an exclusive camera claim
  (`climelapse_preview`), a top bar (Pause / Restart / Stop, a scrub bar,
  Space / ← → / Home, a camera-path line), HUD hidden; an analemma scrubbed
  back restarts and steps forward; from a key on a spread path it starts at
  that key's place in the video. Esc or Stop puts the clock back where it
  was and the player camera back.
- Old `start_climelapse_export(start, end, time_scale, path, fps)` still works
  (it fills the remembered options). Selftest + probe in the Validation list.

## Sim pre-render + playback (2026-10-17, the timeline's 📈 Render button)

Plan: `~/.claude/plans/i-ve-noticed-that-as-quiet-dove.md`. The sim is a
deterministic function of sim-hours, so a stretch of it is RENDERED ahead into
the live caches and the ambient tick REPLAYS it (reads) instead of simulating,
which is what lets the player explore in first person with a growing graph.
`core/sim/`: `SimRenderCache` (ranges + keyframes), `SimBakeStepper` (the ONE
deterministic step, shared with `ChallengeBakeEngine`), `SimRenderer` (a child
of SystemGraphView, `sim_renderer()`); `scenes/ui/hud/render_progress_card.gd`.
- **The user's complaint was measured first** (`tools/bench/flow_step_bench.gd`):
  on Mount Vernon (14 items) the flow step was 0.3 ms a frame; the pond twin
  push was **36 ms a frame, 215 ms peaks** — `get_pond_info` re-swept the
  basin three times and ran a 19-sweep level bisection per pond every 0.25 s.
  `TerrainLoader._basin_samples_for` memoises the basin's ground samples on
  `_basin_ground_fingerprint` (cleared on sculpt commit / undo) and
  `PondBathymetry.*_from_samples` integrate over them in the SAME cell order,
  bit-identical (pinned exactly in terrain_selftest). 16 → 35 fps at 60×, the
  same as paused. The F3 HUD gained `gv_pond_push`, `gv_dc_throttle`,
  `gv_faults`, `gv_placeholder`: read them before blaming `flow_engine`.
- **Render into the LIVE timelines.** `energy_timeline` (battery) and every
