  tank's `ResourceTimeline` already had backward read + forward-in-cache read;
  the render fills them ahead of the playhead through
  `SolarUI.make_sim_render_evaluator(model)` (solar = SPA + weather + shade +
  DC caps at the instant; load = the SAME `GraphAcLoad.compute_kw` the live
  tick integrates, zero while the inverter is shed; aux = scene aux + the flow
  engine's graph DC from the PREVIOUS step — hydro into the battery, one-step
  lag like the live 0.25 s sync). Range = `[playhead, end]` (tanks can only be
  rendered from the current state), end = the Ctrl-drag selection's end or
  +24 h, capped at `MAX_RENDER_H` 7 d (the live timelines are a fixed 1-min
  grid of 20160 samples INCLUDING history). `_sim_series` stays for the
  observed-vs-sim Compare render (Shift-click 📈).
- **Keyframes carry only what no timeline records and nothing re-derives**
  (`SimRenderCache.keyframe_key`): node states, starved kinds, habitat ideal
  imports, batch progress, camp power, pop_state, the deficit tanks (no
  timeline), the wire flows, and the engine's between-step state
  (`internal_state_snapshot`: batch progress, demand overrides, per-scope AC,
  supply curves) so a live step resuming at any instant of the range starts
  from THAT instant's state. Hydro `live_*` is recomputed on replay by
  `_refresh_hydro_telemetry_readonly`; `dc_*` is the DC throttle's live display.
  Sparse deltas every 15 sim-min; the range's first keyframe is FULL; a
  non-incremental compose ERASES keys later keyframes introduced (a node
  state the engine set at step 40 must be gone at step 10).
- **Replay = read, never simulate** (`_tick_resource_flow_ambient`): inside a
  rendered range `cache.apply_at` then `flow.replay_at(now)` (apply first — it
  restores the engine's clock-at-keyframe; replay_at leaves `_last_abs_hours`
  at now, so a later live step continues from here); camp power stands down
  (keyframes carry `camp_*`; `_camp_power` is cleared so it re-seeds from
  specs on exit); the DC throttle runs display-only; SolarUI reads the
  rendered SOC and takes the readouts from the cache (the divergence
  truncation is gated OFF inside a range — the live scene-sun path differs
  from the pure evaluator by more than 0.05 kW on the first tick). NPCs keep
  simulating live off the cached supply (user's call). **Not in LIVE mode**
  (`SimMode.is_live()`): HA measurements are authoritative there, and this
  also sidesteps a 1× playback resolving LIVE and pushing to HA.
- **Invalidation is `GraphModel.user_rev`.** `struct_rev` moves on topology,
  `user_rev` on any write made while `model.sim_writing` is false. The view's
  `_begin_sim_writes()` / `_end_sim_writes()` is THE bracket for every sim
  writer (it replaced eight hand-rolled `was_suppress / was_bulk` blocks) and
  sets the flag; the HA linker and the fault check set it themselves; wire
  telemetry goes through `stamp_connection_telemetry` (reason
  `"conn_telemetry"`: a coalesced redraw, no fault check, no conduit remesh,
  no counter). A `user_rev` move → `SimRenderer.invalidate_from(playhead)`
  cuts every range there (drops one starting after the playhead) and
  truncates the energy + tank timelines. Non-graph inputs the render
  integrated are compared each tick (`_weather_sig`: datasets loaded +
  forecast window; connector-losses setting; PopTestPrefs generation) and a
  sculpt commit calls `invalidate_sim_render_all`. ⚠ **ANY unbracketed sim
  write kills the cache** — by design. `GraphModel.trace_user_rev = true`
  prints each move with the item and the changed keys; the probe turns it on.
  Found that way: `_sync_graph_energy_from_solar` reached from the post-tick
  flush (panel `current_output_kw` / `pv_offered_kw`). The bench prints a
  `user_rev` PASS line for the graph-closed regime.
- **The render owns the world like the bake**: exclusive clock claim
  `"sim_render"` at time_scale 0 (time stands still, the player can walk), the
  ambient tick suspended, `_pond_twin_push_blocked` (render steps would walk
  the 3D water to the range's end), `NpcPopulationBridge.freeze_tiers` (a
  FULL snapshot cannot `restore_all` onto a camp CrowdFocus re-tiered
  meanwhile), snapshots of specs / rosters / battery / flow internals /
  `camp_power_state_snapshot`. Finish or cancel keeps the rendered part
  (Premiere keeps a partial preview) and restores the playhead: specs →
  `cache.apply_at` → `flow.replay_at` → rosters → `reseat_battery_at` → one
  pond push → claims released. Steps on a 24 ms per-frame budget (Mount
  Vernon: 24 h ≈ 1441 steps ≈ 5 s; solar ~0.4 s, resources ~2 s of that).
  `SaveSystem` skips an autosave tick while a render is active (the specs are
  at the cursor). Refused in LIVE mode, while another system owns the clock,
  in the bootcamp sandbox, or for an end at or before the playhead.
- **Timeline UI**: 📈 enabled whenever nothing owns the clock (it used to be
  disabled without a CSV clip, and the disabled look was invisible —
  `_mk_icon_btn` now has a `disabled` stylebox + `_dim_disabled`); a
  3 px **render strip** at the top of the clips lane (`RENDER_STRIP_H`; the
  default clips track is 14 px): green = rendered, dim green = rendering,
  red = a selection ahead of the playhead not yet rendered; the
  `RenderProgressCard` (HudLayout top_center: range, bar, %, ETA, Cancel);
  toasts on refusal and completion; `TimeDirector.Provenance.RENDERED`
  (`register_rendered_ranges`, the data chip reads RENDERED in green). Tour
  stop `20b_render_sim`.
- **Live-sim streamlining, accuracy-neutral (the bench hash is the pin):**
  `GraphNesting.flat_connections_cached` (keyed struct_rev + user_rev +
  count; read-only — fault-flag writers keep the fresh copy) for the flow
  index, the AC load reading (10 Hz) and the DC sum (4 Hz); the engine's conn
  index rebuilt only when that key moves; lazy `duplicate(true)` in the
  siphon / JIT passes; a per-step pond-tag → tank map for culverts; the
  siphon outlet stamp through the index; `_write_if_changed` (exact compare)
  for the PBI / catchment writes; the deferred fault check coalesced to one
  per frame and never queued by `conn_telemetry`; `GraphPlaceholderHost`
  one deferred sync per frame and none for sim writes; `_find_terrain_loader`
  cached; `_dc_analysis` keyed on struct_rev.

## Flat-pack furniture designer (core/flatpack/, 2026-10-23)

Slotted plywood furniture, Burning Man "PlayaTech" style, cut on a CNC
router: Library → Structures → "Flat-pack furniture designer…" (no hotkey).
Plan: `~/.claude/plans/c-users-notsa-documents-playa-tech-glb-dapper-wilkinson.md`.
Built from the user's `Playa Tech.glb` (a SimLab export, inches): an 8 ft
sofa of 12 half-inch parts that sets up upright, reclined or flat as a
daybed and nests onto exactly three 4×8 sheets. `tools/flatpack_glb_reference.py`
measured it into `core/flatpack/testdata/playatech_daybed_ref.json` (the GLB
is not committed; it carries a scale figure).
- **Units are INCHES** until the mesh builder (×0.0254) or a mm export.
- **Outlines keep true arcs** (`FlatpackProfile`): a ring is points + DXF
  bulges. A part is a straight-edged BASE polygon + per-vertex fillet radii +
  EDGE NOTCHES; `ring_from_base` lays the notches in and shrinks a fillet
  that would run into a slot. Inside corners get dogbones, T-bones (overcut
  sideways only, slot bottoms stay flat) or none. Holes are CW rings.
- **Every slot is derived from the 3D assembly** (`FlatpackJoints`): a
  template emits slabs (base + `frame` Transform3D whose z is the normal)
  and joints; the solver intersects the mid-planes, clips the line to both
  outlines and cuts: `cross_lap` (A notched from the end toward `open`, B
  from the other, A takes `ratio`; width = other sheet / sin(angle) + 2 ×
  clearance) or `tenon` (A's outline carries tabs; B gets a mortise, or an
  edge slot where the tab reaches B's edge; `wedge` adds a wedge hole in A
  drawn in 1/16" and a wedge part). Slots from every POSE are laid in
  together, and parts in one `match` group are cut identically (union), so
  one set of parts assembles every way — exactly the sample. Only the 2-D
  base is used for chords; parallel or <45° pairs are refused with a reason.
- `FlatpackJoints.interference` walks the line where each pair's mid-planes
  meet: a point solid in BOTH finished outlines is a clash (a grid sample
  misses a 15/32" band). Every built-in design is clash-free in every pose.
- **Templates** (`FlatpackTemplates`, furniture frame X length, Y up, +Z
  front): sofa (the sample; rails, cross rails, arms, deck slotted into the
  arms, back + braces per pose; the upright brace stands ~7" forward of the
  reclined one so their rail slots do not overlap, never far enough to reach
  the deck); the table family (bench / stool / table / coffee table: tabbed
  leg panels or crossed X legs, a stretcher wedged outside the end legs, a
  bench back from leg posts); chair / lounger (side profiles from six control
  points the player can drag — `profile_offsets` — seat and back on tabs,
  wedged stretchers). `FlatpackPresets`: the sample as drawn (0.5" exact, no
  clearance/relief/spacing — what the selftest pins), router-ready versions
  (15/32" actual, 0.010" clearance, dogbones, 3/8" spacing, 0 margin so a 96"
  part comes out of a 96" sheet) and the library `user://flatpack_library.json`.
  Router-ready sofa defaults (11 1/2" rails, 35 1/2" deck, 23 3/4" arms and
  braces) still nest on three sheets.
- `FlatpackDesign.solve(spec)` (cached by the resolved spec) is the ONE
  solved design the modal, builder, packing and CNC writers read: parts with
  rings, cut list (identical parts grouped, labelled A, B1…), MaxRects nest
  (`FlatpackNesting`, Jylänkä 2010, BSSF, grain lock), BOM (sheets, use, cut
  feet, passes, router minutes, mass from 1.5 lb/ft² per 1/2" — APA).
- **CNC** (`FlatpackCam`): R12 DXF per sheet (POLYLINE + bulges; layers
  OUTSIDE_CUT / INSIDE_CUT / ETCH_LABELS / SHEET; $INSUNITS), SVG per sheet
  sized in real in/mm (no fills, no background rect — an importer would cut
  it), a fit-test coupon (slots at thickness −0.010…+0.020"), a cut-list txt;
  `write_all` → `user://flatpack_designs/<name>/` or a native folder pick.
- **Modal** (`scenes/ui/flatpack_designer_modal.gd`, on the loader's
  CanvasLayer 27 like the rack builder; `UiFit.keep_fitted`, modal claim):
  types + designs left; Assembled (orbit, pose, explode, build scrub, click
  picks a part) / Sheets / Side profile centre; Size, Material, Joinery
  (per-joint kind / wedge / share overrides), Machine, Style, checks, parts,
  cut list, export right. ⚠ Godot takes a SpinBox's decimals from its step
  (a 1/4" step prints 23.75 as "23.8"): length spins step 0.001 with the
  arrow step at the real increment.
- **World**: ModelCatalog procedural `flatpack_furniture` (record key
  `flatpack_spec`; one "Mesh" MeshInstance3D so prop collision works),
  `begin_flatpack_placement`, prop editor "Edit furniture…", PackedSpec
  DYNAMIC (`FlatpackDesign.packed_spec`: a panel_stack of the parts).
  `PlacedPropService.tag_flatpack_space` tags it `sleep` (daybed pose: one
  per lying spot) or `quiet` (one per seat), tables untagged.
- **People sit ON it**: the builder's `seat_spots` meta (local metres, yaw
  turning −Z to the faced direction) → the bridge's `_resolve_seat_spots`
  (once a second, spaces whose prop is flat-pack furniture) → ctx
  `seat_spot_of(sid, k)` (forwarded by the engine's `_make_ctx` WHITELIST)
  → full tier `NpcAgent._take_seat` (target, face anchor, `seat_elev` read by
  `elev()` while DOING, lie yaw) and light tier `CrowdCohort._take_seat`
  (`_seat` read by `elev_of`). No furniture = no change (the tier
  equivalence pins are untouched). Light-tier sleepers still use their camp
  beds, so a daybed sleeper is full tier only.
- Not built: true-shape nesting (bounding rectangles today), router G-code
  (the user chose DXF + SVG), PDF templates, an NPC crew that cuts and
  assembles it.

## Dome & zome designer (core/domelab/, 2026-10-25)

Library → Structures → "Dome & zome designer…" (no hotkey); click a placed
dome or the prop editor's "Edit dome…" reopens it bound to the prop. Pure
modules under `core/domelab/`, the modal `scenes/ui/domelab_modal.gd`
(flat-pack designer pattern: own CanvasLayer 27, `UiFit.keep_fitted`, modal
claim, SubViewport studio). Record key `domelab_spec`, model id
`domelab_structure` (`DomeLabBuilder.MODEL_ID`), the existing crafted 2V
`geodesic_dome` / `DomeParts` is untouched.
- **`DomeLabGeodesic`** is the Goldberg–Coxeter construction: a (b, c)
  triangular lattice per face of the icosahedron / octahedron /
  tetrahedron, Class I (f, 0), Class II (f/2, f/2), Class III (b, c),
  projected to the sphere. Straddling corners are carried across the edge
  with `(λ1 + λ3, λ2 + λ3, −λ3)` on the neighbour (the reflected far corner)
  until inside; vertices merge by position, faces by vertex set. Chord
  factors match Domebook / desertdomes to 2e-5 (2V, 3V, 4V pinned).
  ⚠ **The lattice maths is 64-bit scalars, never Vector2**: a Class II tie
  (unit triangle whose centroid lies ON the face edge) computed in float32
  read −1e-7 near two corners and 15 faces of 240 vanished with V − E + F
  = −8. ⚠ Every icosahedral mirror plane holds two icosa edges, which a
  Class II lattice straddles, so a Class II "hemisphere" is never a clean
  great circle: the 8 straddlers are trimmed (4V edge-up keeps 116 of 240)
  and the base-level check says so. Truncation picks the ring nearest the
  fraction's height (rings merged within 3 % R: a 3V "5/8" base is two
  heights ~0.01 R apart = one ring; `flat_base` levels it, adding strut
  lengths; the real 3V "5/8" is ~0.59 of the sphere). `stretch` makes an
  ellipsoid. Normals for the connector maths are the FULL surface's
  face-average normals, taken before the cut (base hubs keep the true
  surface normal).
- **`DomeLabZome`**: the polar zonohedron of order n — generators on one
  cone, vertices V(i, k) = Σ of k consecutive generators, rhombi
  R(i, k) = [V(i,k), V(i,k+1), V(i−1,k+2), V(i−1,k+1)], ONE strut length,
  n(n−1) rhombi. Layers 0 … K; "cut" floor = the bottom row trimmed to
  triangles on the level ring V(·, K); "zigzag" keeps whole rhombi. Every
  edge is tagged with its RIB (R_i: fixed i; L_m: fixed i + k). The helix
  zome (simplydifferently.org/Helix_Zome) is exactly the polar zonohedron's
  infinite-frequency limit: `rib_point` is the smooth curve through a rib's
  nodes (r = L sinθ sin(kπ/n)/sin(π/n), ψ linear in k, y linear in k); the
  ribs option builds continuous curved ribs lapped where R crosses L.
- **`DomeLabConnectors`** reads every angle off the geometry: dip =
  asin(−d · N) (half the central angle on a sphere = the conduit end bend),
  azimuths in the tangent plane → hub arm patterns (canonical rotation of
  the gap/dip sequence, `angle_tol_deg`), dihedral → flange fold = half the
  angle between face normals, flat-bar arc = chord · δ / sin δ, bend radius
  = chord / 2 sin δ, strain = t / 2R. Strut classes by (cut, sorted end
  bends) within `group_tol_mm`, A = shortest. Systems: `bolt_stack` (cut =
  chord + 2 × hole offset, bend = dip, one bolt per hub sized from the
  stack), `hub` (socket: cut = chord − 2 × reach; plate: flattened ends on
  a star plate, drill template per hub type; ring), `flat_bar` (arc lengths,
  bars lie flat on the bolt), `nexorade`, `plate`.
- **`DomeLabNexorade`**: every edge a slat turned about its midpoint in the
  tangent plane by ρ; consecutive slats round a vertex cross at the skew
  lines' closest points → four holes a slat (two ends, two inboard), length
  = span + overhang. `mode` "band" (flexible bands on the surface, holes
  spaced along the ARC; auto fits the engagement LENGTH to `engage_frac` of
  the edge) or "rigid" (straight slats; auto fits the mean eccentricity to
  the slat thickness — tiny angles for thin slats, that is physics).
  Base-ring slats have no neighbour below and are shorter.
- **`DomeLabPanels`**: a panel per face inset by the seam gap, screw holes
  along the edges (strut systems) or FLANGES (plate system: mitred along the
  exterior bisector, ext = w · tan(ext/2) capped at 1.5 w, relief, fold
  lines carry the bend); each part turned to its smallest bounding box and
  nested with `FlatpackNesting` onto the sheet (material's, or the
  Fabrication override). Classes = congruent panels. Rings are
  FlatpackProfile rings in MILLIMETRES.
- **`DomeLabDesign.solve`** (cached by `DomeLabSpec.key_of`) is the one
  solved design: geo, frames, edges, fans, struts, classes, hubs, nexorade,
  ribs, panels, bolts, stats (height, floor area, surface, volume, chord
  factors), the build order (rings from the base up), `DomeLabBom.compute`
  (rows, first-fit-decreasing stock packing with kerf, fasteners, masses)
  and the checks (Euler, stock length, slenderness L/r, flattenable
  section, bar strain, rhombus mechanism, base level, nexorade fit, panel
  fit, folding sheet). `packed_spec` = strut bundle (longest cut × √(n ·
  section) square) merged with the panel stack. `DomeLabCam.write_all`:
  DXF (R12, layers OUTSIDE_CUT / INSIDE_CUT / FOLD / ETCH / ETCH_LABELS /
  SHEET) + SVG per sheet and per plate-hub template, a strut-end SVG per
  conduit class, `_struts.csv`, `_bom.csv`, `_cut_sheet.txt`,
  `_design.json` (`DomeLabBom.fabrication_json`: vertices, faces, struts,
  hubs with arm azimuths / dips, nexors, panel outlines, BOM, checks).
- **`DomeLabBuilder`**: one MeshInstance3D "Mesh" with a surface per
  material, tubes round (8 sides, 16 past 6 cm, RADIAL normals), bars flat
  on the surface, lumber / beams / ribs on edge, hubs as bolt + nut /
  sphere / disc, slats offset by half a thickness, ribs as helix segments;
  `explode` moves parts out along the normal, `assembly` drops rings in
  from the base up; `record` keeps segment / sphere / triangle pick data
  read by `pick`. The placed dome counts as SHADE (`shade_footprints`).
  ⚠ **Never `generate_normals()` on these SurfaceTools** (2026-10-25): its
  default smooth group merges every vertex by position, so the flat panels
  and the prisms' edges rendered as one rounded "bubble" — every emitter
  writes the normal it means (`_tri` / `_tri_n`). Finishes follow the
  STOCK: `DomeLabMaterials.STRUT_LOOK` / `SHEET_LOOK` (galv / alu / paint /
  plastic / wood / ply / glazing / fabric) → `StructureMaterials` kinds
  (GALVANISED, ALUMINIUM, PLASTIC, GLAZING, FABRIC were appended for it);
  the PV-glass PANEL kind is not used here. A part is drawn in the player's
  colour, or the stock's own while the colour is still the default
  (`_part_color`; the modal's Colours rows show the drawn colour and reset
  to the stock). The studio lights with a sky ambient + SSAO so the facets
  shade apart; the Sheets tab scrolls at a readable size.
- **Helical zomes (`DomeLabHelical`, family "helical", 2026-10-26).** The
  zome's n generators indexed over all integers; a CELL is the zonohedron
  of w consecutive ones, and cell a−1 sits at b(a) + g_{a+w−1} — one step
  round and down. w = n is the polar zonohedron swept along a helix (n steps
  a turn); w = 3 stacks rhombohedra, n = w = 4 at 54.7356° rhombic
  dodecahedra (your photo's "stacked cubes"). The surface is EXACT: bricks
  {i<j<k, k−i<w} at Σ_{i<l<j} g + Σ_{l>k} g tile every cell with the SAME
  bricks wherever cells overlap, so the boundary = brick faces met once.
  ⚠ Keys are integer generator-count vectors; 0.1 mm float keys split one
  face pair in ~2700 and left a hole. Spec `helical` {sides, pitch_deg,
  window, steps, hand, levels (rows kept from the apex, floor cut level
  there, straddling rhombi keep their top triangle), stretch}; radius_m =
  one CELL's widest ring. Faces carry `face_zone` (generator distance,
  1 … n/2 = one rhombus shape each; the plain zome got it too).
  `Helical Zome Corten Steel.glb` (user's Documents) is reproduced node for
  node by n = w = 10, θ 57.1°, 1.585 m, 20 steps (452 / 900 / 450); preset
  `helical_corten` cuts it at the person's floor (14 rows), 3 mm corten,
  PMMA in zones 1–2. `tools/diag/rack_model_study.gd --dome-preset=<id>`
  shoots a preset the same eight ways as the GLB.
- **Folded plates are solid (2026-10-26).** `DomeLabPanels.flange_section`
  is the ONE section (mm, x into the face, y along its normal): flat plate
  to xc, a bend of inside radius `fold_radius_mm` (0 = t) swept 90° + ang/2,
  a flange parallel to the dihedral's bisector plane with its outer skin
  gap/2 off it, so neighbours meet back to back and the bolted pair is the
  strut (SPACEPLATES). The builder extrudes it per edge, each profile point
  clipped on the plane bisecting the two flanges at a corner (closes like a
  folded box). Bolt holes are laid out per EDGE (`bolts3d`, margin from the
  corner angle), so both plates of a seam are drilled alike; floor-edge
  holes are anchors. Openings: `oculus` + `oculus_mm` + `oculus_round` +
  `oculus_zones`, a `glazing` pane lapped 25 mm behind (DomeLabPanels.
  rounded_inset); `thickness_mm` overrides the sheet. Faces go into packed
  arrays, not SurfaceTool (the 216-plate home: 608k vertices, ~130 ms).
  Sheets corten_2/3 (look "corten" → `StructureMaterials.Kind.
  WEATHERING_STEEL`, appended) and pmma_4/6.
- **Folded-plate seams that bolt up (2026-10-26).** The flanges "almost
  joined" because:
  - **Valleys folded the wrong way.** `flange_bend` was `acos(n1·n2)/2`,
    which is unsigned, and the section clamped it to ≥ 0. A helical zome's
    cells meet in VALLEYS (12 seams on `helical_corten`; 85 of 372 on the
    user's saved window-8 home). There the flanges stood 160–168° apart.
    - `DomeLabConnectors.edge_records` now signs it: negative when the second
      face's centroid is above the first face's plane (`_valley`). `dihedral`
      is then over 180°.
    - `flange_section` takes a half-angle in ±`MAX_HALF_BEND`. A valley's
      fold is less than 90°.
    - BOM / cut sheet folds print the signed half-angle.
  - **Corners of 4+ plates.** At 3-plate nodes the three bisector planes
    share one line, so the plate mitres close exactly (measured 1e-4°). At
    nodes of four or more plates they don't: the two plates on a seam ended
    their flanges along mitre lines 20–118° apart (the wedges).
    `DomeLabPanels._node_cuts` gives such a seam end ONE plane that both
    flanges of the pair end on (`pn.node_cuts`, world mm, keyed
    `_cut_key(face, node, a, b)`). That plane runs halfway between the two
    mitre lines, at least `NODE_END_MIN_DEG` 40° off the seam, square to the
    seam, and set back `NODE_CLEAR_MM` past both mitres. The node itself is
    left open, as a real folded-plate node is.
  - **Mitre cap.** A mitre never runs past its corner by more than
    `MITRE_CAP` 1.5 × the point's depth (the flat pattern's own cap). Without
    it, a steep valley flange and its plate's next flange met 200–330 mm
    off.
  - **The flat pattern is developed from the section** (`developed`,
    `BEND_K` 0.44):
    - the face region is the outline inset by xc;
    - each flange is the bend allowance plus the run;
    - the DXF fold lines are the bend centre lines;
    - each hole sits where the folded flange carries it.

    Before, holes were at flange/2 from a gap/2 inset, which missed the 3D
    bolts. Bolt end margins clear any node cut.
  - Gate: `domelab_selftest._test_plate_seams` (196 checks). For every plate
    preset plus a window-8 valley variant it checks, as the builder draws
    them:
    - flange skins within 0.5° of parallel and gap ± 0.5 mm apart;
    - every flat-pattern hole, folded up, within 0.5 mm of its partner and
      of a bolt;
    - node-cut pairs on one plane.

    It fails at 160° and 88 mm on the old code.
  - Diags: `tools/diag/domelab_seam_probe.gd -- --preset=<id>|lib:<id>`
    (headless numbers: seams, corner wedge by valence, spikes) and
    `tools/diag/domelab_seam_look_diag.gd` (WINDOWED, APPDATA at a scratch
    folder; close-ups of a valley, a ridge, a 4+ node and a 3 node;
    `--library=<id>` for a saved design).
- 16 presets (`DomeLabPresets.builtins`); library `user://domelab_library.json`.
  Panels that do not fit the sheet are an ERROR in the checks (a real
  blocker): the presets are sized so every one solves clean. Gates in the
  Validation list; tour stop `18d_domelab`.

## CNC gantry designer (core/gantrylab/, 2026-10-25)

Library → Structures → "CNC gantry designer…" (no hotkey); click a placed
machine or the prop editor's "Edit gantry…" reopens it bound to the prop.
The dome-lab pattern: pure modules under `core/gantrylab/`, the modal
`scenes/ui/gantrylab_modal.gd` (own CanvasLayer 27, `UiFit.keep_fitted`,
modal claim, SubViewport studio). Record key `gantry_spec`, model id
`gantry_machine` (`GantryLabBuilder.MODEL_ID`, catalog category "tools"),
library `user://gantrylab_library.json`, exports `user://gantrylab_designs/`.
- **The pattern language** is `GantryLabSpec.KINEMATICS` (bedslinger,
  cartesian_xy, corexy, corexz, hbot, delta, router) with `KINEMATICS_WHY`
  (when to use each) and `APPLICATIONS` (a job → pattern + tool + sizes,
  `for_application`). `resolve` couples the shared-belt axes (CoreXY / H-bot
  copy X's drive onto Y; CoreXZ onto Z), forces a delta's bed round, and
  keeps `volts` an int (the JSON round trip made it a float and moved the
  cache key). `motor_axes(kin)` names the motors (A / B, the three towers).
- **Parts are data with sources** (`GantryLabParts`): V-slot 2020 / 2040 /
  2060 / 4040 / C-Beam 4080 / 3030 with kg/m and Ix / Iy (OpenBuilds /
  Misumi), guides (V-wheel, MGN9 / 12, 8 mm rod, HGR15), drives (GT2 6 / 9,
  GT3 15, Tr8×8, Tr8×2, Tr12×3, SFU1605 / 1610, mod-1 rack; belt spring rate
  per metre, screw root diameter, efficiency), motors (NEMA 17 pancake …
  NEMA 34, holding torque / amps / mass), boards with their usable step
  rate (RAMPS 10 k … Klipper RP2040 500 k) and firmware list, tools
  (hotends, pellet and clay extruders, spindles, lasers, pen: mass, watts,
  line width, feedstock kind), beds, hardware prices.
- **`GantryLabKinematics`** (pure): steps/mm, CoreXY A = x + y / B = x − y
  (H-bot the same on one belt, CoreXZ with z), delta carriages
  `z + √(L² − d²)` + forward trilateration, `motor_velocity` (per-motor mm/s
  per mm/s of tool: a CoreXY diagonal runs one motor at √2 and the other
  not at all), force from torque (half the holding torque usable), belt
  stretch, `screw_critical_rpm = 4.76e6 · d_root · C / L²`, beam sag
  `F L³ / 48 E I`, the toolhead's ringing frequency.
- **`GantryLabGcode`** reads moves with feed / E / line (G0–G3 with I J and
  R arcs expanded to 1 mm chords, G20 / 21 / 28 / 90 / 91 / 92, M82 / 83,
  M104 / 109 / 140 / 190, M3 / M5 with S ≤ 1000 read as laser power so a
  laser program "extrudes"), and `to_toolpath` emits the game's Toolpath
  shape (points + extruding, decimated) so the job store takes it.
  `GantryLabMotion.plan` is the classic-jerk trapezoid planner (per-move
  caps from feed, max feed, per-axis and per-motor step-rate caps,
  `v_junction = jerk / |d₂ − d₁|`, backward then forward pass);
  `sample(t)` is the scrub. `GantryLabSamples` generates seven real
  programs sized to the machine (cube, vase, speed test, pocket, laser
  raster, plotter, surfacing).
- **`GantryLabFrame.layout`** is the geometry: the static frame (beams with
  profile + `up`, parts, screws) and the moving ASSEMBLIES ({parent, base,
  beams, parts, mass, axis}); `pose(spec, layout, tool_mm)` is the
  kinematics as offsets (a bed-slinger's bed at `vy/2 − y`, a cube's bed at
  `−z`, delta carriages at their heights), `belt_routes` / `delta_arms`
  the drawn loops. Machine frame: X → local +X, Y → local +Z, Z up; the
  work origin is the bed's front-left at its surface (`origin`); beads go
  under `bead_parent` ("Bed" where the bed moves, else the root) at
  `bead_origin`. A delta's carriage base is the TOWER CENTRELINE with the
  pivot `carriage_r` inward (the delta-radius convention) — the first cut
  put the base on the tower face and the drawn arms were 34 mm short.
- **`GantryLabDesign.solve`** (cached by `key_of`) → layout, bom, motors
  (steps/mm, resolution, speed caps, accel capable), limits for the
  planner, stats, checks, `graph_preset`. Checks: step rate at the max feed
  (× √2 on a shared belt) vs the board, acceleration vs torque and moving
  mass, Z lift force, Tr8×8 back-driving a heavy bed, belt stretch, X-beam
  sag (tolerance `sag_tol_mm` = max(process floor, a tenth of the line —
  an 8 mm clay bead forgives 0.8 mm), router rail sag and upright flex,
  screw whip (Z runs 10 mm/s on a Tr8×2, 30 on other screws, never the XY
  feed), resolution vs the line, delta reach and arm ratio, H-bot racking,
  driver count, 12 V above 120 mm/s, bed-slinger inertia past 300 mm, 2020
  past 350 mm. `GantryLabBom`: cut list rounded to 5 mm packed first-fit
  into 1.5 m stock, corner hardware per beam end, rails + carriages per
  axis, belts (two motors for A/B), pulleys / idlers / screws / nuts /
  couplers, motors + drivers, a PSU sized to the DC load, endstops, wiring,
  cable chain, tool, bed, enclosure. `GantryLabExport`: Klipper
  `printer.cfg` (kinematics, rotation_distance, delta arm / radius, input
  shaper at the ringing estimate), Marlin `Configuration.h` defines, grbl
  `$` settings, BOM CSV, cut list, design JSON (INF → null).
- **`GantryLabBuilder`** (Node3D): the static frame as one "Mesh" (the
  V-slot profile outline with a 6 mm groove per 20 mm cell, extruded;
  parts as boxes, screws and motor shafts as cylinders; surface per
  material key), a Node3D per assembly parented as the layout says (its
  mesh carries `skip_prop_collision`), "Belts" rebuilt per pose, and three
  DRIVER nodes `XDrive` / `YDrive` / `ZDrive` whose local position along
  their axis is the tool in metres; `_process` follows the drivers
  (`follow_drivers`, off in the studio), `set_tool_mm` is the one pose
  call, `set_toolpath_preview` / `set_preview_progress` lay beads at true
  scale on the bed node, `pick` tests per-part AABBs through the assembly
  chain from LOCAL transforms (a studio node is picked before it is in a
  tree).
- **In the world** a placed gantry's record carries `gantry_spec` and kind
  `gantry_machine` — NOT `cartesian_machine` (the GLB machines' record
  kind, whose `CncMachineRuntime` maps a profile's tagged sub-nodes).
  `GantryRuntime` (gameplay/) attaches by MODEL ID and plays the graph's
  job through `PrintJobPlayer` (see "One print pipeline"), moving the
  drivers in true mm along the PLANNED motion and growing the roads under
  the nozzle move by move. `PlacedPropService.seed_gantry_graph` (deferred on
  placement) makes a `cartesian_machine` processor from
  `GantryLabDesign.graph_preset` through `create_bound_generator_node`
  (machine_role fdm_printer for an extruder, cnc_router otherwise;
  inputs = the tool's feedstock — the new `filament` resource kind,
  `plastic_flake`, `mud`; watts and work volume from the design);
  `sync_gantry_graph` after Apply. The TOOLS preset "CNC Gantry
  (designed)" carries an empty `gantry_spec` (placing it from the graph
  builds the default bed-slinger). Modal Simulate → "Send to placed
  machine" = `start_machine_job` with the PrintJob of the parsed program
  (the move list + the design's limits), so the placed machine replays the
  very plan the tab showed.
- Gates: `gantrylab_selftest` (227), `tools/checks/gantrylab_designer_check.gd`
  (41), tour stop `18e_gantrylab`.
- **High-detail parts (2026-10-26).** Modelled on
  the user's CR-10 S4 GLB: `GantryLabDetail` (`core/gantrylab/gantrylab_detail.gd`)
  draws every part the frame names — motors on brackets, GT2 pulleys and
  idlers, Tr8 screws with couplers and brass nuts, V-wheels on their axles,
  rails and blocks, endstops, a V6-class hotend, a Bowden extruder, spool,
  springs, feet, corner brackets, PSU, LCD, board — in a LOCAL frame whose
  +Y is the part's axis. Belts are LOOPS of pulleys (`lay["loops"]`, nodes
  {asm, c, r, s = wrap sign, kind}) solved by common tangents

  per turning part (angle = motor mm / per_rev_mm) and scrolls the belt
  teeth (`gantry_belt.gdshader` `offset_m`); screws / couplers / springs are
  plain cylinders under `gantry_thread.gdshader` (UV = angle, metres).
  Still open: the look pass by eye (belt wrap signs, the i3 bed belt), the
  modal pass. ⚠ Loop node key `s` is the wrap sign — a clamp's extent

- **Parts that MATE (core/gantrylab/assembly/, 2026-10-26).** The V-slot
  machines (bed-slinger, Cartesian XY, CoreXY, H-bot; `GantryLabAssembly

  - `GantryLabCatalog`: real parts with FEATURES in their local frame

    band point), couplers, Tr8 screw / nut, motors (face + shaft).
  - `GantryLabMates`: `COMPAT` (child class → target class → mate type:
    slot, grid, endgrid, lines, butt, run, pattern, shaft, idler), `place`

    `fits` (every bolt on a slot line / grid hole / pattern hole), `snap`,
    `slide_range`, `infer` (pose → mate numbers), `fasteners` (T-nuts,

  - `GantryLabAssembly`: `build(spec)` = generated doc + the player's

    is zero: parts are drawn where they are at tool 0, so a node's position
    IS the jog). Belt planes come from the loop's first node; `auto` nodes
    (idlers on spacer stacks, pulleys on shafts) and clamps follow it, so a
    belt is planar by construction. A mate's `s` is measured from its
    `anchor` (start / centre / end) so resizing keeps distances. Twins:
    `edit_part` re-solves the mirrored twin (`mirror_mate`: mirror the
    world pose across x = 0, pick the turn whose boxes overlay the mirror

  - `GantryLabClash.check(spec, lay)`: oriented boxes (shrunk 0.4 mm, mated

  - The CoreXY routing: motors behind the back corners on L mounts whose

  - `GantryLabBom` counts what the assembly draws (`_assembly_rows`):

  - Builder: picks carry the part `id` and hit `point`; `mark_part` /

- **Shaft-guided lowering bed + modules (2026-10-26).**

- **Print preview = extruded roads (2026-10-26).** The old preview put ≤4000

  line_mm, layer_mm, color, mottle)` lays one rounded road per extruding
  planner move (straight runs merged), line wide (nozzle × 1.12 for
  additive), layer tall (`layer_guess_mm`: the commonest Z step), its top at
  the nozzle, alternate layers shaded, under the bed node.

  nozzle; `set_preview_progress(frac)` (the in-world runtime, by printed

  ⚠ Two MultiMesh traps, both of which hid the print:
  - Instances written while `visible_instance_count` hides them are dropped
    when the count grows: only the road being drawn showed. Every road stays
    drawn (`visible_instance_count = -1`), unprinted ones at a zero basis
    (`_HIDDEN`), and `_set_shown` rewrites only the range that changes.
  - The engine's own bounds are taken once, while few roads show, so the
    rest was culled: `custom_aabb` covers the whole print.

  Headless, MultiMesh keeps no transforms: tests read `road_transform(k)` and
  `roads_shown()`. A pale colour washes out white under the studio light;
  plastic flake is a mottled deep blue. The cube sample now has solid bottom
  and top layers and 25 % crossing infill. Diag:

## One print pipeline — slicer, planner, the machine in the world (2026-10-28)

The Trash Printer, the Mud Printer, the CNC router, a designed gantry and
any machine the player imports and tags all print through ONE pipeline.
Before this the GLB printers ran a point list at constant speed, STLs were
"sliced" as a raster over the bounding box, the mud printer clipped the STL
mesh with a shader, and only the gantry designer's Simulate tab had the
planner. Now:
- **A job is a move list** ({p0, p1, feed_mm_s, e_mm, rapid, line} in work
  mm, the shape `GantryLabGcode.parse` makes) plus the machine's motion
  limits (`PrintJob.limits_for_specs`: the specs' `max_feed_mm_s` /
  `accel_mm_s2` / `junction_mm_s`, a designed gantry's own, else
  `PrintJob.LIMIT_DEFAULTS` by machine_kind). `PrintJob.from_parse`
  (`core/machines/print_job.gd`) plans it with `GantryLabMotion.plan` and
  the plan's `total_s` IS the job's duration (`est_time_hr`, then the
  graph's `speed_factor`). `PrintJob.from_toolpath` turns an old point list
  (`Toolpath`, `StlLoader`'s router raster, `MudWallSlicer`'s dense slice)
  into one: travels where the flag is 0, roads at the print speed, an
  optional `shift_xy` onto a corner-origin bed. `start_machine_job` takes
  either and converts.
- **Work frame**: X / Y across the bed with (0, 0) at the bed's front-left
  corner, Z = 0 at the bed top (the gantry designer's convention); the
  model is centred at `centre_xy` (work / 2 + the offset). The mud
  designer's plan is centred on 0 and shifted by work / 2.
- **`StlSlicer`** (`core/machines/slicer/stl_slicer.gd`, pure): the
  triangles cut at each layer's MID height, each segment oriented
  solid-left from the triangle's winding (travel = up × n), chained by
  welded end points into loops (outer CCW, holes CW); perimeters by
  `Geometry2D.offset_polygon` (a SIGNED distance that keeps orientation:
  −d shrinks an outer, +d grows a hole — measured, not assumed), inner
  walls first; infill as parallel lines clipped by an even-odd scan over
  every loop (holes fall out of the parity), ±45° turning a quarter each
  layer or a grid, top / bottom layers solid; spiral vase after the solid
  bottom (Z ramps along one wall); travels with an optional Z hop; E =
  w·h·L / (π d² / 4) in mm of the feedstock bore d (`filament_mm`), so the
  job's `volume_mm3` IS the road laid and the graph bills w·h·L. Capped at
  `max_moves` (160 k; a warning). Not done: skin detection over overhangs
  beyond the top / bottom counts, support, bridging, retraction tuning.
  ⚠ Per-layer segment buffers are plain Arrays: a PackedVector2Array
  fetched from an Array / Dictionary is a copy-on-write VALUE and appending
  to it in place fills nothing (the first cut hung the whole engine).
- **`PrintGcodeWriter`**: the move list as real G-code — RepRap (M82, G92
  E0, G1 X Y Z E F, ;LAYER:n, temperatures) or the mud printer's GRBL
  relay dialect ("M3 S1000" / M5 round the roads, hops on travels, no E).
  `GantryLabGcode.parse` reads both back to the same moves (the S word on
  M3 is what flags the roads; `PrintJob.from_parse` re-derives w·h·L for
  a printer reading a relay program). The parser's `temps` are the HOTTEST
  the program asks for (a cool-down at the end used to zero them).
- **`MachineJobStore` v2**: a job with `moves` is written as
  `<id>.job` (binary, `store_var`: p0 / p1 / feed / e / rapid packed
  arrays + limits + road size + totals); v1 `<id>.json` point lists still
  load. **`PrintJobPlayer`** loads by id, plans (or re-plans an old point
  list through `from_toolpath` with the specs' speeds) and `sample(p)` →
  the nozzle at p × total_s: pos, move i, s, v, extruding, layer / layers,
  remaining_s. Both runtimes read it, so the machine in the world
  decelerates into corners and rapids between islands exactly as the
  studio did, and scrubs with the timeline.
- **`PrintRoads`** (`core/machines/print_roads.gd`, a MultiMeshInstance3D)
  is THE print: one rounded bead per extruding move (straight runs merged),
  line wide, layer tall, top at the nozzle, laid at true scale in a frame
  whose origin is work (0, 0, 0) — road local = origin + (x, z, y) · 0.001.
  `set_progress_move(i, s)` grows the current road to the nozzle;
  `set_wet(color, mm)` tints the last mm of road (mud dries behind the
  nozzle); `bake_mesh(color, offset)` → one ArrayMesh (a finished mud print
  becomes a placed object). `GantryLabBuilder.set_print_preview` and
  friends delegate to it (`roads()`), the pinned road transforms unchanged.
- **`CncMachineRuntime`** (rewritten): the profile's tagged axes move in
  TRUE millimetres. `_calibrate_frame` snaps the axes to rest, measures the
  tool tip (the tool node's AABB bottom) against the bed (the Z bed's plate
  top for a lowering bed, the frame's base centre for a fixed one) and
  keeps per axis `metres per local unit` + the local units that put the
  tool over the bed centre (z: at the bed, or the bed's home); an
  uncalibrated axis takes its window from the work volume. The roads'
  frame = the x / y axes' world directions + up, origin at the bed's
  front-left corner, parented to the Z bed when it drops (the print rides
  it). A finished additive job is baked (`PrintRoads.bake_object`) to a
  mesh + STL and handed to `register_printed_object` — a `print_persist`
  (mud / clay) print stays on the map; a bed print is credited to the
  parts inventory by the graph and handed off `on_bed` + `machine_item`
  ONLY after a lowering bed has dropped to the bottom of its travel
  (`_bed_bottom_mm`: the calibrated Z window, else the work volume;
  `FINISH_DROP_MM_S`). It is a printed object the player can grab and set
  anywhere (`update_printed_object_transform` clears `on_bed`);
  `start_machine_job` calls `clear_printed_objects_on_bed(item)`, so a new
  print takes the old one off the bed and out of the world (the inventory
  keeps it). A reload of a handed-off job lays nothing
  (`has_printed_object`). GantryRuntime does the same (a cube's Z bed is
  the bead assembly with axis "z"). A cut job's roads stay on the bed
  until the next job. Gate: the trash half of `print_pipeline_check`.
  A `Label3D` over the machine reads the progress, layer, speed
  and time left. `begin_print_preview(job)` ghosts the roads on the bed and
  `preview_tool_mm` follows the studio's scrub. The old STL reveal shader,
  print-span travel calibration and 40 %-footprint bead ghost are gone.
- **Print setup** (`scenes/ui/print_setup_modal.gd`, the prop editor's
  "Print…" / Interact on a printer, any cartesian_machine with a runtime,
  the gantry too): Load STL (sliced here: layer, line, walls, infill % +
  pattern, top / bottom, speeds, Z hop, scale, turn, offsets; a 0.3 s
  debounce), Load G-code (run as written), part presets (trash dome
  parts), Design building (mud). The studio shows the bed, the roads and a
  nozzle marker with the Simulate tab's transport (Play / Restart / speed /
  scrub / the HUD: time, move, position, speed, layer, feed-cap shares);
  the real machine's ghost and tool follow. Export G-code (relay dialect
  for mud), Start print. The estimate line: layers, moves, size, "OFF THE
  BED", material (g / kg, L for mud), the planned time and the sim time.
- The inspector's "Load G-code / STL" slices an STL on an additive node at
  the machine's own settings and parses G-code with `GantryLabGcode`.
- ⚠ **Machine jobs tick with the graph CLOSED now.** `_tick_graph_tools`
  (and the PP extruder / sheet press ticks) sat below `_process_frame`'s
  `if not visible: return`, so a print the player stood watching never
  advanced until G was pressed; the first sandbox run read 0 % with every
  road laid (the runtime's own clock-derived progress had long passed the
  end). They run in the ambient block too, inside the sim-write bracket.
- **Where the print is on the GLB machines** (measured 2026-10-28): the
  Trash Printer's extruder barrel pokes 9 cm through its deck INTO the
  cabinet and the Z bed rises to it there, so the print grows inside the
  white box, out of sight from outside (the status label over the machine
  is what reads); the Mud Printer prints on the terrain inside its frame
  (`_bed_world_origin` takes the ground height there). The saved
  `profiles.json` can name a static node as a machine's tool (the trash
  printer's says "Node") and carry print-span soft windows narrower than
  the bed: the runtime reads the tip off the deepest moving carriage when
  the tool node does not ride an axis, and never clamps the print pose to
  the soft window.
- Gates: `print_pipeline_selftest` (103), `tools/checks/print_pipeline_check.gd`
  (29 PASS on Mount Vernon) and `tools/checks/print_scale_frame_check.gd` (35).
- **Improvement pass (2026-10-28).** Four player reports, each with its trap:
  - **"A gyroid cube prints to 10 % with infill, full height without."**
    The slicer stopped at a 160 000-move cap and handed back the partial
    print with only a warning; infill just hit the cap sooner. A move was a
    Dictionary, measured at ~810 bytes, and a 150 mm gyroid at a 0.45 mm
    line is ~3 M moves (2.5 GB). Moves are now `PrintMoves`
    (`core/machines/print_moves.gd`, packed arrays, 37 bytes a move) from
    the slicer through PrintJob, the planner, PrintRoads, the G-code writer
    (streamed to the file in 20 000-line chunks) and the job store.
    `max_moves` (8 M) REFUSES with advice; it never truncates. Every reader
    takes either form through `PrintMoves.from_any` (G-code parses and the
    gantry designer still hand over Arrays of dicts); `GantryLabMotion.plan`
    keeps "moves" as given plus "pm" packed. The job store saves the PLAN
    too, so a million-move job is not re-planned when the world loads it.
    Measured: a 450 mm gyroid at a 6 mm line is 906 k moves, sliced in
    11 s, planned in 0.8 s, laid in 0.6 s; the 150 mm one at 0.45 mm is
    3.27 M moves over all 750 layers, 21 s to slice (on the worker), 2.9 s
    to plan, 2.1 s to lay, 523 MB with the mesh.
  - **PrintRoads past `DISPLAY_MAX_ROADS` (250 k)** merges curves into
    chords: the sagitta from arc − chord (≈ 8 s²/3L) plus the last vertex's
    offset, within a tolerance that grows with the overflow. Progress still
    runs move by move (arc length per road, the chord scaled). Rows are
    packed and the MultiMesh buffer is uploaded whole past `BULK_WRITE`
    instance writes (a CPU copy `_buf`). `set_base_color` recolours
    without a re-lay. The budget is a target: infill strokes are separate
    roads (travels between), so that 3.27 M-move gyroid still draws ~500 k.
  - **"The ghost and the print are rotated out of phase."** Two causes:
    (1) roads map work (x, y, z) to local (x, z, y), a REFLECTION, while the
    STL ghost is (x, z, −y): a mirror image, and so the Turn spun them
    opposite ways; (2) the ghost was centred on the TURNED footprint's
    centre, not the turned file centre. The studio now puts the roads under
    `PrintRoads.work_basis()` (work +Y → −Z) with the bed's front-left at
    +Z, and the slicer returns `place_xy` (where the model's own box centre
    lands). The GLB runtime picks the work-Y direction that makes X × Y =
    up (`_y_sign`), and GantryRuntime mirrors work Y about the volume's
    middle (the gantry frame maps Y → +Z): prints in the world were mirror
    images of their models too. A finished mud print is baked through the
    reflection (`bake_mesh(..., post)` reverses the winding) so the placed
    object has a proper turn.
  - **"The scale is fixed at 4×; let me set the width."** One exponential
    scale slider from 0.001× to 1000× for every printer (the mud printer's
    8× cap also clamped `set_slicer` calls), never reset on reopen, and a
    **Size (mm)** row: W / D / H spin boxes (the model's own extents × the
    scale; type one, the scale follows) with 1:1 and Fit bed.
  - **"Scaling is off between parametric and GLB printers."** A designed
    gantry is "generic FDM" to FdmPrinterCaps, whose 0.2–2.5 mm line range
    clamped the 6 mm flake head to 2.5 mm roads; `_fit_ranges` now widens
    every range to the machine's own head. GantryRuntime also drew roads
    12 % wider than the job. A delta's work origin is the bed centre
    (`origin_centred`, `bed_centre_mm()`); the setup centred prints at
    work/2 on it.
  - **The Trash Printer model was 1.79× too big.** Its GLB is already in
    true metres (SimLab inches under a 0.0254 node; NEMA 23 motor 56 mm,
    bed 32 × 21.3 in), and the catalog's `reference_height_m: 2.0` fitted
    its 1.12 m on top of that. Removed: the bed is 813 × 541 mm and the
    player's profile travel 610 × 368 × 411 mm (its preset work volume is
    still a 600 mm cube). Before trusting a `reference_height_m`, dump the
    GLB (`glb_dump_diag.gd`): a 0.0254 node means it is already metres.
    The PP shredder / beam extruder / sheet press had the same double fit
    (files 1.01 / 1.06 / 1.24 m fitted to 1.6 / 1.8 / 2.0 m; their M12 x 40
    bolts, 49 in sheet and 1.245 m beam confirm the files) — removed too.
    The CNC router (1.303 vs 1.3) and HomeBiogas (1.26 vs 1.3) are fine.
    The sheet press runtime wrote its 0.12 m stroke raw into an inch-space
    node (0.12 in, and DOWNWARD — its "Z axis" is the lower platen on a
    jack); it now measures the gap to the fixed platen (208 mm), closes
    toward the sheet's side and carries the sheet. The beam clip shader
    used `##` comments and never compiled. Gate:
    `tools/checks/machine_scale_check.gd` (15).
  - Slicing runs on a WorkerThreadPool task (progress, a `cancel` Callable
    the slicer polls, a change mid-slice restarts it, close waits). The
    harness API (`load_stl`, `set_slicer`, `job()`) finishes pending slices
    synchronously. A fresh slice shows the whole print on the plate.
  - Diag: `tools/diag/slice_probe.gd -- --stl=<path> [--scale --line --layer
    --infill=0,20 --plan]` prints layers, the top road reached, moves, ms.

## Toroid designer (core/toroidlab/, 2026-10-26)

Library → Structures → "Toroid designer…" (no hotkey); click a placed
toroid or the prop editor's "Edit toroid…" reopens it bound to the prop.
The dome-lab pattern: pure modules under `core/toroidlab/`, the modal
`scenes/ui/toroidlab_modal.gd` (own CanvasLayer 27, `UiFit.keep_fitted`,
modal claim, SubViewport studio; it reuses DomeLab's emitters `_atri` /
`_hex` / `kind_for_look`, DomeLabSpec's formatting, DomeLabMaterials' bolts
and DomeLabCam's DXF / SVG writers). Record key `toroid_spec`, model id
`toroidlab_structure` (`ToroidLabBuilder.MODEL_ID`), library
`user://toroidlab_library.json`, exports `user://toroidlab_designs/`.
- **It is a torus.** The user's "Overview Toroid structure.glb" (in their
  Documents, not committed; inch units, SketchUp via SimLab) measured with
  `tools/diag/glb_mesh_table_diag.gd` (every mesh as a JSON row, `--verts-mat=`
  dumps a material's vertices): a least-squares circle fit of every rib tube
  gives ONE circle, r 1.825 m centred 2.205 m out and 1.352 m up, for the
  outer wall, the top AND the inner hourglass. So a design is
  `torus {major_r_m, minor_r_m, centre_h_m, base_y_m, segments}`; a point is
  (θ round the axis, φ on the minor circle from its outer equator up over the
  crown, ρ from its centre). The modal edits inner radius at the ground /
  outer radius / height and solves back (`torus_from_measures`:
  r = (H + A) − √(2AH)).
- **Ribs**: outer ground (φ = −g, the ground cut) to the inner top ring
  (−1 = 180 − g, so the arcs are equal) in `ribs.pieces` arcs (couplers);
  every `inner_every`-th rib continues down the inner wall (`inner_skip` =
  a doorway; the reference leaves ribs 17 and 19 open), with an optional
  straight post beside it.
- **Rings** sit at φ; on a rib node they take tees / crosses (5-way where
  a post joins), off a node they pass ONE OD inside the ribs on crossover
  clamps (the reference crown ring at 77° is clamped under the ribs); ring
  tubes span `piece_bays` bays; splices off a tee are couplers.
- **Bracing** = a list between ring indices (in φ order: outer ground = 0),
  pattern x / diag / zigzag, member tube (swivel clamps) or cable (eye
  clamps, a turnbuckle, thimbles), every / start.
- **Canopy** (`ToroidLabCanopy`): per bay a diamond pleat — seam A–B on the
  rib, mid-bay valley Vi, peak P, valley Vo, each at (φ, depth inside the
  rib circle) — as three triangles per half, unfolded isometrically (A at
  the origin, B on +x, flaps across A–P and P–B), a 2" flange along the
  seam standing in the rib plane, bolted back to back with the neighbour's
  (each half a sheet's thickness off the plane). Pieces turned to their
  smallest rectangle that fits the sheet; MaxRects nesting. The reference:
  692 × 2434 mm, one 4' × 8' sheet per half-bay, 48 sheets, 144 bolts —
  the user's build. ⚠ `phi_in_deg` 118.8 (measured 119.2) keeps the seam
  under 2440 mm; at 119.2 it is 2444 and nothing nests.
- **Solar**: per bay, centred mid-bay at `centre_deg`, flexible modules
  bent along the minor circle (rigid ones on the chord, with a sag warning);
  `series` × `parallel` from the spec. Placing (or Apply) seeds a graph
  array tagged `toroid_<prop_id>` (`PlacedPropService.seed_toroid_graph`;
  packed = removed; delete = removed) and
  `add_imported_solar_panels` now honours `opts.series` / `opts.parallel`
  instead of its own best guess. A full ring's mean normal is straight up,
  so the array is flat (tilt 0).
- `ToroidLabCam`: the canopy sheet layouts (one file per distinct layout),
  a full-size SVG bending template per bent class (the tube's band, the
  chord, ticks every 100 mm), tube / BOM CSVs, cut sheet, JSON.
- Not built: tube splice positions on rings longer than a stick (counted,
  not placed), the canopy's hanger hardware drawn, an NPC crew, per-panel
  azimuths on the graph (one flat array).

## Pelton wheel designer (core/peltonlab/, 2026-10-28)

Library → Structures → "Pelton wheel designer…" (Main hosts it, so it opens
on every map), the Hydro Lab's "Design Pelton wheel…" (nozzle kinds; bound
to that turbine), or the prop editor's "Edit Pelton wheel…". Modal
`scenes/ui/peltonlab_modal.gd` on Main's `PeltonLabLayer` (LAYER_MODAL + 1,
above the graph and the Lab). Model id `peltonlab_turbine`, record key
`pelton_spec`, turbine kind `designed_pelton`, graph preset "Pelton (designed
wheel)", library `user://peltonlab_library.json`, exports
`user://peltonlab_designs/`.
- **One cup for every wheel**: `assets/hydro/pelton_cup.stl` (the user's
  `pelton_turbine_bucket.stl` = "Pelton wheel bucket" by hydro, Thingiverse thing:16628, CC BY-SA, credited in CREDITS), measured into
  `PeltonLabParts.CUP`: 79.04 mm wide, splitter x = 39.52, open face +y,
  tip z 4.6 → bowl to 77 → root tab (34 mm thick along the shaft) to 114.8,
  pitch point at z = 40 (widest), 63.1 cm³. Scaled whole by `cup_width_mm`.
  `PeltonLabCup` reads the STL into the CUP frame (origin = the pitch point,
  emitted a, c, b for Godot's winding, normals smoothed below a 50° crease)
  and seats cups: runner frame shaft +Y, open face toward −t (the jet
  arrives along +t), width along −Y (the cup is symmetric, a mirror would
  flip facing). The tab is clamped between TWO side discs with axial bolts
  (two stations: M6 at full size, one: M10), a spacer ring the tab's
  thickness inside them, a flanged hub with an N-bolt pattern through it all.
- **Frames**: runner → CANONICAL (shaft +X, drive end +X, window = the −Z
  wall) → model (vertical turns +X up). The record's `spin_axis` is the
  design's ("x" / "y"); the catalog leaves it "" because it varies.
- **Physics** (`PeltonLabDesign.performance`): the PeltonPhysics operating
  point at the site (or a bound turbine's head / penstock / supply), rpm at
  x = 0.46, runaway at 2× from the gross head. Runner η = 0.78 × design-rule
  penalties (jet ratio m, B/d ≈ 3.1–3.4, Z = 15 + m/2: Thake, Nasir 2013 —
  the penalty sizes are the game's). Generator η peaks at its rated rpm (a
  log-speed parabola, an estimate); drive × bearings; capped at the rating.
  Checks: crowding (tabs touching at the bowl root / root), discs vs bolts and
  bowls, hub pattern between boss and spacer, cup pull mω²r at runaway on the
  bolts (double shear) and tabs, disc bearing, hub bolts and coupler at the
  STALL torque, shaft max-shear (bending from the stalled jet + rotor weight,
  torsion) vs 40 MPa, bearing L10, belt wrap / speed / minimum pulley,
  generator speed, runaway past its limit, open-circuit volts vs the bank.
- **Apply** (`SystemGraphView.apply_pelton_design`): `turbine_patch` writes
  turbine_kind, pelton_spec, runner_pcd_m, nozzles, turbine_efficiency (the
  runner η), generator_efficiency (drive × generator at its speed),
  max_power_w; the bound prop becomes the designed machine. HydroSource then
  makes exactly the designer's watts (selftest + harness pin). The close-up
  builds the turbine's own design (`pelton_spec` in its state, nozzles off,
  axis + tip radius from the design — the cups are a MultiMesh, so mesh
  measuring sees only the disc). "Place in world" goes through the graph's
  library placement with that preset.
- Builder nodes: Machine/Runner (cups MultiMesh + rotor; what spins),
  ShaftSpin (follows Runner), GenSpin (× the ratio, reversed for gears),
  Static, Housing, Window, Jets. Base = plates on 40 mm tube legs.
- Reused from the gantry lab: GantryLabDetail's primitives and its NEMA
  motor emitter (steppers as generators); the DXF / SVG writers from DomeLab.
- Not built: a cup-shape editor (on purpose — one cup), true belt / gear
  meshing animation beyond the ratio, flow through the housing in the close-up
  for vertical wheels, per-jet valves.

## Wind turbine designer (core/windlab/, 2026-10-28)

Library → Structures → "Wind turbine designer…" (Main hosts it, every map),
the wind node inspector's "Design wind turbine…", or the prop editor's
"Design wind turbine…" (on a designed turbine AND on the shipped `vawt` /
`small_hawt` GLBs). Modal `scenes/ui/windlab_modal.gd` on Main's
`WindLabLayer` (LAYER_MODAL + 1). Model id `windlab_turbine`, record key
`windlab_spec`, record kind `windlab`, graph preset "Wind turbine
(designed)" (type `wind`), library `user://windlab_library.json`, exports
`user://windlab_designs/`.
- **Rotors** (`WindLabParts.TYPES`): ugrinsky, savonius, lenz2 (sheet, drag /
  hybrid), darrieus_h, helical (airfoil blades on arms), hawt (propeller),
  multiblade (farm windmill). `WindLabAero.cp_model` gives Cp_max, λopt,
  the torque line and the WORST static torque `cq_start` (what decides
  starting). Drag rotors: Cq = Cq0·(1 − λ/2λopt); lift: Cp = Cp_max·x(2−x)
  with a Darrieus dead band plus the static torque fading out under it
  (`cp_at`) — without that a helical started and then hung at λ ≈ 0.
  Sources in the file: Savonius 0.19 @ λ 0.85 (Blackwell et al. SAND76-0131,
  Akwa 2012); Ugrinsky = that × 1.43 × the Sakamoto et al. 2021 tables
  (S/D table 2, L/R table 3 — a 2-D Re-1000 study, so the RELATIVE gain is
  used); Lenz2 0.19 @ 0.85 (claims 0.38, small tests 0.06–0.09); Darrieus
  0.34 × solidity / Re / tip-loss factors; propeller = Wilson–Lissaman–Walker
  with L/D at the blade's own Re; blades by Schmitz (chord, twist). Penalty
  SIZES are estimates.
- **The lawn-sign build** (`WindLabPresets.lawn_sign_spec`, measured off the
  user's `Lawn sign wind turbine.glb` in Documents — not committed; its flat
  cut pattern was SketchUp edges and SimLab dropped it): Ø 181 mm × 455.5,
  S = 0.36 D, L = 0.84 R, 72° tail; two 8 in MID discs 2 in apart clamping a
  40 mm NEMA 17's face (22 mm boss, 4 × M3 on 31 mm); the motor's SHAFT is
  in a coupler on a 24 in rod and its BODY turns with the rotor (`mount`
  "body_spins" — the check says the leads need a slip ring). Each blade
  unrolls to ~7.8 in, so the 24 in sign = 2 blades + an 8 in strip for the
  two discs; kerf 1 mm, margin 0 or the 18 in blades do not fit.
  Ugrinsky geometry (`ugrinsky_geom`): semicircle S radially from the rim
  to e = R − S, then a tail arc of radius L tangent to it with its centre
  L − e out on the far side (an S-bend), `sweep` degrees.
- **The operating point** (`WindLabDesign.op_point`): rotor torque
  Cq(λ)·½ρv²AR against G·T_gen(Gω)/η + bearings, from rest (no start if the
  cogging `start_torque_nm` beats Cq_start·q·A·R; `start_assist` takes the
  fastest stable crossing). An MPPT load picks the rotor speed that puts
  the most into the battery (`_mppt_point`, capped by what the magnets take
  at the controller's lowest voltage). `WindLabGen`: steppers K = T/(√2 I),
  phasor E² = (U + RI)² + (XI)² into a bridge (U = 4/π Vc per stepper
  phase, 2/π Vc six-pulse), current ceiling K/(pL); 3-phase from rectified
  V/rpm; brushed DC. Generator tables are cached per generator on a
  QUADRATIC rpm grid to 4 × max rpm, the same for every ratio, so ranking
  (`rank_generators`, ~0.5 s) reuses them.
- **Power curve** 0.5–30 m/s; auto cut-out at the generator's top speed or
  1.5 × its rating; the year's energy over a Rayleigh spread at the HUB's
  mean (10 m mean shear-corrected — a lawn sign at 0.84 m sees 2.6 m/s of
  a 4.5 m/s site). `best_ratio` / `drive_for_ratio` (stock GT2 / HTD tooth
  pairs, planetary ratios); a rotor without its own shaft is ranked 1 : 1.
- **Graph**: `WindTurbineSource.power_kw_from_graph_specs` returns the
  designed `power_curve_w` when a node has one (plain nodes unchanged);
  `rpm_curve` drives `WindTurbineSpin` / `HawtTracker` too, so Apply with
  "Keep its 3D model" gives a shipped GLB the designed curve.
  `SystemGraphView.open_wind_designer / apply_wind_design / place_designed_wind`.
  A placed designed turbine runs `WindLabRuntime` (gameplay/), NOT the GLB
  spin / tracker (both guarded on model id): same hub wind as the graph,
  spins `Machine/…/Rotor` at the solved rpm (display compressed past 150),
  yaws a propeller's `Yaw`, refreshes the bound node with the graph closed.
- **Making it**: parts are cut / scored (`d["parts"]`, FlatpackProfile
  rings, score lines on the FOLD layer — facet spacing 2r·acos(1 − tol/r)
  for radii under the sheet's free bend radius), nested by FlatpackNesting.
  ⚠ A corrugated sheet's flutes: along a sign's SHORT side, along a 4 × 8's
  LENGTH (`SHEET_SIZES.flutes`) — blades stand on a sign and are laid
  TURNED on a 4 × 8 (`nest.turned`; WindLabCam pre-rotates them).
  `WindLabMesh` is the ONE triangle source (mm, Z up, CCW outside) for the
  builder (mapped (x, z, −y)·0.001, winding reversed) and the STL files.
  `WindLabCam.write_all`: sheet + per-part DXF/SVG, STLs (propeller blades,
  airfoil sections, hub, a sheet blade as a solid), power-curve CSV, BOM,
  JSON, summary. "Make on a machine…" writes the STL and opens the nearest
  printer / router / gantry's print setup with it (`load_stl`).
- ⚠ The spec key goes through JSON.stringify: var_to_str kept 609.5999999 vs
  609.6 apart after a save, so a saved design missed its own cache.
- ⚠ GantryLabDetail's emitters set a UV on every vertex; `add_tris` must
  too, or SurfaceTool errors on mixed formats.
- Not built: furling / yaw dynamics, gusts and turbulence in the curve,
  blade bending stiffness, a Savonius's swept end-plate tip vortices, tower
  shadow, an NPC crew building one.

## Solar concentrator designer (core/csplab/, 2026-11-03)

Library → Structures → "Solar concentrator designer…" (Main hosts it, every
map; `Main.open_csplab({spec, prop_id})`), or the prop editor's "Design
concentrator…" on a placed one. Modal `scenes/ui/csplab_modal.gd` on Main's
`CspLabLayer` (LAYER_MODAL + 1), on the kit (DesignerShell + StudioViewport +
FormRow + Collapsible). Model id `csplab_concentrator`, record key
`csplab_spec`, record kind `csplab`, graph preset "Solar concentrator
(designed)" (processor role `csplab`, water in → steam out), library
`user://csplab_library.json`. First draft: no tour stop, no modal-audit
entry, no CAD export yet.
- **Eight types, one tracer** (`CspLabOptics`): lens (plano-convex, convex
  side up), ball lens (glass / water globe), Fresnel lens (grooves down, round
  or square), water lens (water on a sagging membrane), parabolic trough,
  parabolic dish, linear Fresnel rows, a heliostat tower field. A ray is born
  ON the optic (uniform over the aperture's projection; a field samples a
  mirror row / heliostat face) with weight = the cosine of its incidence, one
  spectral band (`CspLabParts.BANDS`, ASTM G173 direct fractions), a sun
  direction from the pillbox disc (`sun_half`) + Gaussian tracking error, and
  every loss is booked to its cause (shading, reflectance, Fresnel at each
  interface, Beer–Lambert absorption per band, groove tips/draft ESTIMATE,
  glazing, blocking, air attenuation Schmitz 2006, spill, end loss). Losses +
  captured = 1 exactly (pinned per type); the reference is DNI × aperture.
  `trace_section` is the same code with a fan of rays in the z = 0 plane
  (tower: the vertical plane through the tower along the pole).
- **Frames**: the optic frame has +Y the optical axis, +Z a line focus's
  length; mirrors at the bottom with the receiver above, lenses above the
  receiver at the origin. A field's frame is the ground (an E–W linear
  Fresnel turns it so rows run along local Z). `CspLabSite.pose(spec, s, lat)`
  is THE tracker: az-el (yaw −az then tilt), polar (hour angle about the pole,
  declination), one axis (N–S, E–W, polar: normal = the sun projected off the
  axis), fixed (tilted to the equator); sun_local = basisᵀ·s. The builder,
  the runtime, the studio and the year all read it.
- **CSP is not PV**: a concentrator lives on DNI (`CspTroughSource.dni_wm2`,
  the project's one DNI model) and takes diffuse light only through étendue,
  at most 1/C of it (`CspLabSite.heat_w`). The site year (`CspLabSite.Year`,
  stepped; hourly, every other day, WeatherService where it covers the site,
  clear sky otherwise) shows the DNI and the global light side by side.
  Efficiency at a sun: two-axis optics are their design value; one-axis,
  fixed and fields are traced at the sun quantised (2.5° / 7.5°) and cached
  on the solved design (`eff_cache`).
- **Heat** at the design DNI and working temperature: absorbed = DNI·A·
  captured·α (a cavity's apparent α/ε from Duffie & Beckman), losses =
  εσA(T⁴ − Ta⁴) + hA(T − Ta) (an evacuated envelope keeps 5 % of h),
  stagnation by HeliostatSource.stagnation_temp_k, steam with the trough's
  budget. Concentration is reported as × DNI and as suns (1 kW/m²) beside the
  thermodynamic limit 1/sin θs (line) / 1/sin²θs (point).
- **Structure** (`CspLabStructure`): members by frame (base / stage / optic)
  for each mount (az-el or polar fork pedestal, torque tube on pylons, row
  frame + A-frame receiver masts, lattice tower or monopole + heliostat
  pedestals); wind ESTIMATES after Peterka et al. 1989 (Cd 1.2 face-on, Cm
  0.25; stowed 0.3 / 0.05); post / pylon / leg stress at ×1.5, pointing sag
  and torque-tube twist against the surface error, the drive picked from
  `CspLabParts.DRIVES` by turning and holding torque, the swing radius vs the
  axis height.
  - **Built the way real ones are (polish pass 2026-11-03).** A dish:
    curved ribs + rim and mid rings behind the mirror (`_par_back`: the
    profile offset along its normal), a hub, the elevation axis BEHIND the
    vertex on a headframe over the azimuth slew drive, a screw jack, a
    quadripod to the receiver, and two counterweights on arms behind the
    axis sized so their moment equals the dish + receiver's
    (`optic_cg`, `receiver_kg`), the arm short enough to clear the ground
    pointing straight up. A lens: the tilt axis through the lens + receiver's
    centre of gravity, trunnions out to a fork, receiver legs tied by a mid
    ring. A trough: ribs at every pylon and half-way that follow the back of
    the mirror (parabola or CPC profile), rib arms out from a torque tube
    behind the vertex, purlins, bearings and the drive at the middle pylon;
    a FIXED trough's pylons run east–west along its tube (they stood across
    it). Rows: posts on footings, cranks and a link bar to one drive, A-frame
    masts with ties and longitudinal braces. Tower: X-braced lattice, a work
    platform + rail inside the tower's footprint (no shade on the light),
    heliostats on piers with a back frame (`_back_frame`).
  - Members may carry `"mat"`: "concrete" (footings: counted as
    `concrete_kg` / `concrete_m3`, never in `mass_kg`) or "counterweight"
    (`counterweight_kg`, moves with the optic, in the drive's moving mass).
    The builder groups surfaces by frame + material. The BOM lists
    "Concrete footings" with `foundation: true`; `bom_mass` (the lift
    total) leaves it out.
- **UI (polish pass 2026-11-03).** Headline tiles (useful heat, optical
  efficiency, suns, stagnation) top the right column; the left column says
  what the chosen type is for (TYPE_WHY); months by name; a ray-colour
  legend over the 3D view and in the 2D section; the 2D section zooms on the
  wheel about the pointer, drags to pan, double-click resets
  (`SectionCanvas.zoom` / `pan`, reset on a new design); the 3D view marks
  the sun (`CspLabBuilder.show_sun_marker`, the designer only); the
  Structure tab orbits to the back of the optic (`_view_from_behind`) and
  names + highlights the member under the pointer (`pick_member`: capsule
  per member in world space; `describe_member`); the scale figure stands
  beyond the subject from the camera (`_place_person`); a CPC shows
  NightHawkInLight's credit with "Watch the video" (OS.shell_open on a
  click; CREDITS.md entry `inspiration-nighthawkinlight-cpc`).
- **Optimizer** (`CspLabOptimizer`): golden-section per ticked parameter
  (`CspLabSpec.OPT_PARAMS`), two passes, fixed seed (common random numbers),
  objectives net heat / optical efficiency / mean suns / kW per m². Stepped
  in the modal's frames; Ctrl+Z undoes its answer.
- **World**: `SystemGraphView.place_designed_csp(spec)` /
  `apply_csp_design(gid, spec)`; `_tick_graph_csplab` (0.5 s) writes dni,
  thermal kW, steam and the water / steam port rates; `CspLabRuntime`
  (gameplay/, attached by PlacedPropRuntime) turns the builder to the sun
  twice a second (a field re-meshes its mirrors).
- **Compound parabolic troughs** (`CspLabCpc`, 2026-11-03, from
  NightHawkInLight's string-and-speed-square drawing). The trough's
  `optic.profile` is "parabola" | "cpc_tube" | "cpc_flat", with
  `accept_deg` (the FULL angle between the drawing's two lines, 20–40° as a
  rule of thumb), `truncate` (share of the full height cut off) and
  `receiver.gap_mm` (tube only: the wall is drawn round tube + gap; light
  through the gap is lost). The string drawing IS the math:
  - round tube (Rabl 1976): contact angle θ from the tube's bottom, string
    length ρ = rθ while it unwraps (involute, θ ≤ θa + π/2), then
    ρ = r(θ + θa + π/2 − cos(θ−θa)) / (1 + sin(θ−θa)) while the square
    moves (parabola, to 3π/2 − θa); mirror = tangent point − ρ·tangent.
    The halves meet in a cusp under the tube — the "W". Full aperture
    2πr / sin θa, so C = 1 / sin θa.
  - flat absorber (Welford & Winston): each wall a parabola, focus at the
    OPPOSITE absorber edge, axis tilted θa, f = a(1 + sin θa), up to a
    vertical tangent; aperture a / sin θa.
  - Rays enter across the aperture and may bounce several times
    (`_ray_cpc`: 2D segment hits with boxed runs, ≤ 16 bounces); a ray
    beyond ±θa turns back out ("spill"). `CspLabDesign.across(d, deg)` is
    the efficiency with the sun tilted ACROSS the trough. Diffuse sky
    reaches it through `heat_w`'s 1/C — a CPC (C ≈ 3–4) keeps a quarter of
    a cloudy sky. The 2D section draws the acceptance lines and the
    mirror's circle; "Export profile template" writes a 1:1 SVG
    (user://csplab_designs/<name>_profile.svg) to cut ribs from. Presets
    `cpc_pipe`, `cpc_flat` (fixed, tilted to the latitude — at the solstices
    a ±15° trough rightly sees nothing: re-tilt with the seasons). The
    selftest proves acceptance by tracing (everything inside ±θa lands,
    most at 25° is rejected); the faceted 120-segment wall softens the
    edge, so it is tested at 0.8 θa.
- Traps found building it: heliostats aimed at an external cylinder's AXIS
  put a fat receiver's beams under it (more receiver caught LESS) — aim at
  the skin facing each heliostat (`aim_r`); a missing `--script` file makes
  Godot open the project's main scene and run forever.
- **Fix + polish pass (2026-11-04).**
  - ⚠ **Every placed concentrator was the default dish.** The ghost and
    `PlacedPropRuntime.model_extras` never passed `csplab_spec` to
    `ModelCatalog`, so placing and Apply built from an empty spec.
    Both carry it now; the ghost also forwards `windlab_spec` / `pelton_spec`.
    The designer check asserts the built type for a dish, a trough, the
    water lens and a Fresnel field, plus Apply turning a dish into a trough.
    Before, it placed a "trough" without checking what came out.
  - **Mirrors** use `csplab_mirror.gdshader`, one copy per builder
    (`_mirror_mat`). It adds the sky gradient in the reflected direction,
    the ground and the sun's glint over the engine's reflection, because the
    world's sky radiance often left a metallic 1.0 dish black.
  - **Receiver glow** (the GLB trough's recipe): emission, OmniLights and
    additive `csp_focal_glow` cards, all driven by `set_glow_focus(f)`.
    - f = (DNI now / design DNI) × (optical efficiency at this sun / design
      efficiency).
    - `CspLabRuntime` computes it twice a second from real weather.
    - Below 4 % of the design flux the glow is off.
    - A line focus gets many small overlapping cards: spaced a card apart
      they read as pearls.
  - **The water lens is level, always.** `tracking.mode` "level" and mount
    `suspended_frame`: four posts and a top frame, the film ring hung under
    it. `resolve` forces both on a water lens and turns "level" into "fixed"
    on anything else.
    - The receiver rides a cart (frame "cart", node `ReceiverCart` /
      `ReceiverLift`) into the spot: `CspLabOptics.focus_follow` puts it on
      the chief ray from the curved vertex, at the Coddington
      least-confusion distance.
    - The stand lifts at most `FOLLOW_MAX_RISE_M`. Past
      `FOLLOW_MAX_ZENITH_DEG` (40°) the cart is parked under the lens.
    - The tracer uses the same offset (`Acc.rec_c`), so the 3D and the
      numbers agree.
    - The design point is noon at the summer solstice
      (`CspLabSite.solstice_noon_sun`).
    - At 35°N: 28 % at solstice noon, 21 % two hours either side, 3 % at the
      equinox, 0 in winter. That year line is in the checks
      (`level_lens_note`).
    - A frame lower than the focus is an error.
  - **Drives as degrees for real motors** (`CspLabActuators`, pure).
    - Channels per mount: azimuth + elevation, hour angle + declination,
      one-axis rotation, `row<k>`, `h<k>_az` / `h<k>_el`; none when fixed or
      level. They come from the same pose the builder draws, in the prop's
      own frame.
    - The record's `csplab_ha` = {enabled, mode live | always, deadband_deg,
      min_interval_s, channels: {id: {entity_id, scale, offset, invert,
      min, max}}}.
    - `CspLabRuntime` sends through HomeAssistant `call_service`:
      `input_number` / `number` set_value; `cover` / `valve` take a
      position as a percentage of the range.
    - It sends only past the deadband and the interval. In "live" mode it
      waits for `should_run_realworld_actions`.
    - UI: the designer's "Motors & Home Assistant" section
      (`scenes/ui/csplab_motors_panel.gd`). It opens by default for a
      placed tracker and offers "Name the helpers" and "Copy Home Assistant
      YAML" (input_number helpers plus an example automation).
  - Gates: selftest 234 checks, designer check 141.
- **Performance pass (2026-11-05).** Measured with
  `tools/bench/csplab_bench.gd` (ten placed concentrators, every kind).
  The mirror shader was never the cost (0.13 ms GPU for all ten); the CPU
  was.
  - **Fields turn, never re-mesh.** A tower / linear Fresnel field's mirrors
    are ONE MultiMesh of a unit heliostat (or row), and `set_sun` rewrites
    the instance transforms (`_field_transforms`, a left-handed frame is made
    right-handed by flipping the symmetric width axis). A 150-heliostat
    re-mesh was 14–34 ms on every sun move; now 0.1 ms.
    `field_mirror_transforms()` reads them back (a headless MultiMesh keeps
    none).
  - **Efficiency is traced live in chunks.** `CspLabSite.optical_eff_at(...,
    live = true)` (the runtime's glow and the graph's heat tick) never traces
    a new sun cell in one go: it queues it, `advance_live(d)` (called every
    frame by the runtimes and the graph tick) traces chunks of rays inside
    ONE budget a frame shared by every caller (`LIVE_TRACE_BUDGET_US`
    2.5 ms), and meanwhile the lookup answers with the partial estimate
    (≥ 300 rays) or the nearest angle already traced. Designer calls stay
    whole and deterministic.
  - **One efficiency table per design.** `CspLabDesign.eff_table(key_of)`:
    the builder's design, the graph's and the designer's share one table
    whatever their ray counts. The graph tick caches each node's solved
    design (`_csplab_designs`, by the spec's hash + latitude) and solves at
    the builder's ray count.
  - **One mirror material.** Every placed concentrator shares
    `CspLabBuilder.shared_mirror()`; the runtimes push the world sun with
    `push_world_sun` (change-gated, ≤ 2 Hz). The designer's studio builder
    sets `private_mirror`. The shader is no longer a full mirror (METALLIC
    0.72, a light albedo, a night floor), so it is lit like any bright
    surface and never reads black; past `detail_far` (90 m) the painted
    reflection is one flat sky colour and the glint is skipped.
  - **Glow and drives.** A line focus's glow cards are one MultiMesh (one
    draw, one material; `glow_card_count()`). Drive angles are re-derived
    only when the pose moved (`pose_serial`); Home Assistant is serviced
    once a second and sends at most `MAX_HA_SENDS` 16 calls a pass, biggest
    change first, the rest a second later.
  - Result, ten concentrators at 1440x: frame median 50.8 → 34.4 ms (the
    world's own), `csp_runtime` 11.0 → 0.2 ms avg (peak 55 → 3.7),
    `csp_graph` peak 102 → 4.7 ms; F3 sections `csp_runtime` / `csp_pose` /
    `csp_drives` / `csp_glow` / `csp_ha` / `csp_graph`.
  - Not done:
    - The graph tick ignores the prop's yaw.
    - The prop editor shows no angles.
    - An inbound HA link (a real tracker's angle driving the sim) is not
      built.

## FarmBot designer (core/farmbotlab/, 2026-11-10)

Library → Structures → "Garden robots (FarmBot)" (`Main.open_farmbotlab({spec,
prop_id})`, layer `FarmBotLabLayer`), or a placed bed's "Edit FarmBot…". A
FarmBot-style gantry robot on a raised bed of ANY size (FarmBot sells 3 × 1.5 m
Genesis and 6 × 3 m Genesis XL kits), the crops it grows, its day move by move,
and its cost against the hand work it saves. Model id `farmbot`, record key
`farmbot_spec` (record `kind` "farmbot", `plant_abs_h` = when it was planted),
graph preset "FarmBot bed (designed)" (a food `plant` of the bed's area,
`planted_abs_h` stamped so it establishes), library
`user://farmbotlab_library.json`.
- **`FarmBotSpec`**: bed (length, width, wall concrete / galvanized / timber,
  wall height), gantry (clearance over the soil, Z travel, soil Z), motion,
  tools, crops (mix of GardenCrops ids with shares, packing hex | square,
  layout rows | blocks | interleave, spacing scale, sowing section length),
  care (water mm/day + clock times, nozzle flow, weed / photo / soil every N
  days, hours), cost. Kit price = $2,500 + $250/m length + $167/m width
  (fitted to the docs' ~$3,500 Genesis / ~$4,500 XL; `kit_usd` ≥ 0 wins).
- **Motion is the firmware's, not a printer's** (`FarmBotMotion`): each axis
  runs its own trapezoid from a start speed to a top speed over a ramp
  distance (a = (vmax² − vmin²)/2·ramp), all three start together and finish
  apart (dog-leg paths), and it stops at every target. Defaults from FarmBot
  OS's hardware parameters (400 steps/s top, 50 start, 300-step ramp; 5
  steps/mm X/Y, 25 Z): 80 / 10 mm/s and 60 mm on X/Y, 16 / 2 mm/s and 12 mm on
  Z. Not GantryLabMotion (coordinated lines, junction speeds).
- **`FarmBotLayout`**: the bed is cut into sowing SECTIONS (rows across the
  bed, lanes along it, or alternating strips), each one crop packed at its
  GardenCrops spacing × scale, half a spacing in from the edges, nothing
  under the tool bay (`toolbay_rect`). Hex = offset rows 0.866 sp apart in
  whichever orientation and phase fits most, never fewer than square: a strip
