  too narrow for an extra row only loses plants to the offset, and a grower
  keeps it square (over open ground hex is +15.5 %, in a 6 × 3 m bed ~6 %).
  Sections are sown in succession over a crop's first cycle (GrowBed's rule)
  and resown each cycle (`sections_sown_on`).
- **`FarmBotJobs.day_plan(spec, layout, day, detail)`** is a day as jobs
  (watering at each time, seeding the due sections, weeding every N days =
  a camera grid then a plunge per weed, a photo survey, soil readings), each
  a list of move / dwell segments; a job starts at its hour or when the last
  ends. Tools hang in a bay along the -Z wall at the -X end (picked up by
  lowering onto them and sliding out along Y, put back the other way); the
  seeder takes one seed at a time from a trough that rides the gantry;
  watering lowers once to the canopy and dwells per plant for its share of
  the day's water at the nozzle's flow. `sample_day` / `sample_job` are pure:
  the placed robot (`FarmBotRuntime`, gameplay/) reads its pose from the
  clock every frame (day rolls at local midnight: absolute hours count from
  it), so it scrubs and skips at speed. Estimates said so: camera footprint
  400 × 300 mm, 0.4 weeds/m²/day, dwell times.
- **`FarmBotEconomics`** (all hand rates are ESTIMATES, in the file): the
  robot's side averaged over 28 steady days from day 120; the same work by
  hand (8 s a seed, 12 L/min + 3 min setup a watering, 0.5 min/m²/week
  weeding, 4 min a day looking; soil readings not counted); what it still
  needs a person for (seed refills, 30 % of the weeding = the ones in the
  crowns, upkeep h/yr); power 12 W idle + 55 W working; payback = (kit +
  assembly h × rate) / (saved h × rate − running). The bed's own cost is shown
  but left out of the payback (needed either way). Harvest is in neither.
- `FarmBotDesign.solve` (cached by key) → spec, layout, robot, money, checks
  (gantry over 3 m wide, track over 12 m, crops taller than the clearance, a
  busiest day over 16 h / 24 h, unprofitable).
- **Radial arm for the keyhole beds** (spec `kind` "radial", `keyhole` = GrowBed's
  keyhole keys + `sweep` slot | full + `arms` 1–4; Robot row in the modal). A
  pivot post in the compost basket carries a light aluminium truss arm out to
  a curved rail on the outer ring's wall, driven at its outer wheel; the
  carriage runs along the arm, Z drops to the plants. `FarmBotGeom` is the
  one machine ↔ bed mapping for both kinds: radial X = mm of ARC along the
  rail (so the outer wheel's speed is X's speed and FarmBotMotion is
  unchanged; the arm turns at v / R), Y = mm out from the post; "slot" stops
  the rail either side of the keyhole's path in (X = 0 just past it), "full"
  bridges it. The ring beds are GrowBed's exactly (`_keyhole_rings`, angles
  from +Z), so the area matches the greenhouse keyhole (192.5 m²). Layout:
  ring sectors (rows = rings by area, blocks = wedges, interleave =
  sectors dealt in turn), plants on arcs stepped by CHORD (an arc step puts
  neighbours closer than the spacing) and offset rows placed plant by plant
  clear of the row before (rows on circles of different radius do not stay
  in step). Tools hang on a ring round the post in the path inside the first
  bed; the seed trough rides the arm over the path nearest its middle.
  **Several arms** share the post and rail, each with its own tools and its
  own schedule in its sector (`FarmBotJobs.arm_range`; `day_plan` returns
  `arms` [a plan each], `windows` (each job across the arms), `busy_s` = the
  longest arm's day, `arm_s` = the arms' hours; `sample_arms`;
  `FarmBotBuilder.set_arm(i, …)` / `set_arms`). Measured: one arm on the 20 m
  keyhole (~2,500 plants) needs ~28 h a day and is flagged; the preset
  "Keyhole greenhouse (20 m dome)" uses three (9.3 h a day, 14.3 h busiest,
  photos every 2 days, weeding every 3). Arms meeting at a sector boundary
  are not simulated (the later one would wait). Price (estimates): base +
  $450 pivot + $180/m truss per arm + $35/m rail + $1,800 per extra arm.
- Perf: plants carry their machine X/Y (`mx`, `my`, set once in
  `FarmBotLayout.solve`), the serpentine sorts natively on Vector3 keys (a
  comparator lambda cost seconds), the photo grid / weeds / watering order
  are built once per day and shared by the arms, `FarmBotMotion.axis_time`
  allocates nothing. The 20 m keyhole solves in ~0.7 s (was 5.7 s).
- `FarmBotBuilder`: bed + soil, the crops as one MultiMesh per crop on the
  garden crop shader (`set_days`), tracks on the wall tops, Gantry (X) →
  CrossSlide (Y) → ZAxis, NEMA 17s from GantryLabDetail, the tool bay and
  tools, seed trough, electronics box, a spray column. `set_machine(mm, tool,
  spray)` is the one pose call; tip height = soil + (z − soil_z)/1000.
- Modal `scenes/ui/farmbotlab_modal.gd` (DesignerShell): designs gallery;
  3D / Plan tabs (the plan draws sections, plants, the bay, the gantry and the
  job's path, done in yellow); day, job (or the whole day), Play (Space),
  speed, scrub, a live line (time, act, tool, X/Y/Z); KPI tiles, checks,
  Labour and cost, the crop mix editor (crop, share, plants), every setting.
- Gates: `core/farmbotlab/farmbotlab_selftest.gd` (offline, 119),
  `tools\harness.ps1 -World w6af22bac295d -RunScript res://tools/checks/farmbotlab_designer_check.gd -Label farmbotlab`
  (48, real clicks on the gallery, Add a crop and Play; a placed bed watering
  at 07:05 on day 130 where its schedule says, scrub back, Apply; the Robot
  row to Radial, the 20 m keyhole by a click, all three arms turning on Play,
  a placed keyhole robot's three arms watering where their schedules say),
  diags
  `tools/diag/farmbot_probe.gd -- --preset=<id>` and
  `tools/diag/farmbot_look_diag.gd` (windowed, APPDATA at a scratch folder).
- Not built: harvesting, a tour stop, rows the player draws by hand, the
  robot's water taken from a graph tank (the graph's plant model bills the
  crop's water), the rotary tool's job, a modal-audit run (the entry is in
  the list).

## Greenhouse designer (core/greenhouselab/, 2026-11-13)

Plan: `plans/GREENHOUSE_PLAN.md`. Library → Designers → Greenhouses
(`scenes/ui/greenhouselab_modal.gd`, static `open(tree, {spec, prop_id})`),
the prop editor's "Edit greenhouse…" (on the house or any of its parts).
User's choices: the house and its parts are SEPARATE props mounted on it;
convert Closed Loop Ten; a lumped, physics-based climate.
- **Pure core.** `GreenhouseSpec` (record key `greenhouse_spec`; forms
  gable / lean_to / hoop / gothic / dome; local frame: length along X, width
  along Z, +Z the front, floor y 0), `GreenhouseMaterials` (glazing τ, τ
  diffuse, τ long-wave, U, cost — cited; walls, frames, fans, heaters),
  `GreenhouseFrame` (profiles, faces with their glazing / normal / area,
  ribs, vents, doors; the gothic arc through the wall top and the ridge;
  the dome through `DomeLabDesign`), `GreenhouseBeds` (auto rows / keyholes /
  the player's own, barrels, checks), `GreenhouseDesign.solve` (cached on
  `key_of`: stats, BOM, cost, packed spec), `GreenhousePresets` (8 + the
  library `user://greenhouselab_library.json`).
- **Placed: one house, its parts its own props** (`GreenhouseWorld.sync`,
  from placement through `apply_catalog_earthworks` and from Apply):
  `GreenhouseParts` makes a `grow_bed` (layout "rect" / "keyhole") or a
  `farmbot` per bed and a `grow_light_rack` per lit bed, each record
  `gh_part` + `mount_host {kind: "prop", id, local, owned: true}`
  (`PlacedPropHosts`): every move path carries them, pack / delete /
  duplicate cascade. A sunk or bermed house writes `earthworks`
  (`GreenhouseWorld.earthworks`, a ramp to the door when sunk).
- **The climate** (`GreenhouseClimate`, pure): the air solved quasi-steady
  each step (iterated for vents, transpiration, condensation); three masses
  stepped (barrels, bed soil, structure + earth); sun per glazing face
  (PvLabShading.poa, Fresnel IAM, shade cloth), skin U·A raised with wind,
  long-wave to a Berdahl–Martin sky through τ_lw, the ground at the
  Kusuda temperature (EarthTemperature), stack + wind vents (ASHRAE), fans,
  Penman–Monteith transpiration (Stanghellini resistances), soil
  evaporation, Lewis-analogy condensation. The energy ledger closes
  (selftest). `GreenhouseControl.decide` is the built-in controller
  (proportional vents, RH flush, rain / gale caps, fan + heater hysteresis,
  lamps in a photoperiod while the day's light is short); an override
  {vent, fans, heater, lights} wins, −1 hands it back. Heater and fans run
  a duty cycle inside a step (the air has no capacity to bang-bang against).
- **Crops** (`GreenhouseCrops`, pure, over `CropPhysiology`): per bed, per
  crop by share: thermal time to maturity, growth = LUE × PAR × temperature
  × VPD × canopy cover × the stand alive, frost losses, harvest capped at
  1.5 × the table yield (an estimate: a closed-canopy LUE overstates).
- **The year** (`GreenhouseYear`): `weather_table` on the main thread
  (WeatherService where it covers the site, else a synthetic year from the
  latitude — said so), `run` pure on a WorkerThreadPool task (~3 s a year
  at 1 h). The designer's **Climate** tab (`GreenhouseClimateChart`: every
  day's inside min–max over outside, hover a day) + the year's totals,
  harvest by crop and a month table; tiles "Coldest night" and
  "Harvest / yr" once it has run. Re-runs when the tab shows a changed design.
- **The graph: ONE node** (`GreenhouseGraph.definition` →
  `SystemGraphView.sync_greenhouse_system`, realized at root and made
  unique, identity `greenhouse_prop_id` + `bound_prop_id` + `gh_sig` +
  `gh_yaw` + `gh_spec`). Inside: a plant node per bed (bound to the bed's
  prop; the prop's `graph_item_id` points back), a lamp load per lit bed
  (one load past 5), fans, vent motors, an electric heater on a breaker
  panel, the water barrels (`gh_role` barrels), the roof catchment
  (`catchment_kind` "roof") into the tank, a harvest and a residue store.
  Ports: `ac_in`, `water_in`, `food_out`, `biomass_out`, and with
  `beds.feed` ("Fed beds") a nutrient store feeding every bed and a
  `nutrients_in` port. The house TRADES with what is wired to its ports
  (`ResourceFlowEngine._gh_exchange`, each step): its tank and nutrient
  store are topped up to 60 % from the wired sources, its harvest crate and
  residue bin emptied into the wired stores — a plain wire between two
  tanks moves nothing unless the source is `jit_outflow`. A design change
  rebuilds it keeping its spot, its outside wires and its stores' levels.
  Not a power island: its loads draw the site's AC.
- **The engine** (`ResourceFlowEngine._process_greenhouse`, before every
  other item): steps the climate by the clock (a scrub back holds, a jump
  past 6 h restarts it from the outside air; packed = nothing), writes the
  loads' `requested_state` from the controller (so the AC the site pays
  follows), stamps `gh_*` on the compound (`gh_t_air`, `gh_rh`, `gh_t_out`,
  `gh_vent_pct`, `gh_fans`, `gh_heater`, `gh_lights`, `gh_dli`,
  `gh_t_water`, `gh_cond_lph`, `gh_power_w`, `gh_frost`, `gh_power_ok`),
  and `_process_plant` grows a bed with `gh_bed` from the INSIDE light
  (sun through the glazing, + lamps over a lit bed) and its crops'
  temperature × VPD response in place of the outdoor season. State in
  `internal_state_snapshot` (`gh_state`, `gh_climate`, `gh_last_h`).
  A load's `gh_manual` ("on" / "off", inspector "Greenhouse control") takes
  it from the controller. Automations read `greenhouse.<id|name>.temp /
  .rh / .dli / .vent / .water_temp` and the state `.frost`.
- **Roofs catch rain with no Rain wire**: `_process_catchment` treats
  `catchment_kind` "roof", any `structure_water` catchment (an Earthship's)
  and a greenhouse roof as direct, like a pond's surface. Before, a
  structure's roof caught nothing without a Rain-PBI wire.
- **World** (`GreenhouseRuntime`, gameplay/, on the house): vents ease to
  the node's share, fans spin while they run, the lamp racks in it glow
  with the lamps, the glazing mists with condensation, a label over the
  door ("27 °C · 68 % · vents 40 %"); rests with no node.
- **Closed Loop Ten** (`tools/fixes/closed_loop_greenhouses.gd`): each
  dome-over-bed pair → a `dome_20m` greenhouse at the dome's pose, the
  plant's wires and planting hour carried over, chores re-pointed, 40 %
  shade cloth May–September and NO fans (2 × 560 W in twelve domes is more
  than the site's array carries).
- Gates: `greenhouselab_selftest` (89), `greenhouse_climate_selftest` (26),
  `greenhouse_year_selftest` (17), `greenhouse_graph_selftest` (16),
  `placed_prop_hosts_selftest`, `crop_physiology_selftest`;
  `tools\harness.ps1 -World mtvernon -RunScript res://tools/checks/greenhouse_designer_check.gd -Label greenhouse -Timeout 1200`
  (REAL clicks on the Plan, the Climate tab's year, placed parts following
  every move path, pack, a sunk walipini, delete) and
  `tools\harness.ps1 -World mtvernon -RunScript res://tools/checks/greenhouse_world_check.gd -Label greenhouse_world -Timeout 1200`
  (one node with its parts bound both ways, the climate on the clock, the
  loads following the controller, the card, the runtime, move / pack /
  delete); tour stop `18o_greenhouse`; modal audit `greenhouselab`; look
  sheet `tools/diag/greenhouse_look_diag.gd`.
- Not built: a bed's drawn crops following the climate's development
  (GrowBed still draws from its planting hour), crop frost in the live
  engine (the year preview has it), propane on the graph, the simkit /
  bombay_ten `with_greenhouse`.

## Tri-clamp designer (core/tclab/, 2026-11-06)

Library → Structures → "Tri-clamp designer…" (Main hosts it, every map:
`Main.open_tclab({spec})`, layer `TcLabLayer`). Plan:
`plans/TRICLAMP_DESIGNER_PLAN.md`; all 8 phases landed (standards, parts,
assembly, the modal, specialty fittings, vessels, the biochar reactor +
condenser preset, the world, performance).
- **`TcStandards`**: ASME BPE inch sizes ½"–8", every number in mm with
  its source: tube OD / ID / flange OD from a sanitary sizing guide, 2CMP
  elbow and 7MP tee centre-to-face from catalogue tables (the tee's citing
  BPE DT-4.1.2). The ferrule profile, 45° elbow, reducer length, clamp
  ratings and gasket temperatures are flagged estimates (`estimates()`,
  printed by the selftest). 1" and 1½" share the 1.984" clamp face; ½" and
  ¾" the mini (`clamp_class`).
- **`TcGeom`** (mm, pure): lathe (profiles walked with the solid on the
  left, outward normal = (dz, −dr)), swept tubes, saddle-cut tee branches,
  boxes / cylinders / hex, the ferrule end (face + gasket groove, rim, 20°
  taper, hub, bore), gasket, hinged clamp, NPT thread. `tri` fixes the
  winding from the intended normal, so every emitter is front-face
  correct. ⚠ The accumulator holds the current material's PackedVector3Arrays
  in members (`_sel` / `_flush`): appending to one fetched from a Dictionary
  copies the whole array every triangle.
- **`TcParts`**: 38 types in 11 categories; the base 15 (spool, 90° / 45° / any-angle bend, tee, reducing
  tee, cross, 45° lateral, weld ferrule, cap, cap × FNPT, flat reducing cap,
  concentric reducer, TC × MNPT, TC × barb), `build(type, size, params)` →
  geo, ports {id, kind tc | weld | npt_m | npt_f | barb, size, pos, z out, x
  roll ref}, body capsules (picking, clash), mass, bore volume; cached by
  key. `can_mate` is the one compatibility rule; a clamp joint adds the
  gasket gap.
- **`TcAssembly`** (pure): child port frame = parent port frame · T(gap) ·
  Rx(180°) · Rz(roll) — symmetric, so joints are undirected. One root (`xf`)
  per connected group; BFS places the rest; a joint met twice CLOSES a loop
  and reports its error. A spool with `fit` solves its length numerically to
  close the loops it is in. Edits are pure (`add_part`, `remove_part`,
  `detach`, `attach`, `set_root_xf`, `set_joint`, `set_part`) and end in
  `pin_roots` (exactly one root per group, where the last solve had it).
  `pick` = ray vs capsules, open-port and joint spheres (ports win within
  25 mm). `clashes` = capsule pairs not mated directly.
- **`TcDesign.solve`** (LRU on `TcSpec.key_of`) → spec, res, bom, clashes,
  checks ({level, text, why, ids}), stats. **`TcBuilder`**: a MeshInstance3D
  per part sharing one ArrayMesh per part key, one per clamp joint
  (gasket + clamp), overlays for selection / clashes; `flat` merges all
  (exports). **`TcExport`**: GLB (`GLTFDocument`), binary STL (mm), BOM CSV,
  JSON → `user://tclab_designs/<name>/`. **`TcPresets`**: 8 built-ins
  + `user://tclab_library.json`.
- **Modal** (`scenes/ui/tclab_modal.gd`, DesignerShell + StudioViewport +
  FormRow): clamp-size chips + palette left; click an open end (or the
  floor) to place, Tab = which end of the new part joins, R = roll (or yaw on
  the floor), Shift-click keeps the tool; click selects a part / clamp / open
  end; dragging a part detaches it and carries what hangs off it, dropping on
  an open end joins it (a short drag snaps back); cards for part (size,
  params, roll, detach, remove), joint (roll, gasket, clamp, rating) and open
  end (label + resource kind for the later graph link). No scale person (a
  1.75 m capsule dwarfs fittings) and its own `_frame` (the kit's
  `frame_sphere` adds a metre of air).
- **Specialty fittings** (`TcSpecialty`, Phase 4): sight glass, column
  section, bubble plate, dephlegmator (water jacket, two ½" FNPT bosses),
  butterfly / ball (2- and 3-way) / check / diaphragm / relief valves,
  pneumatic + electric actuators, dial thermometer, pressure gauge,
  thermowell, in-line and Y strainers, cartridge housing, strainer basket,
  funnel, spray ball, TC heating element. Bodies are drawn to the reference
  GLB's look (flagged estimates). A valve has a `stem` port and an
  actuator mounts on it (`can_mate`: stem ↔ stem). `manual` false drops
  the handle. Short-pattern elbows / tees (`short`: half OD + hub + 6 mm,
  an estimate) are what the reactor's compact condenser needs.
- **Vessels** (`TcVessel`, type `vessel`, Phase 5): Y up, origin at the
  shell's bottom seam; heads flat / ellipsoidal 2:1 / torispherical / cone
  / open, a separate lid (dished, flat) with its clamp ring, jacket (none /
  full / lower, gap), insulation, legs, internals (retort can, basket, false
  bottom, coil), PRESETS (jacketed boiler, brew kettle, conical, pot still,
  storage). Nozzles are params (`ports`: {id, kind tc | npt | weld, size,
  face shell | top | lid | bottom, angle_deg (0 = +Z, 90 = +X), h_mm /
  r_mm, tilt, stub_mm}); `nozzle_frame` places each on the outside skin
  (`r_eff`: jacket / insulation), `surface_hit` turns a ray into a new
  angle + height (or radius on a head). The modal's vessel card edits it
  all; a nozzle is selected by clicking its face and DRAGGED round the
  vessel; `Cutaway` cuts a quarter out (the builder rebuilds the vessel
  with `cutaway`, never stored). The solid shell counts in `clashes`.
- **The biochar reactor preset** (`TcPresets`, Phase 6, built-in
  `biochar_reactor`, plus `tc_condenser`, `pot_still`, `brew_kettle`,
  `filter_train`): Ø340 × 650 shell, full jacket → Ø396, 516 mm dished lid,
  retort can, element, butterfly drain, six ½" bungs, and on the back a
  3-column 2" condenser (standard tee on the vapour nozzle, short elbows,
  two 18" dephlegmators and a 346 mm gas column, short tees, a centre tee
  closing the loop, TC × ½" MNPT drains, "Woodgas out" labelled). Parts go
  on with `_attach`, which picks the roll (15° steps) that points named
  ports where they must face. `tools/diag/tclab_reactor_parity.gd` holds it
  to the GLB: every nozzle 1–6 mm from the model's collars except the
  vapour nozzle, raised 21 mm because the catalogue's tee and elbows are
  larger than the model's; columns at −140 / 0 / +140 mm (model −124 / −4 /
  +118).
- **In the world (Phase 7).** Catalog ids `tclab_assembly` (record key
  `tc_spec`) and `tclab_<builtin>` (biochar_reactor, pot_still,
  brew_kettle, filter_train; a record with no tc_spec builds its id's
  built-in, `TcBuilder.handles` / `spec_for_model`). `tc_spec` is forwarded
  by `PlacedPropRuntime.model_extras` and the placement ghost (the CSP
  "always the default" trap). The designer: **Place in world** /
  **Place a copy**, **Apply to placed assembly** (opened with
  `{prop_id}` from the prop editor's "Edit tri-clamp assembly…").
  - The placed node stands on y = 0 with its plan centre on the origin
    (`TcDesign.world_offset`, shared by the builder, the ports and the
    crew pieces).
  - **Graph binding**: `spec.binds` names a processor preset (the
    designer's "On the graph" row); `PlacedPropService.seed_tclab` (from
    BOTH `_commit_prepped` and `place_model_at_xz`) stamps the design and
    makes that node bound to the prop once. `TcDesign.graph_handles` maps
    each labelled end's "carries" kind to the preset's first unused output
    of that kind, else input (`res_out_<i>` / `res_in_<i>`). The graph's
    **Biochar Reactor preset now places `tclab_biochar_reactor`** (the
    plan's decision 7 once parity passed; the static drum GLB stays as
    `biochar_reactor`). Its feed → biomass in, woodgas out → woodgas out,
    the condenser's warm cooling water → hot water; the char has no pipe.
  - **Connection ports**: every labelled open end
    (`TcDesign.connection_ports`, read by `ConnectionPortDefs` for a record
    with tc_spec or a tclab id), so a 3D conduit from a node handle ends on
    the real fitting.
  - **Packing**: `TcDesign.packed_spec` = PackKitter over the parts (the
    vessel and each fitting a piece, long spools sticks, clamps + gaskets
    loose at `clamp_kg`, an estimate). PackedSpec DYNAMIC fallbacks.
  - **Crew build**: `pieces` builds one tagged MeshInstance3D per part
    (vessel "frames" order 0, fittings "parts" by joint depth from it,
    clamps tagged and riding with them).
  - Tour stop `18k_tclab`; modal audit entry `tclab`.
- **Performance (Phase 8).** A placed assembly is two merged meshes, one
  surface per material: "Mesh" to `FAR_M` 40 m (skip_prop_collision) and
  "MeshFar" beyond, every part at `FAR_SEG_SCALE` 0.3 of its segments and
  no clamps — also the collision. Cached per design key
  (`TcBuilder.world_meshes`, `WORLD_CACHE_MAX` 16), so placed copies share
  them. `TcGeom.seg_scale` drives the far parts (TcParts caches them
  apart); rigid `merge` and `geo_to_mesh` transform whole arrays; joint
  gasket + clamp geometry is cached. The spec resolve builds a port map
  once and the clash test sweeps and prunes along x. Measured
  (`tclab_bench`): the reactor 68k triangles near, 19k far, first world
  build 33 ms; a 200-part manifold solves cold in ~23 ms, a drag solve in
  ~11 ms (was 45 / 30), its first world build 127 ms (cached after: 7 ms).
  Ten placed reactors in view: +10 draw calls, ~1.4 ms a frame on Mount
  Vernon. The studio keeps one MeshInstance3D per part / joint (meshes
  shared by part key) for selection overlays: a MultiMesh of clamps was
  not needed once the world merges everything.
- Capsules for the clash test are shortened by their radius at each end
  (`TcAssembly.clashes`): with round caps, a spool's end reached into an
  elbow two joints away and the reactor reported a clash that was not there.
- Found on the way: `DesignerShell`'s mode chip collapsed to a dot whenever
  there were no breadcrumbs (an ellipsized label has no minimum width and
  the empty crumb row expanded); `_sync_strip` now expands the chip.
  `StructureMaterials.Kind` gained `STAINLESS` and `RUBBER` (appended).

## TC Process Lab (core/tclab/process/, 2026-11-06)

Plan: `plans/TC_PROCESS_LAB_PLAN.md` (9 phases; the user chose process
units in TC Lab for the downstream chain, the detailed model in the LAB ONLY
with a fitted summary on the graph, automations on the design, and a default
batch of ~10 kg chips at 20 % moisture on two 600 W bottom elements).
Landed: all 9 phases (the network, the species / thermo / reaction
library, the stepper, Process mode, seeing inside, control, the molecule
lens, the summary on the graph, process units, scenarios + tour). An educational process model, not a
chemistry engine.
- **`TcFlowPaths`**: per part type, which ports share a fluid volume
  (`TYPE_RULES`; a type missing there fails the selftest). Roles: VOLUME
  (pipe, junction, vessel, jacket, condenser, coolant, column, plate, sight,
  filter), LINK (valve, check, relief), ATTACH (blind, probes, heater,
  basket, spray, feed). A dephlegmator is two circuits (product a↔b,
  coolant w1↔w2); every vessel nozzle opens into one volume.
- **`TcProcNet.build(d)`** (cached by the geometry key): control volumes
  (consecutive 2-port pipes merge), links (joints; valves / checks /
  reliefs as links), thermal links (condenser ↔ its coolant, vessel ↔
  jacket) and boundaries by role: feed, product, drain, coolant_in / out,
  outlet, atmosphere (an open clamp end), plug (a spare threaded bung on a
  vessel). Positions stay in the assembly's mm frame.
- **`TcSpecies` / `TcThermo` / `TcReactions`**: rows with sources
  (Antoine, NIST cp at 500 K, LHVs, JANAF hot cp for flame T), Miller &
  Bellan 1997 three-component wood pyrolysis (`wood_step`: exact
  exponential decay, stable at any dt), Liden tar cracking, a 15 % acid
  share of primary tar (wood vinegar, estimate), plastics as one global
  step (estimates), O2-limited combustion, silica gel, filter captures.
  `WaterSteam` (power_system/sources/) is the shared boil-off budget the CSP
  sources now use too.
- **`TcBed`**: the charge, one domain per element (equal volumes; one
  element on the axis = the whole vessel), NR 8 rings × NZ 6 layers. Heat
  into the inner ring over the element's reach; conduction is IMPLICIT
  (backward Euler by Gauss–Seidel, fluxes from the solved T applied
  pairwise: stable and energy-exact at 30 s); k = 0.12 + 4εσdT³. Columns
  are walked bottom-up with a PACKET: steam condenses in cells still below
  the boiling point (the heat pipe that runs the drying front ahead), hot
  gas trades heat with each cell. Element T = contact + radiation h.
- **`TcProcSim`**: dt 5 s, the bed every 6th step (its output released
  evenly between). Pools boil at the bubble point (Raoult, Wilson γ);
  walls: gas ↔ wall, condenser wall ↔ coolant (the water's own energy
  balance), wall → room through the jacket gap (`jacket_fill` air |
  insulation; the reactor default is insulation: an air gap loses two
  thirds of 1.2 kW at 200 °C) or insulation; condensation / evaporation
  toward the wall's saturation pressure; tar cracking above 650 K; the
  pressure network solved EXACTLY each step (dense elimination over the gas
  CVs — ⚠ Gauss–Seidel never settles a chain of tiny pipe volumes and piled
  gas up mid-chain at 400 bar), species and enthalpy upwind as mixing cells
  in falling-pressure order; liquids run to the lowest potential (a drain
  pulls a level header toward it). Pipework traps drip into a jar by
  default; a labelled liquid nozzle ON A VESSEL starts shut (a kettle
  drained itself through its whirlpool return). Elements have a 900 °C
  high-limit that resets 150 K lower.
  - Ledgers: `energy_ledger()` (in = stored sensible + latent + loss +
    coolant + reaction + out; the latent of condensables formed straight
    from the solid, reaction water included, is booked against the
    reaction) and `mass_ledger()`. The batch closes to 0.1 % / 0.0000 kg.
  - `snapshot` / `restore` / `seek(t)` (keyframes every 120 s),
    `readings()`, `cv_state(i)`, `set_actuator("heater:<pid>" |
    "valve:<pid>" | "cooling[:<cv>]" | "drain:<ref>", v)`, events,
    `TcProcSim.prof` (section µs).
  - The default batch (selftest): dry at 2.6 h, all char at 3.4 h, char
    35 % of dry wood, ~3.5 kg condensate out of the traps + 1 kg held,
    woodgas ~7–13 MJ/Nm³, almost no N2. ~0.7 ms a step (10 h ≈ 5 s
    headless): the bed is packed arrays per domain — local copies written
    back after the loop (copy-on-write: a write through `d["cel"][i]`
    lands on a copy).
- The `biochar_reactor` preset was rebuilt to the user's real reactor: two
  2" elements up through the bottom (r 80 mm; the second added LAST so the
  condenser keeps p9–p20), no retort can, 160 mm legs, and a `process`
  block (`TcProcSpec`, kept by `TcSpec.resolve`, left out of `key_of` so a
  process edit never re-solves the geometry). `tclab_reactor_parity` lists
  the moved element as KNOWN.
- **Process mode** (Phase 3): the designer's studio strip has Design /
  Process buttons (`tclab_modal.set_run_mode`, `scenes/ui/
  tclab_process_panel.gd`, a Node child of the modal). Process swaps the
  side columns (`design_left/right` ↔ `process_left/right`), keeps the
  studio (orbit + click only) and adds a transport under it. Left: the
  scenario (load, mass, moisture, each element's watts, cooling water,
  jacket gap, room, relief, back-pressure, batch length), written through
  `set_process_block` (undoable, never re-solves the geometry). Right:
  tiles, the clicked volume's composition, a stacked chart
  (`tclab_process_chart.gd`, click / drag scrubs), the event log
  (`run_events`, kept across seeks), where the heat went. The lab clock
  is its own (`_process`, 6 ms a frame, speeds 1×–600×; the world clock
  is untouched); "Run the whole batch" steps to the end at 12 ms a frame
  (16 s in game for 10 h), then scrubs by `seek`. Parts are tinted by
  their volume's temperature (`material_overlay`). Space plays, F frames.
  ⚠ Don't name a method `set_process` / `set_process_mode` on a Node.
  Gate: `tools\harness.ps1 -World mtvernon -RunScript
  res://tools/checks/tc_process_check.gd -Label tc_process` (30, REAL
  clicks: mode swap, play / pause, pre-run, chart scrub to 1 h and 3 h, a
  condenser clicked, the vessel tinted, watts edited, UiAudit 0 errors).
- **Seeing inside** (Phase 4, `scenes/ui/tclab_process_view.gd`, a sibling
  of the builder under the studio holder; shaders in
  `core/tclab/process/shaders/`). The view bar under the transport: Look
  Solid / Section / X-ray, the cut (Facing me — follows the camera, through
  the clicked volume — / Left-right / Front-back), an offset slider,
  Contents.
  - Section: every part surface gets `tc_section.gdshader` by its MATERIAL
    KEY (`TcBuilder.geo_to_mesh` now names each surface by its key); the far
    side of one world plane is discarded and back faces seen through the cut
    are painted as the cut face (the cap trick). Glass gets the ghost.
    X-ray: `tc_xray.gdshader` (fresnel ghost, no cut). Solid: overrides
    cleared, the panel's overlay tint as before. Temperature tint and an
    element's glow are INSTANCE uniforms (`tint`, `glow`) in section / X-ray.
  - Contents: a tube along each CV's centre line (gas: `tc_gas.gdshader`,
    colour from what is not air, drifting the way the CV's outflow links
    point; liquid: `tc_liquid.gdshader`, the same tube below its level);
    the vessel's headspace gas and pool; the charge as a cylinder whose
    back faces take the colour where the view ray crosses the cut plane
    (`tc_bed.gdshader` reads an NR × NZ·domains texture of the cells:
    wet, dry, pyrolysing, char, glow above ~420 °C) — the cut face is the
    bed's real cross-section. Pooled particles: vapour off the charge,
    bubbles in a boiling pool, the outlet plume, drips in the three volumes
    condensing most (from the liquid's rise over lab time).
  - Motion runs on the lab clock (stops when paused, sqrt of the speed).
  - The modal hides its open-end markers in Process mode.
- **Control** (Phase 5b, `TcProcControl`, the panel's Readings / Control
  tabs on the right):
  - Every design gets Home Assistant-shaped entities, prefixed by its
    name as a slug (`biochar_reactor_condenser`):
    - sensors: the charge (max / mean T, water left, char), the vessel
      gas T and pressure, each element's T, every thermometer / gauge /
      thermowell part, sight-glass and trap levels, cooling water out, gas
      out, LHV, condensate, energy in, plus probes the player drops on the
      selected volume (`process.sensors`);
    - switches: each element, every element, valves, cooling, drains;
    - numbers: element watts, cooling flow.
  - `process.automations` are the inspector's WHEN / IF / THEN cards (the
    shared `automation_card_editor.gd`, `auto_rebuild`) and run INSIDE the
    model: `TcProcSim._run_automations` steps an `AutomationSim`
    (rich_commands) every `AUTO_EVERY_S` 30 lab seconds on the lab clock
    (absolute hours from `process.start_hour`, so a 9:00 rule fires an
    hour into an 8:00 batch), reading only the entities the rules name.
    Its state is in the keyframes (`AutomationSim.snapshot / restore`), so
    a seek replays the same switches.
  - A rule's untargeted switch action switches every element. Each action
    is an event ("auto"); the list folds a run of them into one row.
  - Switches / numbers by hand apply from now and cut the computed run
    there. "Copy as Home Assistant YAML" (`TcProcControl.ha_yaml`) also
    saves `user://tclab_designs/<slug>_automations.yaml`.
  - Presets (`TcProcControl.templates`): hold the charge near 450 °C (off
    at once above 450, on after a minute below 400 — a narrow band
    switched every minute: the hottest point is next to an element), stop
    when the gas stops, empty a trap at 80 %, more cooling water when it
    runs hot.
  - ⚠ `TcDesign.solve` is cached on the GEOMETRY key, which leaves the
    process block out, so the cached design's own `spec` carried an OLDER
    process: until 2026-11-06 Process-mode edits (watts, rules) never
    reached the run. The modal's `_solve` returns a shallow copy carrying
    the live spec.
- **Molecule lens** (Phase 6, the view bar's "Molecules"):
  - `scenes/ui/tclab_molecule_lens.gd` is a picture-in-picture over the
    studio's top-right corner. It is a top-level PanelContainer on the
    modal with its own SubViewport (own_world_3d), and is freed while
    off.
  - Contents, read off the selected volume:
    - ~30 gas molecules sampled by mole fraction
      (`TcMolecules.sample_counts`), flying at `display_speed` ∝ √(T/M),
      bouncing elastically off the box and each other;
    - the liquid, as a layer at the bottom;
    - for the vessel, the charge: glucose units turning to carbon
      hexagons as it chars, with water in the wood.
  - The model's `react_rate` (drying, boiling, condensing, pyrolysis /
    charring, cracking, burning) plays storyboards at a rate following
    its own (log scale). The reactants' atoms move into the products,
    matched by element, and the bonds stretch and re-form.
  - `TcMolecules` (pure) holds layouts in Å, adding what TcSpecies leaves
    out: levoglucosan's 10 H, the glucose unit, the char hexagon, CH2
    chains. Every `STORY` balances atom for atom (selftest).
  - Motion is on the lab clock (frozen while paused). It follows the
    selected volume.
- **Into the world** (Phase 7, "Use this run on the graph" under Readings):
  - `TcProcSummary.fit` turns a finished run into a ProcessRecipe for the
    flow engine's existing scrub-safe batch path, so the engine needs no
    new code. The panel runs the whole batch first if needed.
  - What the recipe carries:
    - in: the charge, frontloaded;
    - `watts`: the run's mean draw;
    - out: biochar at the end, the cooling water through the batch, and
      woodgas (dry Nm³), wood vinegar (L) and tar (kg), each over the
      window it really came out;
    - the phase changes as chore-less steps;
    - `gas_lhv_mj_nm3` + `gas_composition` (dry).
  - Outputs keep the bound node's PORT ORDER, so wires stay on their
    handles. New kinds are appended.
  - It lives on the design as `process.recipe` (`TcProcSpec`; editing it
    does not restart the run, see `_same_run`).
    `PlacedPropService._stamp_tc_recipe` writes it onto the node when a
    reactor is placed, on Apply, and at once when the designer was
    opened on a placed reactor (`write_recipe_to_bound` →
    `apply_tclab_recipe`).
  - Rules with time / sun triggers that switch the whole machine are
    copied to `graph_automations` (ids `tc_…`). Rules reading lab
    sensors stay in the lab and are listed in the note.
  - New ResourceKinds `wood_vinegar` (L) and `tar` (kg). The Biochar
    Reactor preset appends both outputs (indices 3, 4), and the reactor's
    condensate drains carry `wood_vinegar`.
  - `ResourceFlowEngine._fuel_wh_per_unit`: a generator's
    `energy_wh_per_unit` scales by the wired gas's
    `gas_lhv_mj_nm3` ÷ 5 MJ/Nm³ (the producer gas the preset assumed),
    looking through one tank. The default batch fits 4.0 h at 1.2 kW:
    2.8 kg char, 0.9 Nm³ at 7.4 MJ/Nm³, 2.2 L vinegar, 2.3 kg tar.
- **Process units + the whole chain** (Phase 8, `TcUnits`, palette
  category "Process units"): `gas_holder` (a water-sealed bell, `volume_l`,
  `hold_kpa`), `dryer` (a column of silica gel or activated carbon),
  `genset` (48 V DC, `rated_kw`, `efficiency`, one clamp inlet), `flare`.
  Each part's circuit carries a `unit` dict through TcFlowPaths → the CV.
  In `TcProcSim` (`_setup_units`, `_unit_step`, `units`):
  - A bell between empty (`HOLDER_MIN` 4 %) and full has its row PINNED at
    its weight's pressure in the implicit solve, and its volume follows its
    gas after it (`_holder_volumes`, before and after the flow step). It
    starts empty (air at the minimum volume). Full, it is a rigid tank; past
    `SEAL_BLOW_PA` over its weight it blows off to air through its seal.
  - A genset is a SINK in the pressure solve, never a post-step removal:
    its intake is 0.6 L, so emptying it after the solve capped it at a few
    mmol a step. Demand = rating ÷ efficiency ÷ the LHV of the gas it is
    FED (the richest CV within `ENGINE_FEED_HOPS` up its line — a fresh
    intake is full of air until the engine draws it through); it will not
    fire under `ENGINE_MIN_LHV` (2.5 MJ/Nm³). If the demand would pull the
    intake below 1 atm − `ENGINE_MIN_PA`, the row is pinned there and it
    gets what comes. The draw is booked in the mixing sweep (burned_mol,
    heat + latent to e_out); kW = draw × the mixed gas's LHV × efficiency.
  - A dryer takes 85 % of the water vapour below 80 °C up to its sorbent's
    capacity (`SORBENT_CAPACITY`, estimates); the latent stays in the gas.
  - Engines start off (`proc.engines[pid].on`); `set_actuator("engine:<pid>")`.
  - TcProcControl adds `<holder>_level` %, `<dryer>_saturation` %,
    `<genset>_power` kW, `electricity` kWh, the genset switch, and the
    preset "Run the genset from the gas holder" (on at 60 %, off at 15 %).
  - Built-in `biochar_genset` ("Biochar reactor → genset", catalog
    `tclab_biochar_genset`): the reactor's gas line down to `GAS_LINE_Y`,
    300 L holder, silica dryer, 2.5 kW genset (since 2026-11-08 the 30 gal
    barrel gasometer and the 350–750 W generator, see the improvement pass),
    the two rules (units are
    stood upright with `_attach`'s `["@up", Vector3.UP]` want — scoring
    ports alone laid them on their sides). Measured
    (`tools/diag/tc_chain_probe.gd`): the bell fills to ~40–60 % and the
    genset runs at ~2.4 kW for a few minutes a cycle, 0.44 kWh over 8 h —
    the batch's ~0.9 Nm³ of gas × 22 %.
  - Graph: `spec.part_binds` [[pid, "holder" | "genset" | preset label]]
    (TcSpec keeps it). `PlacedPropService._seed_tc_units` makes one node
    per bound part beside the main one (`TcDesign.unit_node`: a woodgas
    tank of the bell's m³; a Woodgas DC Generator at the reference gas ×
    efficiency Wh/m³ and its rating), all bound to the same prop, in a row,
    wired in order by kind (`_wire_by_kind`); `graph_item_ids` on the
    record. Deleting the prop removes them all. Not a compound (a grouped
    compound only exposes ports for wires already crossing it).
- **Scenarios** (Phase 9): each built-in carries its own process block
  (`TcProcSpec.pot_still_default` / `kettle_default` / `plastic_default`).
  - Pot still: 20 L of a 10 % wash on 2 kW boils at 92 °C (the Wilson VLE
    bubble point) and makes ~2 kg of ~29 % ABV spirit in 3 h at the product
    end; the first condenser runs hot and refluxes.
  - Brew kettle: 40 L on 3 kW, boils at ~1.4 h and off through the lid vent
    (a vent labelled with a gas kind counts as product, not vented).
  - `plastic_retort` (no graph node, `binds` ""): 8 kg of PP pellets on the
    reactor. Pellets MELT (`TcBed.MELT_K` PE 130 °C / PP 165 °C), then the
    melt conducts at `K_MELT` and wets the element (`H_MELT`); it cracks into
    light gas + ~5 kg of oil and wax in 8 h, no char.
  - The filter train has no vessel: Process mode says so.
- Stepper fixes that came with them (each a trap):
  - **A plastic cell that cracks out has no char to hold its heat**: the
    cracking heat drove it to −10⁶ K and NaN'd the run. Conversion is
    limited to what the cell can pay above `MIN_REACT_K`, and `_cap` has a
    `CAP_FLOOR` (5 J/K).
  - **Condensers only condensed what stood in them between steps**; a 2 kW
    boil passes through ten times a step and walked straight out.
    `_condense_stream` condenses the stream in the mixing sweep (role
    "condenser" CVs): what can stay vapour is set by the inerts,
    n_s = n_inert · y_s / (1 − Σy), and the transfer coefficient rises as the
    inert share falls (`K_MASS / x_inert`, ≤ 1 m/s): pure vapour condenses
    as fast as the wall takes the heat. `H_COOLANT` 600 → 1200 W/m²·K.
  - An outlet / product boundary lets the LIQUID that reaches it run out
    (the distillate, counted in `drained_by`) — never from a vessel CV.
  - Solid-feed kinds (`TcProcNet.FEED_KINDS`: biomass, plastic_waste,
    plastic_flake) are closed feed ports; a crown labelled plastic_waste was
    an open vent and the oil and wax left through the lid.
  - Bed events are feed-aware (melt / cracking / "all the plastic has
    cracked"); "burnable gas at the outlet" counts C3H6.
- Tour stop `18l_tc_process` (the reactor pre-run, cut open at 2 h, the
  molecule lens, the Control tab); modal audit entry `tc_process`; bench
  `tools/bench/tc_proc_bench.gd` (per built-in: CVs, links, ms/step, the
  pre-run time, section costs; 1 s steps; snapshot / seek).

- **Improvement pass (2026-11-08).**
  - **The vapour is contained.** The vessel's vapour puffs draw through
    `tc_smoke.gdshader` (billboard in the vertex stage; every fragment
    outside the vessel's inside cylinder + lid dome, in the vessel's frame,
    is discarded, with a soft fade toward the wall). The outlet "Plume" is a
    short jet out of the pipe end with no buoyancy: it used to rise over the
    reactor and read as smoke through the lid. Emitters whose source stopped
    are hidden while paused.
  - **The charge cools and settles.** `TcBed.volume_frac()` (display and
    readings only; the heat grid keeps its loaded geometry): wood loses
    `DRY_SHRINK` 6 % drying and `CHAR_SHRINK` 45 % charring (estimates inside
    published 40–60 %), plastic slumps and cracks away. The charge mesh is
    one unit high (`charge_mesh`, a ringed top the shader heaps) and
    `tc_bed.gdshader` draws it at `bed_h` now; headspace and vapour start
    there. Glow is temperature alone (`GLOW_FROM_C` 420 → `GLOW_FULL_C` 800,
    dull red → orange → yellow). The reactor presets ship
    `TcProcControl.done_rule` ("Elements off when the charge is done":
    sensor `charge_done` ≥ 97 % for 20 min), so the batch ends with the
    elements off and black char (84 °C at 10 h). New sensors `charge_done`,
    `charge_mass`; tiles Charge mass / Charge volume.
  - **The molecule lens is ONE worked example**, not a box of ~60 flying
    molecules: `TcMolecules.stories()` (kind → storyboards with stage
    positions; `raw` / `centroid` so the link that stays does not move) and
    a rebuilt `tclab_molecule_lens.gd` (before → bonds break → after, name
    tags, light backdrop, C 0.46 Å balls on 0.085 Å sticks, double bonds as
    two sticks). Wood examples: hemicellulose (xylan2 → xylose link +
    furfural + 2 H2O), cellulose (→ glucose link + levoglucosan), lignin
    (→ guaiacol + ethylene + CO), charring; picked from each component's
    rate in the bed's cells (`wood_rates`). Look check:
    `tools/diag/tclab_lens_look_diag.gd`. `TcMolecules.STORY` is gone.
  - **The reactor's lid** was Ø516 (wider than the vessel) and a dished
    ellipse; the GLB's (meshes Geom3D_7 / _8, drawn lifted 116 mm) is a Ø342
    × 59 mm spherical cap on a Ø380 flange. Vessel keys `lid_dome_od_mm`,
    `lid_shape` dished | cap, `lid_clamp`, `bands` (hoops); crown 1½". The
    model's inside face is Ø366; the preset stays Ø340 (Ø366 broke the
    plastic batch's calibration).
  - **From the user's photos:** vessel `legs` ring_stand / casters / saddle
    (a skid on the shell's −Z side: turn the part a quarter turn),
    `handle_ring`; vessel presets ring_stand_reactor, tall_tank,
    horizontal_tank, cylinder, collection_pot; part type `bowl_reducer`;
    built-in designs `ring_stand_reactor`, `tall_tank`,
    `horizontal_receiver`, `parts_kit`. Sizes are read off the pictures
    (estimates). Not catalog ids (designer only).
  - **Barrel gasometer + small generator (same day, from the user's
    `Gasometer-low poly.glb` and `small generator.glb`; drawn procedurally to
    their measured sizes, the GLBs are not in the repo).**
    - `gas_holder` param `style` (`TcUnits.HOLDER_STYLES`): `barrel_30` (the
      default: 30 gal base Ø526 × 866, 15 gal float Ø382 × 730), `barrel_55`
      (55 gal base, 30 gal float), `bell` (the old steel bell; a saved holder
      with no `style` is still the bell at its own volume). Capacity =
      `BARREL_USABLE` 0.8 of the float (45.4 L / 90.9 L); the hold pressure is
      the float's weight (`barrel_hold_kpa`, a few tenths of a kPa).
      `TcUnits.gas_holder(..., style, what, lift)` builds "all" | "base" |
      "float"; float surfaces are the material keys `bell` / `bell_trim`.
    - `genset` param `model`: `small` (the default: open frame 680 × 560 ×
      620 mm, 48 V DC, `min_kw` 0.35 → `rated_kw` 0.75, efficiency 0.18) or
      `skid` (a saved genset with no `model` is still the 2.5 kW skid set).
      `TcProcSim.engine_setpoint_kw(u)` is the governor: `min_kw` with the
      gasometer under `GOVERNOR_LOW` 20 %, `rated_kw` from `GOVERNOR_HIGH`
      70 %, linear between; a set with no floor runs at its rating.
    - The `biochar_genset` chain uses both: on at 80 % full, off at 15 %, plus
      the done rule (it had been missing there). The generator runs ~1.5–2 min
      each time the 30 gal float fills; ~0.3 kWh over the batch.
    - Process mode draws them live (`tclab_process_view.gd` `_build_units` /
      `_update_units`, node `Live`): the built float is hidden and a live one
      stands at fill × `holder_stroke_mm`; a running generator shakes and
      puffs exhaust; `release()` puts the built parts back on leaving. Tiles
      "Gasometer % full" and "Generator W at 48 V". World-placed props do not
      animate the float.
    - ⚠ The seal blow-off runs after the pressure solve, so a 45 L float
      overshoots its seal by ~3 kPa inside one step at peak gas (the selftest
      allows 3 kPa over).
  - **Third pass (same day): flat double bottom, results tiles, Control tab
    + the controller board.**
    - **The reactor has no legs.** Vessel key `jacket_bottom_mm`
      (`TcVessel.double_bottom`): on a jacket that starts at the bottom seam,
      the jacket wall carries on down to a second flat bottom the vessel
      stands on. "bottom" face nozzles stay on the INNER bottom, so the two
      elements' heads sit between the bottoms. The reactor uses 150 mm, which
      puts its underside on the floor the gasometer and generator stand on
      (the gas line ~90 mm above it). Drawing only: the jacket's process
      volume is unchanged.
    - The designer's studio floor is seated under the design's lowest point
      (`tclab_modal._seat_ground`), so nothing draws below the ground.
    - **Results tab** (was "Readings"): eight tiles of what the batch has made
      and used, each a number + unit + a line under it, from
      `TcProcSim.batch_stats()` (a function of the state, so it scrubs):
      carbon in the char (`CHAR_C_FRAC` 0.80, Lehmann & Joseph 2015), CO₂e
      (× `CHAR_PERM` 0.80, IPCC 2019 Refinement, × 44/12; electricity is NOT
      netted off), biochar, gas made (CO, CO₂, H₂, CH₄, C₃H₆ wherever it
      went, normal litres + MJ), heater kWh in, generator kWh out, liquids,
      charge converted. Under them "Right now" rows (`NOW_ROWS`, KVRow; rows
      that do not apply hide). Tile labels are `tile_<id>` / `unit_<id>` /
      `sub_<id>`.
    - **Control tab** order: Rules, Switches, Sensors, Controller board.
      Sensors an instrument can read are listed with a board tick
      (`sensor_list`, 3 columns); the model's own readings fold away
      (`model_list`); the probe adder says which part it will land on.
    - **`TcProcBoard`** (core/tclab/process/tc_proc_board.gd, pure): maps
      each sensor / switch to an ESP part (temperatures → `max6675`, cooling
      water → `ds18b20`, gasometer fill → `vl53l0x` with a calibrate_linear
      to %, pressure → an `ads1115` channel with a 0.5–4.5 V transducer,
      switches → `relay_1ch`; the every-element group and model readings get
      none) and builds an EspSpec NAMED AFTER THE DESIGN whose entities carry
      the Process Lab's own ids (`entity_ids` pins it). The player's ticks are
      `process.board = {on: {key: bool}}` (kept by TcProcSpec; a board change
      does not restart the run, `_same_run`). "Open the board in the ESP
      designer" = `Main.open_esplab({spec})` over the TC designer
      (EspLabLayer is LAYER_MODAL + 2; `tclab_modal._covered()` stops the TC
      designer taking keys underneath).
    - ESP instances gained `ents: {k: {name, unit, dc}}` (EspSpec.resolve
      keeps it, `EspDesign.entities_of` applies it): the exact entity name /
      unit an instance's entity carries.
    - ⚠ `d.get("k", {}) is Dictionary` then `d["k"]` on a missing key threw
      twice more here: test `has("k")` first.
    - Not done: the ESP twin of that board reads the world's weather, not the
      process; the board is rebuilt from the ticks each time it is opened
      (hand wiring is kept only if saved in the ESP designer's own library).

## ESP board designer (core/esplab/, 2026-11-07)

Library → Structures → "ESP board designer (ESPHome)…" (`Main.open_esplab({spec})`,
layer `EspLabLayer`). Plan: `~/.claude/plans/take-a-look-at-shimmering-fountain.md`
(8 phases, inspired by BoardLab, dash.risal.io/boardlab). The user chose: the
sim / real comparison happens in the game (nothing published to HA),
ESPHome-supported boards only, a placed twin reads the world at its spot.
All 8 phases landed (data, solver, YAML, the modal, the twin, boards in the
world, compare with the real board, breadth + tour stop `18m_esplab`). Not
built: the timeline `esp_sim` track; the ESP32-H2 (no Wi-Fi: its YAML would
need OpenThread).
- **Data is GDScript constants**, not JSON (no `GAME_INCLUDE`, no folder
  listing in exported builds): `EspChips` (per chip: input-only, strapping,
  flash / USB / console pins, ADC1 / ADC2, peripheral counts, routing =
  "matrix" or fixed controller pin lists for the RP2040; seven chips incl.
  the ESP32-S2), `EspBoards` (18 boards: header rows "LABEL=gpio" top to
  bottom, onboard use, a screen board's reserved pins, default I2C / SPI
  pins, regulator mA, optional `flash_size` (written to the YAML: the
  XIAO C6 / S3-Zero / T-Display use a devkit board id with their own flash)
  and `pin_note`; `pin_state` = free / caveat / input_only / reserved /
  rails), `EspParts` (61 parts in 12 categories: iface, addresses, supply,
  optional `chips` (prefixes it works on: CAN and I2S are ESP32-family only
  in ESPHome) and `note` (a caveat on its card), pins with roles FROM THE PART'S SIDE
  (`tx` = the part transmits -> board RX), the ESPHome block, the entities
  with HA unit / device_class / decimals and the twin's error model).
- **`EspAutoWire`** (deterministic): locks first, then I2C (clash -> other
  address -> second bus -> error), SPI, UART, 1-Wire, singles on the
  cheapest GPIO (`_cost`: strapping, onboard use, console, ADC kept for
  analog, input-only pins preferred for plain inputs). Checks carry `why`.
  ⚠ A chip's `analog_only` pins (the ESP8266's A0 = GPIO17) take ONLY an
  analog role: it is also input-only, and the input-only bonus used to put
  plain inputs (a PIR, an e-paper's BUSY) on A0, which ESPHome refuses.
- **The diagram looks like the hardware** (`scenes/ui/esplab_diagram.gd` +
  `esplab_board_art.gd`, 2026-11-07 polish). A board is drawn at its real
  size (`size_mm`, one header pitch = 2.54 mm = `PITCH` units) from
  `EspBoards.LOOKS` (PCB colour; `module` wroom / mini_module / chip / can /
  esp12 / esp01 / pico / screen / atom; antenna pcb / ceramic; `usb` micro /
  c / c2 and `usb_top`; buttons, USB-serial chip, regulator, LEDs, mounting
  holes, castellated): plated holes with rotated silkscreen names, and
  outside each edge a pinout column like a maker's chart — a GPIO chip
  coloured by `pin_state` (purple free, yellow caveat, dark input-only, grey
  taken, rails red / grey, EN green) and a function chip: the net when wired
  ("SDA", or "Relay IN"), else the board's default I2C / SPI pin, TX0 / RX0,
  USB, the board's own use (LED, BTN, PSRAM, LCD…), DAC, ADC1 / ADC2; a rail
  pin shows "GND × 3" only on the pin that carries the wires. A wire's board
  end (`_pin_pos`, what `board_pin_local` returns) is the column's outer
  end; the hole is `_hole_pos`; a board pin's hit area is its whole row.
  Pins stay clear of the USB end (the board grows). Part cards are breakout
  PCBs (`Art.PART_LOOK`: colour + glyph: metal can, ultrasonic pair, relay
  cube, screen, probe, PIR dome, terminals…) with gold header holes (the
  wire ends on the hole) and the twin's readings on a display strip. Wires
  are jumpers with Dupont housings; a wire whose rail is on the far side
  goes round the board's nearer end in its own lane (`w["pts"]`, Chaikin
  rounded), never across it.
- **Block kinds in `EspYaml`** (`yaml.special`): `hub` (an entity-less
  top-level block with an id: MCP23017, PCF8574, MAX485 → `modbus`
  with `flow_control_pin`, SN65HVD230 → `canbus` / `esp32_can`), `ads1115`
  (hub + a single-ended channel sensor), `ld2410` (hub on its UART +
  `has_target` binary sensor + `detection_distance`), `i2s_mic`
  (`i2s_audio` bus + `microphone`), `lcd` (16x2 `lcd_pcf8574`, name +
  first reading), `ssd1306` / `epaper` (`_emit_screen`: a font and a
  lambda; the model from `yaml.model`). ⚠ `esphome config` does not compile
  lambdas: a screen printed the diagnostics' readings as `id().state`
  (they have no id) and still "passed". Screens skip id-less entities; the
  selftest greps every screen's YAML for `id()`.
- **`EspEntityNames` is the one naming contract**: HA's entity_id =
  domain.slugify(friendly_name + " " + entity name). A part whose one entity
  IS the part (Relay, Button, LED Strip) takes the instance's own name: a
  relay called "Fan" is `switch.<node>_fan`.
- **`EspYaml`**: `!secret` for Wi-Fi and the API key; OTA is
  `encryption: {}` (inherits the API key). Validated against ESPHome
  2026.10.2: pmsx003 needs the UART's tx_pin; `rp2:` not `rp2040:`;
  `channel_colors: GRB` not rgb_order; rp2040_pio_led_strip needs `pio:`.
  A key starting "#" prints a comment line; "!" strings print raw.
- **`EspSpec.layout`** (the diagram's card positions) rides the spec but is
  never in `key_of`, so moving a card never re-solves. The cached design's
  `spec` may carry an older layout: the modal reads its own `_spec`.
- **The modal** (`scenes/ui/esplab_modal.gd` on `DesignerShell`) and
  **`esplab_diagram.gd`** (drawn in screen space from diagram units so text
  stays crisp; part cards stack on the side most of their GPIOs are on;
  a card the player moved keeps its spot (`spec.layout`), the rest restack
  on every layout so a card that grows pushes the ones below it down). Drag a part pin onto a board pin = a lock;
  double-click a wire = unlock; Delete / Ctrl+Z / F. Export writes
  `user://esplab_designs/<node>/` (YAML, secrets.yaml only if absent,
  wiring.png cut from the viewport, design.json).
- **The twin (`EspSim`) is a pure function of time**: a reading at t is the
  value at the entity's last update tick (phased per unit by a hash), from
  `source(src, at_h)`, then response lag (first-order over earlier ticks),
  a fixed per-unit bias inside the datasheet accuracy (`BIAS_SHARE` 0.5),
  hashed Gaussian noise per tick, range, resolution; then the part's own
  default filters are INVERTED to the raw signal (a soil probe's volts, a
  flow meter's pulses / min) and EVERY YAML filter (the part's, then the
  player's) is applied in ESPHome's order, rounded to accuracy_decimals.
  So an `offset` the player adds moves the twin exactly as it moves the
  board. `series()` = what HA's recorder keeps (a point only on change).
  Entities carry `part_filters` (how many of `filters` are the part's).
- **`EspWorldProbe`** = the world at a spot, asked at an instant (cached
  per (src, t)): WeatherService temperature / humidity / rain / measured
  GHI, `surface_pressure_hpa` (a FORECAST-ONLY Open-Meteo variable added
  for this; no archive cache bump; NAN outside the window -> the ISA
  pressure at the spot's height above sea level, said in a note),
  AirQualityService PM, and ESTIMATES (flagged per source, `note_of`) for
  lux (GHI × 115), UV (GHI × 0.0085), CO₂ (420 + 35 per person within
  4 m), soil (a rain bucket). `bindings` {src: Callable(t) | value} feed
  power / weight / flow / float / switch; `people_fn` and `distance_fn`
  come from the world in phase 5. Autoloads are found by path.
- The modal evaluates every entity once a second at the player's spot and
  the sim clock (`live_readings()`): cards and the entity list show them.
- **In the world (phase 5).** Catalog `esplab_board` (tools), record key
  `esp_spec` (forwarded by `model_extras` AND the placement ghost), seed
  `PlacedPropService.seed_esplab` from BOTH placement chains: an `appliance`
  graph node bound to the prop drawing `EspBuilder.power_w` (the 5 V budget)
  — off, or the site's AC down, makes every entity unavailable (as with no
  power). `EspBuilder`: a sensor station on a 1.2 m stake (primitive
  meshes): enclosure + the PCB at its real size, air / light sensors in a
  radiation shield, distance sensors on arms looking DOWN, soil probes in
  the ground, relays on the side, a screen, an LED strip; metas
  `sensor_points`, `distance_points`, `label_y`, `esp_board`. ⚠ PlacedProp
  renames the model `ModelRoot`: find it with `EspLabRuntime.board_model`.
  `EspLabRuntime` (gameplay/, beside CspLabRuntime) reads the twin once a
  second at the prop and the sim clock: people = NPC dots + the player
  within range; an unbound distance sensor = a ray straight down from its
  arm (own bodies excluded, terrain fallback); `latest`, a Label3D over the
  stake. ⚠ The runtime is a plain Node: its Label3D is parented to the
  PROP or it draws at the world origin.
- **Bindings (`EspBindings`)**: a part's `measures` can name a graph item
  instead of the world: `tank.<gid>.distance_m` (height × (1 − level);
  height = `height_m`, else a cube of its volume — an estimate),
  `tank.<gid>.high` (≥ 90 %), `tank.<gid>.mass_kg`, `item.<gid>.voltage`,
  `load.<gid>.power_w / current_a / current_ac / energy_wh / ac_v / ac_hz /
  pf` (mains 120 V / 60 Hz in the Americas, else 230 / 50), and
  `item.<gid>.switch` (a relay follows its load). Read LIVE from the graph
  specs (never cached by the probe); the part card's "<entity> from" /
  "Follows" picker lists only compatible items. The JSN-SR04T's 25 cm blind
  zone shows as a full tank reading 0.25 m (its range limit, correct).
  ⚠ A tank's level is its ResourceTimeline's: writing specs.level alone is
  undone by the flow engine; set the timeline too (`set_current_level`).
- The designer: Place in world (`begin_placement` with `record_extra`),
  Apply to placed board (record + `seed_esplab` re-rates and renames the
  node), opened bound from the prop editor's "Edit board…" (the live probe
  then stands at the prop and reads the graph).
- ⚠ `PackedStringArray` has no `all()`: wrap it in `Array(...)` first.
- ⚠ A PackedStringArray / PackedFloat32Array fetched from a Dictionary is a
  COPY: `(d[k] as PackedStringArray).append(x)` appends to nothing. Append
  to a local and assign it back (the cards showed no readings until this).
- ⚠ `d.get("k", {}) is Dictionary` is true for a MISSING key: test
  `has("k")` before indexing.
- **Compare with the real board (phase 6, the modal's Compare tab,
  `EspCompare` pure).**
  - **Find my board** (`EspCompare.match_entities`): the id the naming
    contract predicts, else the one catalog entity of the domain whose id
    ends with the entity's slug and whose unit is of the same family (a
    renamed node); a saved choice wins. The map is `spec.real` {twin id:
    real id}; each row also has a picker.
  - **Compare** (`run_compare`): `HomeAssistant.request_history` per entity
    over 6 h / 24 h / 3 d / 7 d, rows onto the SITE clock
    (`parse_history` → `SiteTime.unix_to_site_abs`), against the twin's
    IDEAL series (`EspSim` `ideal`: no per-unit bias or noise, still the
    part's resolution and the design's filters) at the bound board's spot
    (else the player's), tank history from the tanks' ResourceTimelines
    (`EspWorldProbe.tank_level_fn` → `EspBindings.read(..., level_at)`).
    `stats` holds both on one grid: n, coverage, bias (real − twin), MAE,
    RMSE, r, the line real = a·twin + b; `verdict` = good / fair / poor
    against the part's own datasheet accuracy. Chart:
    `scenes/ui/esplab_compare_chart.gd` (held steps, twin cyan, real amber).
  - **Calibrate** writes an ESPHome `offset` (−bias) or `calibrate_linear`
    (the inverse line over the range seen) filter onto that entity
    (`with_calibration` replaces an earlier one, keeps the player's own).
    Calibration filters carry `"cal": true`: `EspYaml` strips the marker,
    the twin SKIPS them (they correct the real sensor toward the twin), so
    after reflashing the comparison reads bias ≈ 0.

## Solar designer (core/pvlab/, 2026-10-27)

Library → Structures → "Solar designer…" (no hotkey); click a placed array or
the prop editor's "Edit solar array…" reopens it bound to the prop. A placed
legacy `pv_array` rack has "Open in Solar designer…", which converts it
(PlacedPropService.convert_pv_array_to_pvlab). Model id `pvlab_array`
(`PvLabBuilder.MODEL_ID`), record key `pvlab_spec`, library
`user://pvlab_library.json` ({modules, designs}), exports
`user://pvlab_designs/`. Plan: `~/.claude/plans/i-want-a-new-foamy-goose.md`.
- **A spec is one module on one array** (`PvLabSpec`): `module` (PvLabModule:
  dims mm, type rigid / glass_glass / flexible / thin_film / folding, cells
  {tech, format, cut, cols, rows — counts of cell PIECES — gap, split gap,
  busbars, fingers, chamfer, parallel}, frame, backsheet, glass, jbox
  {layout, leads_mm, connector}, bypass_diodes, folding, look, electrical
  {mode derived | datasheet, nameplate, coefficients, NOCT, mass}),
  `array`, `rack`, `tracker`, `strings` {mode rows | cols | custom, size
  (0 = the longest the target allows), inputs, groups}, `target` (the
  controller window), `colors`.
- **The cells ARE the electrics** (`PvLabCells`, per-cell Voc / Jsc / vm / im
  read back from real data sheets, cited): Voc = series cells × cell Voc,
  Isc = paths × Jsc × piece area (pseudo-square chamfer from the ingot
  diameter; poly is cast square). A half-cut module is two halves in
  parallel. Datasheet mode keeps the typed nameplate and warns past 12 %.
- **Substrings** (`PvLabModule.substrings`): diode groups by column pairs (else
  rows), each with its parallel paths, each path a list of sample BANDS: a
  path's light = MIN over bands of each band's MEAN (series cells run at the
  weakest; a thin-film strip averages along its length).
- **I–V** (`PvLabIV`): single-diode with Rs, no shunt (Villalva 2009), V(I)
  explicit; a, Rs, I0 fitted per cell through (Vmp, Imp) with dP/dI = 0, so
  a uniform module at STC makes exactly Wmp (pinned). When even Rs = 0 cannot
  reach the fill factor (CdTe), Rs = 0 and a is solved through Vmp; ⚠ v(Imp)
  FALLS as a grows, the first bisection had it backwards. Substring = paths in
  parallel behind a 0.5 V Schottky drop; string = voltages add at one current
  (current grid dense under each substring's limit); array = currents add at
  one voltage; MPP refined. Curves cached on quantised irradiance (2 W/m²).
- ⚠ **Half-cut physics**: one shaded HALF still sends its substring's current
  through the shared diode — it costs a third, like a full-cell module. The
  half-cut advantage is a shadow along an EDGE (every substring's lower half):
  half kept, where full cells go nearly dark. The plan's "a sixth" was wrong.
- **Layout** (`PvLabArray.layout`): the array frame faces +Z (south at yaw 0,
  as PvArrayBuilder). Fixed tables: rows march north, `cols` across, `stack`
  up the slope; row pitch 0 = no winter-noon shade (PvGridSnap.shade_gap_m at
  `site_lat`). roof_flush / none are tilt 0 in their own frame — the PROP's
  pitch / roll lay them on the roof. Trackers: rows spaced along X by GCR,
  the axis along Z, heads turned about Z (+ tips toward −X, west at yaw 0).
- **Racks** (`PvLabRack`): 2x4 / 2x6 lumber (NDS 2018 Table 4A SPF #2),
  Unistrut P1000 / P1001 (catalog Ix / Sx, 25 ksi), generic Al rail
  (labelled an estimate), posts, torque tube, pipe; mounts ground, roof_flush
  (L-feet), roof_tilt, ballast, pole, tracker, none. Span check = simply
  supported rail, bending and L/180 deflection; BOM first-fit stock packing.
- **Tracker** (`PvLabTracker`): Marion & Dobos 2013 eq. 7 (pvlib singleaxis
  convention), backtracking `R − sign(R)·acos(min(cos R / GCR, 1))`
  (pinned: the next row never shades), limits, night / wind stow.
  `PvTrackerRuntime` turns the heads (sim-time aware like CspTroughTracker);
  the energy model computes the same angle per instant itself.
- **Builder** (`PvLabBuilder`): module mesh per design (glass face with
  `pv_module.gdshader` — the cell grid procedural over UV, fingers / busbars
  box-filtered with fwidth so they never shimmer — frame C-profile, backsheet,
  junction boxes, connectors), modules a MultiMesh ("Panels", per tracker
  head), members swept from their real section ("Rack"), string links as
  cables, a hidden "CollisionMesh" (modules + members: other rows' shading
  rays hit it), `pieces` for deploy crews. Overlay tints go through
  INSTANCE_CUSTOM only with `use_overlay` (a plain mesh's COLOR is white).
- **Modal** (`scenes/ui/pvlab_modal.gd`): Cell / Panel / Array tabs over one
  studio, an I–V / P–V chart, string painting by clicking modules (switches
  to custom wiring), test shadows (edge / module / pole / leaf) with the
  mismatch loss, live tables against the controller window, "now" at the
  site when bound (sun, weather, plane, live shade).
- **Graph** (`GraphPvLabArrays`, view delegates add_designed_solar_array /
  remove_designed_solar_array / designed_array_strings): one compound
  `compound_kind` "pv_design" per MPPT input with ONE + / − pair (exposed
  ports "positive" / "negative" over the strings' bus) and the real panels
  wired in strings inside, so flat_connections / PvElectrical /
  GraphDcElectrical see real strings. Re-seeding rebuilds the interior in
  place (outside wires survive). Not compound_kind "array": walk_items counts
  the panels, never the compound too. Panels carry pvlab_tag / pvlab_panel /
  bound_prop_id and their plane or tracker. Opening the designer bound reads
  the graph's strings back (custom wiring).
- **Energy**: `_collect_root_array_aggregate` adds "planes" ONLY when a
  designed array exists (each MPPT input its plane or tracker, the rest of the
  PV one plane at SolarUI's orientation); SolarUI `_compute_solar_kw` sums
  share × POA per plane (`_poa_for` is the same arithmetic). No planes = the
  old single-plane path, untouched.
- **Shade** (`PvLabShading`): samples on the module faces 3 cm out, rays to
  the sun (`Live`: 96 rays a tick round-robin, a pass restarted when the sun
  moves 0.25°), a shaded sample keeps the plane's diffuse share
  (`PvLabShading.poa`, SolarUI's model), the I–V model gives the factor.
  The throttle pass adds one receiver per compound (its `s` + a
  `factor_fn` that GraphSolarShading.factors_at calls for rendered instants:
  one ray per module, ≤ 48). Panel cards say "Shade on N of 3 substrings".
  A tracker excludes its own PropBody (the collider is built flat).
- **Placement** (`PvSurfaceAim`): physics hit on terrain or a PropBody, or an
  OSM roof via `TerrainLoader.roof_ray` (marching `BuildingBuilder.roof_plane_at`
  over footprints the ray crosses — buildings have no collider). A pitched
  surface (> 6°) switches the ghost to roof_flush and lays it in the surface,
  facing down the slope; R / Shift+R turn it. The record stores yaw / pitch /
  roll / y_offset and `mount_host` {kind, id, local}: a prop host moving
  carries it (`_reseat_hosted`), a deleted host drops it to the ground
  (`release_hosted`). ConduitSurfaceAim's merged-buildings lookup now finds
  "Buildings/BuildingMeshes".
- **Second pass (2026-10-27).**
  - **A type is a build** (`PvLabModule.type_patch`, `TYPE_PATCH`):
    switching Rigid / Glass–glass / Flexible / Thin film / Folding sets the
    frame, thickness, front sheet, backsheets, boxes and (for thin film) the
    cells. Before, the type was only a label and nothing on screen changed.
    Flexible laminates have rounded corners (`corner_r_mm`, −1 = by type),
    ETFE dimples and grommets; a clear rear (glass–glass) draws the cells'
    grey backs through it (`cell_material(..., back = true)`, shader
    `back_side`).
  - **Frame lip**: `frame.overlap_mm` (default 4) and `lip_mm` (1.8). The
    glass runs under the lip, which stands proud of it.
  - ⚠ **No point-sampled fine lines in `pv_module.gdshader`.** Every pattern
    (cell gaps, busbars, fingers, scribes, the film's relief) is the
    box-filtered INTEGRAL of its pulse train (`pulse_int` / `pulse_cov`, a
    1.5-pixel box). Footprints are taken once at the top, in uniform control
    flow: derivatives inside a branch are undefined at its edges. Sampling a
    0.35 mm busbar with a soft edge is what made the medium-distance moiré.
  - **Racks are drawn down to the part** (`PvLabHardware`, d["parts"]):
    - module clamps (mid / end, black on a black frame unless set), rail
      splices, end caps (yellow on Unistrut), grounding lugs;
    - a joint at each rail-over-purlin (aluminium L-bracket / P1026-class
      fitting / H2.5A-class hurricane tie) and at each leg top (post bracket
      / gusset / BC4-class post cap);
    - footings (`rack.footing`: ground screw, pier, base plate,
      ABU44-class post base), flashed L-feet on roofs, ballast brackets,
      brace bolts;
    - on trackers: bearings, a slew drive per row, module rails
      (`mrail` members), U-bolt rail clamps and module bolt sets.

    L-feet, ground screws and bearings stopped being members. The BOM counts
    the drawn parts and their fasteners (`FASTENERS`). `PvLabBuilder.emit_part`
    draws each part; `pick_any` picks module / member / part.
  - **The Array tab picks parts.** A click selects a part or member. Its card
    says what it is, its spec, where it is, how many, cost, mass and
    fasteners, with "Light all". The Modules toggle hides the modules. The
    BOM's eye buttons light every part of that kind.
  - **Real modules** (`PvLabCatalog`): 21 data-sheet modules (JA, LONGi,
    Canadian Solar, Trina, Jinko, Qcells, REC, Maxeon, Panasonic, LG,
    First Solar). They come from the makers' data sheets as transcribed, not
    re-checked against the PDFs. The selftest holds every entry to
    Vmp × Imp ≈ Pmax and its cells fitting the face. `module_spec` picks the
    largest standard wafer that leaves a 7–25 mm lip.
  - The left list has a search box that matches every word against maker,
    model, watts, tech and size.
- Not built: per-module orientation on curved hosts (an array is planar), a
  2D plan view for string painting, bifacial rear gain, inverter /
  optimiser / micro-inverter models, a building host re-seated after a style
  change, MPPT-input split of one prop across two controllers by hand (the
  compounds wire to the nearest controller), moving or swapping a rack part
  by hand (parts are picked and listed, not edited).

## Globe mode (core/globe/ + scenes/ui/globe/, 2026-11-05)

Plan: `~/.claude/plans/i-have-been-playing-abstract-frost.md`; spike notes
`plans/GLOBE_SPIKES.md`. A native 3D Earth for picking places and global
context (inspired by Gods Eye View, not a clone). User's choices: native
first, Cesium only later as an optional photoreal layer (3D Tiles for Godot:
no 4.7 build, needs a double-precision engine, ion / Google keys); a SEPARATE
mode beside the unchanged 2D picker; coarse NASA POWER GHI only for now.
Phases 0 (spikes), 1 (globe core), 2 (the mode), 3 (clouds, rain, the
satellite of the day) and 4 (GFS wind streamlines, temperature, wind power)
6 (global ↔ local), 7 (polish) and the Solar Atlas half of 5 landed. Wind
atlas: not done (the user's call, 2026-11-05: GWA's world files sit behind a
figshare bot check and its tiles are an undocumented staging server).
- **`GlobeMode`** (scenes/ui/globe/globe_mode.gd, `GlobeMode.open(parent,
  site, time_provider)`): the hub's "Globe" button, or in-game
  `toggle_globe` (Shift+L; main.gd checks it BEFORE the picker's L, which
  also matches Shift+L) via `Main.open_globe_mode / toggle_globe_mode`
  (sim clock for the sun, "You are here" pin, root `disable_3d` while up,
  handed back on close). Search (Nominatim, or "lat, lon" typed), a click
  card (place via SitePrivacy, zone + kWh from GhiService, "Create world
  here"), a pin per saved world (Play), layers: solar zones (bands /
  smooth) and city lights. Esc steps out: results, card, mode.
- **`WorldLauncher`** (core/worlds/): the ONE place → world path
  (register_map → WorldStore.create → save the running world →
  WorldSession.launch); the picker's map registration and save use it too.
- **GHI layer** (`GlobeGhiOverlay`): 360x180 equirect PNG (R = GHI / 8,
  G = land) built on a worker, cached `user://globe_cache/ghi_overlay_v4.png`
  (bump the name when the build changes); drawn by `globe_surface` from the
  world normal, fading out below ~20 km. ⚠ `TopojsonLoader.is_on_land` marks
  whole latitude bands as land where a small island ring crosses 180°
  (Fiji -16.5°, Wrangel 71°): `GlobeGhiOverlay.land_test` unwraps rings
  wider than 180° but under 10° tall. The 2D picker map still uses the raw
  test.
- **Weather layers** (`GlobeWeather`, a GlobeMode child; all at the globe's
  instant, `GlobeView.current_jd()`: the sim clock in-game, now minus the
  hub's time strip, up to 72 h back):
  - Clouds: nowCOAST `global_longwave_imagery_mosaic` (4096x2048 gray +
    alpha, hourly, ONLY the last ~5 h; frame = nearest within 1.5 h from the
    capabilities' time list, else refused with the window named). Drawn on
    a weather shell at r 1.0016 (`globe_clouds.gdshader`; cover =
    smoothstep(0.30, 0.66, gray) x alpha, fades out below ~20-75 km) with
    shadows on the sunlit ground (`globe_surface` `has_cloud_shadow`).
  - Rain: GIBS WMS `IMERG_Precipitation_Rate_30min` (2048x1024, since
    1998, ~5 h latency: `rain_slot` floors to the half hour and caps at
    now - 5 h; a fully transparent reply = no data, step back 30 min, 8x).
    Drawn over the clouds on the same shell.
  - Satellite of the day: `MODIS_Terra_CorrectedReflectance_TrueColor`
    3857 Level9 tiles registered as fetcher layer `daily_<date>`
    (`GlobeTileFetcher.register_layer`, `GlobeView.set_base_layer`; Esri
    fills in while tiles load); date = the instant's, never after yesterday.
  - Cache `user://globe_cache/{clouds,rain}/<stamp>.png`, decoded + mipmapped
    on WorkerThreadPool (waited on exit). Equirect lookups go through
    `globe_eq.gdshaderinc` (`textureGrad` from a seam-free u, or the mips draw
    a line down 180°). ⚠ `get_shader_parameter` returns null for a parameter
    never set: track layer flags in variables, never `bool(get_shader_...)`.
- **Wind** (Phase 4): `Grib2Decoder` (pure) reads one GRIB2 message:
  grid 3.0, product 4.0, packing 5.0 / 5.2 / 5.3 (NCEP g2clib's comunpack:
  group refs / widths / lengths each byte-aligned, spatial-differencing
  descriptors sign-magnitude), bitmap; ECMWF's 5.42 (CCSDS) is refused.
  `to_field` makes it north-up from lon0, `sample` is bilinear with wrap.
  ⚠ GDScript `floor()` / `round()` return Variant: `var x := floor(..)`
  fails to compile ("Cannot infer the type"); use floorf / roundi.
  `GlobeWeather.request_wind`: GFS 1° from the AWS bucket (2021 onward),
  run = newest at or before the time that is out (4.5 h latency), forecast
  hour = nearest 3 h; a missing run's .idx steps back 6 h (3x). Only
  UGRD/VGRD 10 m + TMP 2 m by HTTP Range from the .idx, cached
  `user://globe_cache/gfs/<run>_fFFF_<u|v|t>.grb2`. On a worker:
  `GlobeWindField.trace` (Fibonacci seeds, RK2 along the direction both
  ways, 0.45° steps, cell ownership at 1.6° = evenly spaced lines; ~1400
  lines / 150 ms on the real field), `line_arrays` (PRIMITIVE_LINES at r
  1.0025, UV.x = distance, UV.y = phase, COLOR.r = speed / 40) and the
  temperature / wind-power overlay images. `globe_wind.gdshader`: faint
  lines + comets moving downwind at a speed-proportional rate (TIME),
  additive, coloured by speed. "Colour by" (Nothing / Solar zones /
  Temperature / Wind power) shares the one overlay slot (set_overlay's
  offset / ramp_lo / ramp_step). Wind power = ½ρv³ at 100 m by the log law
  from 10 m, z0 3 cm (open land; overestimates at sea), a snapshot.
  Fixtures: `core/globe/testdata/gfs_2026110500_f000_*.grb2`, pinned
  against Open-Meteo's GFS at the same hour (open sea, Iceland).
- Pin labels declutter (near side only, priority + no overlap); a world
  whose name is its address label goes through SitePrivacy.
- **`GlobeView`** (Control): its own World3D in a SubViewport, so it runs on
  the launch hub (no Main) and in-game with no camera claim. Earth radius
  1.0, `GlobeMath` frame (+Y north pole, lon 0 on +Z, 90° E on +X).
  Coordinates cross APIs as `PackedFloat64Array [lat, lon]`.
- **Ground = Web Mercator tiles laid straight onto the sphere** (one curved
  16x16 patch per tile, relative to its centre, with skirts; no
  reprojection). `GlobeQuadtree.select` (pure) splits the tile most over
  256 px until the budget (220) or z17; poles above 85.05° are caps tinted
  from the adjacent row's pixels. A tile still loading draws its nearest
  loaded ancestor through `day_rect`.
  ⚠ Tile angular sizes come from CHORDS, never `acos(dot)`: in float32 a z14
  tile's cos rounds to 1, its radius to 0, and the cone test culled visible
  edge tiles (a hole in the screen corner at 10 km).
- **Lighting is the real Sun** at the clock's instant
  (`GlobeMath.subsolar_point`: Almanac low-precision Sun + Meeus GMST,
  pinned against SolarPosition); `time_provider` (JD UTC) or the computer's
  clock. NASA Black Marble lights on the night side, an atmosphere shell
  (back faces, density at the ray's closest approach), the star map behind
  (sky shader, same mapping as `StarSkyMath.uv_from_equatorial`).
- **`GlobeTileFetcher`**: 6 HTTPRequests, nearest-first, unwanted requests
  dropped each frame, disk cache `user://globe_cache/<layer>/z/x/y`, LRU of
  900 textures, ESRI "no data" tiles count as failures. Layers: `esri`
  (z17), `night` (GIBS Black Marble, z8).
