## Fire (crisis_events/fire/) — the burn front

A fire used to be a POINT: it sat where it was lit and "spread" only by
absorbing whole sibling meshes, so a structure that is one mesh never spread,
and `ignition_point_on_mesh_progress` worked in the mesh's LOCAL frame (local Y
is not up on a Z-up GLB, and its "lift" was read off the local height and added
as metres — on an inch-unit import that is metres above the model: "the flame
starts at the very top"). `FireNode` now runs in **surface mode**:

- On its first `_process` frame (not `_ready` — the event positions the node
  AFTER `add_child`, and that position is the ignition spot) the structure is
  sampled once into ~3000 world-space surface points, AREA-weighted over the
  triangles (a box is twelve triangles; one point each is eight candles),
  sorted by height.
- `burn_progress` 0..1 is the front. It climbs in REAL time (~0.22 m/s, 18–90 s)
  as well as sim time, holds while sprayed, and reaches round the base from the
  ignition spot before it tops out. `WALL_GROWTH_PER_SEC` does the same for
  intensity: at 1x sim speed `GROWTH_RATE` alone adds 0.02/s and a fire never
  reached `SPREAD_MIN_INTENSITY`.
- The emitters switch to `EMISSION_SHAPE_POINTS` over the points in a band
  under the front, rebuilt in `BURN_STEPS` steps; the node moves to that band's
  centre so the lights and the extinguisher's detection sphere travel with it.
  In surface mode the emitters keep a FIXED `amount` and unit scale/zero offset
  (the points are world offsets) and `amount_ratio` does the scaling — writing
  `amount` restarts an emitter.
- `fire_char.gdshader` is assigned as `material_overlay` (so the model keeps
  its own materials): scorched behind the front, black below, an ember line on
  the front, all from world height + distance from the ignition point. Late in
  the fire `char_all` takes the whole structure black, then from
  `BURN_AWAY_FROM` of its life the materials are swapped for `fire_ash.gdshader`
  (noise-threshold dissolve, top first) — the overlay is REMOVED at that point,
  because it redraws the whole mesh and would fill the holes back in.
  ⚠ `GeometryInstance3D.transparency` was tried for the fade first: it hides an
  alpha overlay entirely, so the charred structure flashed back to clean wood.
- Restore goes through the existing `_restore_burned_mesh` /
  `regenerate_meshes_under`, which now also clear the overlay
  (`fire_char_overlay` / `fire_pre_overlay` metas). A fire put out part-way
  leaves the char exactly where the front reached, with the embers off.
- **Collapse, then a pile that burns down** (`FireAshPile`,
  `fire_ash_pile.gd` + `fire_pile.gdshader`). Burning away used to leave the
  last quarter of a structure hanging in the air. At `DISSOLVE_AT_COLLAPSE`
  0.65 — MEASURED as 75 % of the surface gone against the ash shader's noise,
  not a guess — the ash shader's `collapse` uniform drops what is left into
  the base (world_vertex_coords; the burn pattern is keyed on the PRE-fall
  position so the holes ride down with the piece), the pile fires a one-shot
  `whoosh()` (flame, smoke, sparks) as the fall passes its midpoint, and the
  meshes are hidden when it lands. The pile covers the footprint of the BASE
  (bottom quarter of the surface points) and is a RENDERER: FireNode hands
  it `FireAshPile.look(age, bonfire_h, ember_h)` every frame (`set_look`);
  it keeps no clock of its own. It is removed by Restore / prop delete.

**The fire is a PURE FUNCTION of sim time (`FireTimeline`,
`crisis_events/fire/fire_timeline.gd`).** Everything a fire IS lives in one
JSON record — `ignited_h`, the three durations `climb_h` (ignition →
collapse), `bonfire_h`, `ember_h`, their `auto` estimate, `holds`
(`[[a, b], …]` abs hours the extinguisher held it; the burn clock stops
inside) and `out_h` (put out: the state FREEZES there) — and
`FireTimeline.state_at(rec, t)` says what to draw. `FireNode` integrates
NOTHING any more: each frame it reads the clock
(`Main.get_absolute_hours`), computes the state and RECONCILES the scene to
it (`_apply_state`, idempotent and order-free), so scrubbing the timeline
backwards stands the structure up again and the whole life runs at the
world's rate at any speed. Records are written only when something happens
(ignition, spray holds, going out, a duration edit). What it replaced, so
nobody restores it: a real-time climb (18–90 s regardless of sim speed),
`fire_time_hours` integration, `DESTROY_TIME_HOURS`, the per-frame re-armed
smouldering pile, and `FireEvent.cleanup` freeing the nodes. Rules:
- **For a placed prop the record rides the prop** (`rec["burn"]`, written
  via `TerrainLoader.set_prop_burn_record`, which is QUIET — a prop rebuild
  frees every prop node and spraying writes once a second — and debounces
  the save). `FireNode.sync_prop_fires` (from `_rebuild_placed_props`) brings
  a saved fire back at the right moment of its life on reload; a FireNode
  whose prop was rebuilt under it `_rebind_scope`s to the new node and
  re-applies the state; one whose record was removed (Restore →
  `clear_prop_burn_record`) disposes itself, pile and all. ⚠ A fresh
  FireNode has no record on the prop until its first flush — `_flushed_once`
  is what stops it disposing itself on frame one. Scene structures (no
  prop) keep the record in memory.
- **Durations are estimated from the structure** (`FireTimeline.estimate`:
  climb from height + base footprint, bonfire ∝ fuel mass^0.7 with a tonne ≈
  6 h, embers a 0.35 share; mass from `PackedSpec` where the catalog knows
  it, else surface area × 25 mm of timber) and the player can override them
  in the prop editor's Fire section — on the LIVE record while it burns
  (`set_duration`, `reset_to_auto`) or as `rec["fire_plan"]` for a fire that
  has not started, which `_estimate_durations` applies over the estimate at
  ignition. The collapse itself is `COLLAPSE_H` = 3 s of SIM time: a real
  fall at 1x, a snap at speed, with the real-time whoosh carrying the moment.
- **The extinguisher writes HOLDS, not progress.** While sprayed the front
  simply does not advance (`burn_hours` nets the hold out), so a held fire
  collapses later by exactly the hold; `intensity` is now only the fight —
  it sits at the phase's level and the spray pulls it down; at the threshold
  `put_out` is written and everything freezes at that hour (char where the
  front reached, embers off, a doused pile loses its glow). `FireEvent` is a
  thin wrapper: it mints the record (`fire.ignite_at`), hears
  `fire_extinguished` ONCE when there is no open flame left (put out →
  RESOLVED; burned down past the collapse → FAILED, the structure is lost)
  and never frees a FireNode.
Scope: `MeshInstance3D` only (as `set_burnable` always was) — MultiMesh-built
structures such as Linkage frames are not sampled. A point fire (no readable
geometry) gets the same timeline and pile without the fall.

## Placed-prop editor (`scenes/ui/placed_prop_edit_ui.gd`) — ONE dock, a gumball

`UILayer/PlacedPropEditUI` is the editor for EVERY placed thing. It replaced
a two-row bottom drawer of spinboxes that locked the mouse into a modal, and
— the complaint that drove it — the per-model redirects in
`interaction_focus.open_prop_edit_ui` that sent a StarShade to the StarShade
designer, a trash/mud printer to the print setup and a pallet rack to its
builder, none of which could move or delete the prop (a StarShade had no
Delete anywhere). Those are BUTTONS in its Model section now; the Interact
key keeps its "use it" meaning (linkage deploy/stow, FDM print setup, packed
crate unpack) while a click always opens the editor.
- **Tool-overlay tier** (`CursorController.request_tool_overlay`, the J
  Light Studio contract): free cursor, RMB look, WASD, one Esc closes (Esc
  first cancels a drag or disarms Delete). Right-edge dock, `UITheme`
  sections: Placement / Display / Fire / Model, footer Duplicate + Delete.
- **The gumball is a `LightGizmo`** (generic despite its name) on the
  prop's origin: arrows + planes move, rings rotate, `L` or the World/Local
  button switches frames, Shift snaps 0.25 m / 15°. Drags preview through
  `TerrainLoader.preview_prop` and COMMIT on release through
  `PlacedPropService.update_prop_record(main, id, patch, rebuild_prop=true)`
  — only THIS prop is rebuilt; the loader's `update_prop_record` rebuilds
  every prop and would pull the node out from under the gizmo (OSM
  replacements still go through the loader so their building re-attaches).
  Clicking another prop in the world switches the editor to it.
- **Fire section**: Burnable; the auto estimate line (durations + fuel
  mass); three duration spinboxes in MINUTES that write `fire_plan` before a
  fire and the live record during one; Auto (reset), 🔥 Ignite (through the
  crisis manager — found by NAME, `CrisisEventManager`, the group is only
  added later), Put out, Restore.
- Delete is two-click (arm, confirm); Duplicate goes through
  `TerrainLoader.duplicate_prop_record` (strips id / burn / graph binding /
  stow state) and selects the copy.
Verify with `--capture=propedit` (Validation list).

## The beat: dancing to the music, sound-reactive lights (2026-10-08)

**One registry, `StageBeat` (`core/population/stage_beat.gd`).** Every stage
with a set on — and every venue playing its own track — publishes its beat
each frame from `StageMusic._publish`: {pos (the speakers), radius
EARSHOT_M 180, bpm, beat, energy, breakdown, build, drop_pulse, until_drop,
since_drop, running, live}. Readers ask `StageBeat.at(pos)` (nearest in
earshot, extrapolated to NOW so a reader between publishes still lands on the
beat). The crowd shader gets the 4 nearest to the camera as globals
`music_pos0..3` / `music_beat0..3` (declared in project.godot
[shader_globals]; beat wrapped mod 128 for float precision; reading a global
back is editor-only, so `StageBeat.pushed_pos` mirrors what was sent). The
music plays at 1× whatever the sim speed, so dancers at a stage move at the
real tempo; it pauses with the sim.
- **Real tracks: live analysis with LOOKAHEAD.** `StageMusic` plays a
  second, silent, non-positional copy of the track LOOKAHEAD_S (5 s) AHEAD of
  the audible one on its own bus (`BeatAnalysis0..3`, ANALYSIS_SLOTS 4) at
  -80 dB with an `AudioEffectSpectrumAnalyzer` — measured: the analyzer reads
  the signal before the bus volume, on WASAPI and the headless Dummy driver
  alike. `BeatTracker` (pure) turns the bass band into kicks, tempo (the
  pairwise-interval histogram gives a COARSE tempo; a least-squares line
  through the kicks' chained beat indices gives the period and phase — the
  histogram alone sat on 0.467 / 0.483 s for a 0.476 s beat because kick
  times are quantised to the 60 Hz analysis frame), breakdowns (slow bass
  under 0.35 of its peak for 1.5 s) and DROPS (the first strong kick after
  ≥ 2 s of breakdown, snapped to the beat). Queried at the HEARD time, a drop
  is known up to 5 s before it is heard — that is what lets the DJ raise an
  arm in time. The audible player starts at, and is re-synced to (> 0.12 s
  drift), analysis − 5 s. Analysis time is the track POSITION only (no
  time-since-mix extrapolation: measured closer to the true tempo).
- **No track: `BeatGrid`** — a virtual set per stage (tempo by hash from
  122/124/126/128/140/174), 32-bar phrases: groove, breakdown at beat 96,
  build from 112, the drop on the phrase. Opens mid-groove so the first drop
  is ~30 s in. Same output keys.
- **Dancing** (Settings → NPCs → "Dance to the beat", `NpcDisplayPrefs.
  beat_sync`, default on): the crowd shader's `music_at` and the stick
  figure's `set_beat` (NpcAvatar hands it `StageBeat.at` while dancing) put
  dance / rave / sway / samba / DJ on the beat — one bounce per beat, half the
  crowd a beat out on the sway — throw harder with the energy, raise both
  hands through the run-up to a drop (3 in 4 dancers; `ANTICIPATE_S` 4 s,
  mirrored in the shader as `MUSIC_ANTICIPATE_S`) and keep them up as it
  lands with a jump. **The DJ** raises the left arm and HOLDS it through the
  run-up, both arms in the last moment and on the drop, and jumps. Verify
  with `beat_look_diag.gd`; the rigged Mixamo body plays its clip unsynced.
- **Sound-reactive lights**: three style keys on every light kind
  (`sound_reactive`, `sound_mode` pulse | beat | both, `sound_depth`), shown
  in the J dock's "Sound" section. `StageBeat.light_level` = a kick envelope
  on every beat (rolling to 8ths then 16ths through a build), scaled by the
  energy (dim in a breakdown), plus a flash on the drop; "beat" mode drives
  the effect clock from the music (`light_time`, chases and mover sweeps move
  with the tempo). PlacedLight / PlacedMoverLight (`sound_level`,
  `effect_time()`) and PlacedStringLight (heard at the middle of the string)
  apply it; a light with no music in earshot is just itself.

## Placed vehicles, third person, the player's body (2026-10-08)

**Driveable vehicles from the library** (Unified library → **Vehicles** tab;
catalog category `vehicles`, entries carry `vehicle: <PlacedVehicle.PROFILES
id>`): EUC, Appa (golf cart), skid steer — the scene vehicles' own art at
native scale — plus **Tool Bus** (the International 3800 out of
`Busses.tscn`, the other bus in that file deliberately left out) and the GMC
camper van, which go
through `VehicleModelBuilder` (`source_path` + `isolate` + real `length_m`:
keeps ONE bus of the pair, FREES every hidden node — `ModelCatalog.mesh_metrics`
measures hidden meshes too — lays the long axis on Z, scales to metres, stands
it on y = 0; `flip` turns a model round if its front is backwards).
`PlacedPropRuntime._maybe_attach_vehicle` hangs a `PlacedVehicle`
(`gameplay/placed_vehicle.gd`) under the prop; it speaks the scene vehicles'
duck-typed API (mount / dismount / get_riding_params / range signals — it
self-notifies the player, since `main._connect_vehicles` runs once at boot),
so the player's riding code drives it unchanged. Rules: getting IN snaps the
rider onto the parked vehicle facing its way (scene vehicles snap to the
rider); the prop's collision is OFF while ridden and re-baked
(`setup_collision`, deferred) after the rider steps out LEFT past its
half-width — the StaticBody bakes ModelRoot's rotation into its shapes; the
record is patched IN MEMORY every 0.5 s while driving and saved on dismount;
a prop rebuild while ridden hands the rider to the replacement node
(`_handover`, never during map unload); electric profiles drain with
distance and trickle-charge parked (`charge_w`, sim time) so a flat battery is
a wait, fuel ones show "fuel" on the dashboard. Interact on a placed vehicle
under the crosshair drives it (`interaction_focus._open_placed_prop_edit` →
`player.request_mount`); a click still opens the prop editor. Riding numbers
for the original three are copied from their scripts (the skid steer's
`model_rotation_offset = 91.145` in the scene is RADIANS ≈ 182.2°). A vehicle
model's ROOT position is zeroed in `ModelCatalog.instantiate` (appa.tscn's
root carries a 0.6 m offset the scene instance overrides — left in, the
driver sat beside the cart). Verify the art faces the right way with
`gameplay/vehicle_look_diag.gd` and the whole loop with `--capture=vehicles`
(Validation). Two pre-existing bugs fixed on the way:
`PlacedPropRuntime.find_by_prop_id` looked only under Terrain, so on the
built-in scenes (props under Main) it found nothing and every
`_reposition_scene_prop` move SPAWNED A DUPLICATE node; and
`PlacedProp.setup_collision` queue_freed the old "PropBody" and added the new
one the same frame, so the new one was auto-renamed and lookups by name found
the dying body (the old one is now renamed and disabled first).

**Third person (F5 `toggle_third_person`, Settings → Player).** The CameraArm
detaches (`top_level`) and is placed every frame behind and over the shoulder;
the Camera3D under it keeps its own LOCAL maths (pitch on rotation.x, shake on
position), which is why the FOV, the crosshair ray, camera claims and the FPV
drone (which borrows this camera — the arm goes home while it flies) all keep
working untouched. Mouse yaw orbits (`_tp_yaw`); walking is camera-relative
and the body turns to face its velocity (or the camera while using a tool);
driving, the camera orbits and swings back behind after 1.4 s untouched; on
the EUC the mouse still steers so the camera rides locked behind. Collision:
a physics-frame ray pivot→camera (`_tp_probe_camera`), pulled in at once and
eased back out. In third person the vehicle tilt / seat offset are skipped
and interaction REACH is measured from the player's head
(`player.reach_origin`, read by InteractionFocus). Fixed alongside: the centre
ray's `exclude` passed the player NODE where Godot wants RIDs. PlayerPrefs
(`core/player_prefs.gd`, `user://player.cfg`) holds camera mode, follow
distance, shoulder, recenter, body and tint, polled by generation (the panel
and the player never reference each other). The **player FOV slider moved**
from Lighting to the Player tab; its storage is unchanged
(sim_settings.cfg [camera] player_fov).

**The player's body.** Default = `NpcSimpleFigure` with `hi_detail` (waist,
pelvis + shoulder girdle, neck, jaw, hands, feet kept level, and two extra
pivots the driver writes directly so they never fight the poses' easing: LEAN
at the hips, NECK for head-look) driven by `_update_character_animation_simple`:
idle / walk / RUN (its own pose, flight phase + pumping arms) / air (tuck
rising, reach falling) / landing dip / seated at the wheel at the vehicle's
seat / standing on the EUC / arms forward with a tool, lean into speed and
turns, head following the camera. ⚠ The figure is built facing +Z and is
turned PI — the player's body had been walking BACKWARDS (the NPC avatar got
this fix long ago; the player's never did). First person hides the head and
neck (shadow-only). Remy (asset pack) and custom characters are opt-in
(`PlayerPrefs.body()`): `.glb/.gltf/.fbx` in `user://player_characters/` load
at RUNTIME (GLTFDocument / FBXDocument), are scaled to 1.75 m and turned to
face forward; their own idle/walk/run clips are used when named so, else a
Mixamo rig borrows Remy's clips RETARGETED by bone name (`_bone_key`:
mixamorig:Hips == mixamorig1_Hips == Hips; hips position scaled by hip height;
a clip binding < 12 bones is refused, never played as a T-pose).

**NPC names (Settings → NPC → Names).** Comma-separated names are ADDED to
`NpcAgent.NAME_POOL` (`NpcDisplayPrefs.custom_names`, `parse_names` splits on
, ; and new lines, dedupes case-insensitively); `NpcAgent.name_pool()` caches
per prefs generation. Changing the list re-deals names. Names carry NO number
("Spark", never "Spark 25" — 2026-10-09): a camp ("<seed>_npc_<i>") walks the
pool from a per-camp start with a stride coprime to its size, so nobody in one
camp shares a name until the camp outgrows the pool; other ids hash. The id is
the unique key everywhere, never the name. The population and cohort
selftests clear custom names in `_init` (`reset_custom_names_for_test`) so a
player's friends never move a pin.

## Living vehicles (core/vehiclelab/, 2026-11-01)

Plan: `~/.claude/plans/pasted-content-id-e788-living-vehicles-vectorized-thimble.md`
(8 phases; the user chose: arrive through a gate, typed trip miles,
procedural bodies with a GLB override, HOUSING FIRST). Landed: Phase 1
(parametric vehicles you can place and drive), Phase 2 (housing),
Phase 3 (the designer modal, exterior), Phase 4 (the interior + the
vehicle's own graph node), Phase 5 (turning circle, fuel kinds +
refuelling, towed trailers, trip cost in the ledger), Phase 6 (cargo bays,
crew unload verified), Phase 7 (driving in through the site gate, camps
arriving with their vehicles) and Phase 8 (wheels that roll and steer, the
driver's view out of the cab). All eight are done.
- **A vehicle's life at a glance (polish plan
  `plans/VEHICLES_TRANSPORT_POLISH_PLAN.md`, Phases 0–6 done 2026-11-02).**
  Each stage has ONE rule, named here so nobody writes a second:
  - **Arrive**: `VehicleDrive.pose_for(arrival, departure, h)`, a pure
    function of the clock (scrubs, reloads); the gate is
    `TerrainLoader.site_gate()`; a camp is away until its first vehicle parks.
  - **Unload**: gated on `VehicleCargo.host_ready` (parked, not packed; a
    trailer's tow vehicle parked), retried every 5 s, rewound if the clock
    goes back before the arrival.
  - **Strike / load**: a Pack-up's load-out row stows crates back through
    `TerrainLoader.stow_prop_in` (`VehicleCargo.restow_patches`).
  - **Leave**: `departure` record, scheduled when a Pack-up's crews finish,
    nearest the gate last; scrubbing back past the event takes it back.
  - **The handling table**: `PackKitter.HANDLING` (hand ≤ 23 kg, team ≤ 60,
    forklift beyond). Haul model, forklift rig, packing labels and labour
    all read it.
  - **The door rule**: `VehicleCargo.door_xz(rec)` for containers and
    vehicles alike (`door_near` finds the nearest usable one); stowed
    crates are placed by `place_stowed` / `place_stowed_node`, never by hand.
  - **Whose vehicle**: `TerrainLoader.camp_of_vehicle` (the painted camp it
    stands in, else the nearest camp middle within 300 m), stored as
    `camp_id`; that camp's crew unloads it and is away while it is.
  - **Cost at scale**: `tools/bench/vehicle_site_bench.gd` (40 vehicles on
    Walton; `VSB_QUICK=1` stops after the idle sample) — see the Phase 5
    bullet below for the numbers to beat.
- **Pure core.** `VehicleCatalog` (chassis + bodies + the 11 types +
  interior element types, sources in the header), `VehicleSpec` (record key
  `vehicle_spec`; `resolve` adds `ch` / `bd`, `key_of` = JSON.stringify of
  rounded values with integral floats as ints — JSON hands every number
  back as a float), `VehicleDesign.solve` (cached: layout, axles, wheels,
  driver seat, living box, interior elements, beds, seats, role spots,
  masses, payload, cargo, checks, turning radius = the outer front wheel's),
  `VehicleEnergy` (road load F = m·g·C_rr + ½ρC_dA v², η and LHV cited,
  every preset inside its chassis' mpg band at 55 mph), `VehiclePresets`
  (one per type with a lived-in interior), `VehicleBuilder`.
- **Frame:** origin on the ground under the middle of the overall length,
  -Z = the front (the rider's forward, profile yaw_deg 0), +X = the right /
  curb side. Interior positions are in the living box's frame: x across, z
  from the box's FRONT, < 0 counts from its rear. Chassis and body are
  independent (`chassis_id` + `body_id`, each with overrides); `integral`
  bodies run over the cab (van shell, bus, step van, Class A), `in_curb`
  bodies are already in the chassis curb mass.
- **Builder:** one "Mesh" (chassis, wheels, cab per style as a side profile
  extruded across, floor, interior) + "Shell" (the living box: a rounded
  cross-section swept along it, raked at the front where the vehicle's front
  is, windows, doors, stripe) — a cutaway hides Shell. Every tri goes
  through `_K.tri` (Godot's clockwise front face) with hand-written normals.
  Metas: `seat_spots` (beds as kind "lie" at the mattress top, yaw = the
  bed's long axis; then seats), `role_spots` {kitchen, shower, restroom:
  stand spots on the floor}, `living_vehicle`.
- **World:** catalog ids `vehiclelab_<preset>` (library Vehicles tab) +
  `vehiclelab_vehicle`, `"vehicle": "living"`; a record without a spec builds
  its id's preset, and placement stamps the spec on
  (`PlacedPropService.tag_vehicle_spaces`, also in the ghost commit
  dispatch). `PlacedVehicle.LIVING`: the profile comes from
  `VehicleDesign.riding_profile` (speed by length, turn radius by wheelbase,
  camera at the driver's eye); a trailer has none and gets no runtime. Fuel:
  litres drawn by the energy model at the driven speed (`vehicle_fuel_l`,
  `vehicle_fuel_used_l` on the record); an empty tank refills from a can on
  the next get-in (never a dead end) — real refuelling is Phase 5.
- **Housing.**
  - One prop, several spaces: a prop target may carry `role` + `anchor`
    ([x, z] local); `_targets_equal` compares the role (none = the old single
    space), `SpaceRegistry.prop_point` turns the anchor with the record.
    A vehicle gets a sleep space (capacity = its sleepers) and kitchen /
    shower / restroom spaces.
  - `NpcPopulationBridge.vehicle_spots`: the sleep space lies on the beds,
    a role space stands at its fixture on the vehicle floor (elev), a quiet
    space sits — never all the furniture spots for every space (the flat-pack
    rule would have put the cook on the bed).
  - Camps: `TerrainLoader.camp_shelters_in_polygon` lists living vehicles
    FIRST with their world beds (`vehicle_beds_world`: pos, yaw, elev), so
    bed k is person k's in the light tier and a friend group (consecutive
    indices) shares a vehicle. A camp's own `van` / `rv` shelters now sleep
    ALONG the vehicle at `CampStyles.BED_H` (were across it on the ground).
  - Both tiers lie at bed height: the full tier sets `seat_elev` from the
    bed's `elev` when no seat took it; the light tier carries `home_yaws` /
    `home_elevs` beside `home_slots` (`elev_of` / `face_yaw` while asleep at
    home; extras piled in beside an owner lie on the ground).
  - ⚠ `_prop_revision` used to be the prop COUNT, so a vehicle moved or
    driven into a camp never re-resolved the beds; it now folds living
    vehicles' positions in (once per frame).
- **The designer** (`scenes/ui/vehiclelab_modal.gd`, TerrainLoader
  `open_vehiclelab` / `open_vehiclelab_for_prop` / `begin_vehiclelab_placement`
  on CanvasLayer 27; library Vehicles tab "Vehicle designer…"; prop
  editor "Edit vehicle…"; modal audit id `vehiclelab`; tour stop
  `18j_vehiclelab`). DesignerShell + StudioViewport + FormRow: types and
  designs (built-ins + `user://vehiclelab_library.json`) left; chassis
  (the type's first, then any of the same kind), body, fuel, wheelbase,
  duals, tank / pack; body size, roof, corners, windows, doors; paint
  pickers + a wrap image (`VehicleBuilder.WRAP_DIR` = `user://vehicle_wraps`,
  object-space triplanar stretched once along each side); "Roof & sides"
  palette + the selected item's card; the player's own model
  (`glb_override` {path, mode whole | body, flip}: shipped art or a file
  copied into `user://vehicle_models`, stretched onto the design's box,
  replacing Chassis + Cab + Shell or just Cab + Shell); the trip; summary +
  checks. A chassis or body swap drops the old one's overrides.
- **Exterior items** (`VehicleExterior`, pure): roof / left / right / rear
  faces, an element = {id, type, face, u, v, …}; `resolve_element` clamps it
  onto its face, `frame` gives its oriented box, `face_hit` the ray against
  the body (the roof found by marching down the crown's slab and bisecting —
  a fixed-point refinement did not converge on grazing rays), `candidate`
  the armed template at a hit, `pick` the smallest item among near-equal hits
  (a fan on a solar array, not the array's flat box), `plane_hit` the ray
  against ONE face's plane — what a drag slides on: from a low camera a ray
  aimed at an item standing on a crowned roof passes over the roof
  altogether. Solar = modules (`MODULES`: rigid 400 / 200 W, flexible 100 W)
  in rows × columns; masses go into the curb, `exterior_totals` carries
  solar W and the items' loads for Phase 4. The builder's nodes are now
  Chassis / Cab / Shell / Exterior / Interior (a cutaway drops Shell and
  Exterior). Body profile numbers (crown, y0, wall_top, rake) live in
  `VehicleDesign` once and both the builder and the exterior read them.
- **Inside** (`VehicleInterior`, pure; Phase 4). The designer's "Inside"
  section is a grouped palette (`GROUPS`: Sleep / Sit & eat / Kitchen & bath /
  Storage & work / Power & water / Fittings); arming a piece takes the skin
  off, the ghost follows `floor_hit` + `candidate`, a click appends to
  `spec.interior.elements` ({id, type, x across, z from the box's front,
  w / l / h, yaw 0|90, kwh / litres / watts}). With the cutaway on, inside
  pieces are picked BEFORE roof items (`VehicleInterior.pick`: the nearest box,
  a smaller box INSIDE it instead — a battery under a bed — and a ceiling piece
  only when nothing else is hit, since in cutaway you look through the
  ceiling); a drag slides it on the floor plane keeping the grab offset, R
  turns it, Del removes. "Plan" looks straight down (front at the top). The
  selection knows its kind (`_sel_kind` "ext" | "int"; ids can repeat across
  the two lists). `VehicleDesign.resolve_interior_element` is public (wall-hung
  pieces snap to the nearer wall, ceiling pieces hang from it, the cab-over
  bunk sits over the cab).
  - **The aisle check** (`VehicleInterior.access`): a 0.1 m grid of the floor,
    a cell walkable when it is half a clear width from the side walls and from
    every piece standing on the floor — `AISLE_M` 0.5 m (shoulders) beside
    anything taller than `LOW_TOP_M` 1 m, `HIP_M` 0.4 m beside a bed, bench or
    counter (only hips pass there; ANSUR II) — flooded with EIGHT neighbours
    from the entries (`entries`: side / rear doors from `VehicleDesign
    .door_spans`, the one door rule the builder draws from too, plus the front
    of the box when you walk through from the cab). Seeds are a step in from a
    doorway (r + 0.2 m): the first version seeded 0.75 m in and jumped a wall
    across the door. Every bed / fixture in `NEEDS_ACCESS` must have a reached
    cell within an arm's reach (`REACH_M`) or the checks say "No way in to the
    X…" (with `ids`, so the check row offers "Show it"). Also: less than 60 cm
    over a bed, shower standing room, carried-whole pieces vs the biggest door
    (info). The built-ins were laid out again to pass: the box truck's bed
    moved to the front (it blocked the roll-up, its only door), the trailer's
    door is mid-curbside (body override `door_at_m` 4.0 m: the side door's
    front edge from the box's front), the shuttle's wet bath and dinette and
    the RV's galley shrank / moved off a 0.3 m corner pinch.
    `tools/diag/vehicle_access_diag.gd [-- --preset=<id>]` prints the grid.
  - **The vehicle's graph node** (`VehicleGraph`, pure, + `SystemGraphView
    .sync_vehicle_system`): `VehicleInterior.systems(d)` (house battery kWh,
    bank voltage 12.8 / 25.6 / 51.2 V by size, roof solar per item, loads from
    the exterior items' `load_w` + interior `watts`, water / grey litres) →
    a component definition → `GraphComponentDefs.realize` + `make_unique` at
    root (the camp-compound way): panels in parallel onto an MPPT controller
    (module Voc / Vmp per class, estimates; past `MAX_PANEL_NODES` 16 modules
    one panel per solar item), the house battery, an inverter feeding one
    appliance per load (AC), fresh + grey tanks with fill / dump ports.
    Identity `vehicle_prop_id` + `bound_prop_id` (so the prop's delete removes
    it), `vehicle_sig` = hash of the systems: an unchanged signature only moves
    the node's site coords; a changed one rebuilds it keeping its canvas spot
    and battery SOC. Site coords are TOP-LEVEL item keys, never specs.
    `PlacedPropService.sync_vehicle_graph` runs first in `tag_vehicle_spaces`
    (placement, Apply) and returns the fresh-water tank, which becomes the
    shower and kitchen spaces' `graph_item_id` — the light tier bills those
    visits to the vehicle's own tank (the full tier still bills its habitat).
  - Gates: `vehiclelab_selftest` (657 with polish Phase 1; 493 with the catalog test of 2026-11-02; 323 with Phases 5–8; 275 at Phase 4: floor hits, picking incl. nesting and
    the ceiling rule, doors, access on every preset + a walled-off and a
    too-narrow layout, the graph definition / signature / merge / realize) and
    `vehiclelab_designer_check.gd` (55 at 1080 and 720: a REAL click on the
    fridge tool and the floor, a drag in plan view, Delete / Ctrl+Z, R on the
    galley, the node on the graph with battery + panels + tanks, both spaces
    on its water tank, Apply with a bigger battery rebuilding the node, delete
    removing it).
- **Driving, fuel, trailers (Phase 5).**
  - Steering follows the turning circle: `riding_profile` sets
    `turn_by_radius`, and `player._handle_cart_movement` caps the yaw rate at
    `VehicleDesign.yaw_rate_limit_deg(v, R)` (v / R) — only for living
    vehicles; the EUC / skid steer / golf cart keep their old feel.
  - `ResourceKinds` `gasoline` / `diesel` (L) + library tanks "Fuel Store
    (Gasoline, 55 gal)" / "(Diesel, 275 gal tote)". `PlacedVehicle.refuel()`
    on getting in and out takes from the nearest tank of its fuel within
    `REFUEL_REACH_M` 12 m (`SystemGraphView.draw_fuel_near`: moves the level
    on the tank's ResourceTimeline too). With none, an empty tank still fills
    "from a can", counted in `vehicle_fuel_bought_l`.
  - The ride dashboard (euc_ui) shows FUEL, litres and range
    (`VehicleDesign.range_mi`, 55 mph).
  - Towing (`VehicleTow`, pure): the one-axle trailer model (the axle is
    pulled toward the hitch at tongue length each step — off-tracking settles
    on sqrt(R² − L²), pinned) with a jackknife limit (80°). Drivable designs
    carry `hitch`, trailers `coupler` + `axle_z`. Backing a vehicle's hitch to
    within 0.8 m of a parked trailer's coupler below 1.5 m/s hitches it
    (records `towing` / `hitched_to`); the trailer prop is moved every frame,
    its collision off while towed and re-baked when parked; the prop editor
    has "Unhitch trailer". The semi stays one rigid unit.
  - Running cost: `SiteCost.running_for_record` (the round trip from the
    typed miles + fuel bought on site) → Site balance "Getting here" row and
    each festival camp's card ("N vehicles here · getting here: $X";
    `TerrainLoader.vehicles_by_camp` / `camp_area_for_lot`).
  - Gate: `tools\harness.ps1 -World mtvernon -RunScript res://tools/checks/vehicle_drive_check.gd -Label vehicle_drive -Timeout 900`
    (16/0: refuel from a tote, hitch on backing up, coupler on the hitch round
    a circle, fuel over 1 km == the model, unhitch; 19/0 with Phase 8's
    wheels and cab view; 20/0 with Phase 1's towed fuel: the kilometre is
    driven with the trailer on the hitch and burns the towed figure).
- **Cargo bays (Phase 6).** `VehicleCargo` (pure): the
  largest clear floor rectangle (histogram method over a 0.1 m occupancy grid)
  under the full inside height, loaded through the rear door (else a side
  door, the load then running across), as a ContainerCatalog-shaped entry with
  a `frame` into the vehicle. `UnpackScenario.stow_plan(id, host)` packs into
  it; `VehicleCargo.spawn_in_vehicle` / `TerrainLoader.deliver_kit_in_vehicle`
  stow a kit's crates in it (`stowed_in`, `stow_local`, staging outside the
  door) and queue the usual unload project from the door.
  `PlacedVehicle._tick_cargo` moves stowed crates with the vehicle and
  `_patch_record` re-seats their records. `VehicleCargo.door_near` replaced
  the container-only loadout lookups (site_deploy_director, prop editor); the
  Packing Lab lists placed vehicles' bays ("vehicle_bay:<id>"); the designer
  summary prints the bay. Verified: `vehiclelab_selftest` cargo tests and
  `tools\harness.ps1 -World walton -RunScript res://tools/checks/vehicle_cargo_check.gd -Label vehicle_cargo -Timeout 1200`
  and (Phase 3) `tools\harness.ps1 -World walton -RunScript res://tools/checks/vehicle_delete_check.gd -Label vehicle_delete -Timeout 600`
  (11/0: 7 crates stowed in the bay, ride along driven + turned, records
  follow, the camp pinned, every crate carried out, the camp released).
  - ⚠ **Why the crew never unloaded (fixed):** the unload went to
    `first_crewable_habitat` on its ROUTINE. In festival mode that camp is
    usually a light camp, whose full engine is PARKED (it has a board,
    nobody works it), and a festival day has no work block at all. A
    vehicle delivery now goes to the camp nearest the door
    (`NpcPopulationBridge.nearest_crew_habitat`) and pins it ALL HANDS
    until the project leaves "active" (`pin_crew_until_done`,
    `_project_pins`, pruned each tick; `is_all_hands` = director OR
    project pin). Every other site project now gets the same pin when it
    needs it (`NpcPopulationBridge.needs_pin_to_work`: the camp is light,
    its engine parked, or its routine has no WORK block — checked in
    `create_site_project`), so container deliveries and the Linkage
    rebuild / breakdown queues get a working crew in festival mode too;
    a container's unload goes to the camp nearest its door as well.
  - **The door opens while unloading** (`CargoDoors`,
    core/vehiclelab/cargo_doors.gd): the doors are baked into the host's
    mesh, so an overlay `ModelRoot/DoorsOpen` draws a dark opening on the
    door face and the leaves swung / slid / rolled / lifted out of it
    (barn and container leaves 250°, hinged 100°, lift 80°, a slider back
    by its width, a roll-up rolled at the head). `plan(rec)` reads
    `VehicleCargo.bay` + `door_spans`; `TerrainLoader._sync_cargo_doors`
    shows it on every host whose unload project is active.
- **Arrival through the gate (Phase 7).** `VehicleDrive` (pure): a record
  key `arrival` = {start_h, route [[x, z]…], park [x, z, yaw_deg]};
  `pose_at(arrival, abs_h)` → {state away | driving | parked, pos, yaw,
  speed, u, s}. Route = outside the gate → the gate → along the one
  festival road nearest both ends (`ROAD_SNAP_M` 120) → `APPROACH_M` 14
  behind the spot along its heading → the spot, centripetal Catmull-Rom at
  2 m; speed 6 m/s cruise, v = sqrt(1.2·r) in bends, 1.5 m/s creep on the
  approach, 0.8 / 0.6 m/s² accelerate / brake (comfort figures). Nothing is
  integrated, so it scrubs backwards and survives a reload.
  - `SiteGateBuilder` (model `site_gate`, Library → Structures, two posts +
    beam + "WELCOME HOME"; PackedSpec curated). Vehicles pass through
    heading its forward (-Z) and appear `OUTSIDE_M` 12 behind it.
    `TerrainLoader.site_gate()`: a placed gate, else the festival road end
    farthest from the site centre, else 180 m south of it.
  - `TerrainLoader.schedule_vehicle_arrivals(start_h, spacing)` (every
    self-driving living vehicle, nearest the gate first, 4 min apart; a
    towed trailer comes behind its vehicle, a lone trailer stays) /
    `schedule_vehicle_arrivals_auto()` (from the next DEPLOY flag ahead,
    else 2 min from now) / `clear_vehicle_arrivals()` / `vehicle_arrivals()`.
    UI: Camps & calculator → "Vehicles: Drive in from the gate / Already
    here" + a status line.
  - `VehicleDriveRuntime` (gameplay/, on every living vehicle, polls its
    record at 2 Hz): away = prop hidden, driving = placed on the road
    (ground + the parked lift, collision off), parked = back at the pose it
    was built at. A hitched trailer follows: coupler on the hitch, axle
    `VehicleDrive.point_behind` on the road. Stowed crates ride in it
    (their transform in the parked frame, taken when the drive starts).
    While away / driving the prop carries `META_BUSY` and
    `PlacedVehicle.can_mount` refuses; the player getting in erases
    `arrival` (it is simply here now).
  - **People arrive with their camp's first vehicle**
    (`NpcPopulationBridge._update_away`, each tick): each arrival maps to
    the nearest camp home within `ARRIVAL_CAMP_M` 300; before its first
    park hour the camp is AWAY: not stepped (either tier), demand override
    {} (nothing consumed), left out of `agent_dots` / `agent_dots_full` /
    `light_cohorts` (nothing drawn). `is_away` / `away_camps`. Camp
    granularity, not per person: everybody of a camp appears when its first
    vehicle parks, wherever they were (no teleport into the vehicle). Not
    gated: DJ / burn-role casting (could cast an away person).
  - Gate: `tools\harness.ps1 -World walton -RunScript res://tools/checks/vehicle_arrival_check.gd -Label vehicle_arrival -Timeout 1200`
    (19/0: placed gate is the way in, away before, on the road mid-drive
    and not mountable, parked at the spot, camp away → home, scrub back
    sends both away, "Already here"). Selftest `_test_drive_in` pins the
    road, the approach, timing bounds, monotone + no jumps, the arrival
    heading, scrub purity, `point_behind`, the default gate.
- **Polish (Phase 8).**
  - Wheels are their own nodes (`Wheels/W<i>`, pivot at the hub, five lug
    bolts so a turn shows; meta `wheel_nodes` [{name, r, steer}]).
    `VehicleBuilder.spin_wheels(model, roll_m, steer)`; `steer_for` (bicycle
    model, tan δ = L·κ) and `wheelbase_of`. Driven: `PlacedVehicle` rolls
    them by signed distance and steers from the yaw rate; driving in: the
    route's arc length and its bends. A whole-vehicle GLB override removes
    "Wheels" with "Chassis".
  - The driver's view: body panels are double-sided (StructureMaterials),
    so from the seat the cab and shell walled the driver in (the first
    surface 0.04–0.85 m from the eye). While driven, `set_inside_view`
    gives the Cab / Shell / Exterior / Interior surfaces one-sided
    duplicates (winding is pinned clockwise, so the outside is unchanged)
    and dismount clears them. The van's eye also sat 4 cm behind its
    windshield: a full-van / cutaway seat is now ≥ 0.55 m behind the cab
    profile at eye height, never behind a cutaway's back wall.
    `tools/diag/vehicle_cab_view_diag.gd` prints the first hit per preset;
    selftest `_test_driver_view` pins a clear road ahead and no eye pressed
    to the glass.
  - Not done: multiplayer review of the
    drive (records already sync as prop ops; the pose is a function of the
    clock), a tour stop for the drive-in.
- **Mass and ratings realism (polish Phase 1, 2026-11-02;
  `plans/VEHICLES_TRANSPORT_POLISH_PLAN.md`).** Every number a sheet gives
  is on the chassis: `gawr_f_kg` / `gawr_r_kg`, `tow_kg`, `gcwr_kg`,
  `roof_kg` (van shells; bodies carry their own), `brakes` (trailers),
  `shell_h_m` (a van shell is as tall as ITS van: ProMaster 2.52, Transit
  2.78), `cg_wb` (where the curb mass sits on the wheelbase, from the
  sheet's empty axle weights — a cab-chassis 0.38, a van 0.5, a 35 ft bus
  0.57) and bare-chassis curb masses (F-59 2900, NPR 2850, M2 4800, E-450
  2650, F-53 3350, a 35 ft bus 8400). Bodies carry `wall_t_m` /
  `ceiling_t_m` (a converted van loses 0.12 m a side and 0.15 m of
  headroom) and `roof_kg`. `VehicleDesign._masses`: laden = curb + a full
  tank (0.74 / 0.84 kg/L) + fresh water + propane + GEAR_KG + a person per
  seat; `laden_out_kg` adds the grey and black tanks (the way home);
  payload = GVWR − laden (`payload_dry_kg` = GVWR − curb). A battery's mass
  and box follow its kWh (12 kg/kWh, 0.018 m³/kWh), a tank's shell its
  litres (0.065 kg/L), propane its lb (`resolve_interior_element`; a typed
  size wins). `_axle_loads` is the lever rule over every mass at its own z
  (the chassis at `cg_wb`, the body at its middle, each piece inside, the
  water in its tanks, the fuel at mid-wheelbase, the driver at the wheel
  and the rest in the seats, roof items on the roof, the gear in the box):
  `axle_f_kg` / `axle_r_kg` (every rear axle together), a trailer's
  `tongue_kg` / `tongue_pct` at the coupler, `cg_z` / `cg_y` and the roof
  load's `cg_rise_m`. A tractor + container is three axle groups on two
  frames, so the semi gets no axle check (`axle_check` false). Checks:
  over the GVWR loaded (error) or only with grey + black full (warn), a
  rear / front axle over its rating, under 20 % on the front, a tongue
  under 10 % (sway) or over 15 %, a trailer over 3,000 lb with no brakes,
  over 13' 6" with the roof items (`overall_h_m`), over 102" with
  side-mounted items (an awning or ladder is an appurtenance: 6" a side is
  allowed, 49 CFR 658.16), the roof load over `roof_kg_max`, a wet bath
  with no black tank (info). New elements: `black_tank`, `propane`
  (bottles of lb), `heater`, `water_heater`, `shore_inlet` (reported as
  `systems.shore_w`; the graph's controller type has no AC-in handle, so
  it is not wired yet). `VehicleGraph` wires each solar item's modules in
  SERIES STRINGS (`string_len`: the longest of 3 / 2 / 1 under the 150 V
  cap with cold headroom that divides the count) in parallel on the MPPT;
  past MAX_PANEL_NODES one node per string. Towing: `VehicleEnergy
  .at_speed(d, v, trailer)` adds the trailer's rolling load and its drag at
  `TRAILER_DRAFT` 0.7 (range_mi / energy_for_distance / trip take it;
  PlacedVehicle and SiteCost.running_for_record pass the hitched trailer);
  `VehicleTow.tow_check(tow, trailer)` = the trailer vs `tow_kg`, the pair
  vs `gcwr_kg`, the tongue vs the hitch class (SAE J684 II–V by tow
  rating), brakes, and the ball vs coupler height (from `frame_h_m`; a
  drop / rise hitch past 8 cm) — `hitch_to` toasts its first two notes.
  Trailer axles sit at 0.58 of the box (a tenth on the tongue). Presets
  were re-laid for it (black tanks, the van's water forward, two seats on
  the camper van, the motorhome's dinette back) and the skoolie's mpg band
  widened to 6–10 (the old 10.4 t curb had held it at 9). Catalog: the
  Sprinter 3500 cab chassis (the Class C's real base); a 20 ft travel
  trailer overloads a 3,500 lb single axle, so that chassis is "other".
- **Design rules and geometry (polish Phase 2, 2026-11-02).** Every check
  carries `why` (the banner's tooltip) and `ids` ("Show it" selects an
  interior element with the skin off, or a roof / side item with it on).
  Rules: rear overhang past 2/3 of the wheelbase (`rear_overhang_m`,
  `OVERHANG_MAX_WB`; the catalog test holds every combination, this is the
  player's warn); a solar array that hangs off its face loses whole
  COLUMNS then rows (`cut_cols` / `cut_rows`, the watts follow — the roof
  face reaches `ROOF_CORNER_SHARE` 0.6 of the corner radius, since two
  1.134 m modules across a 2.44 m bus roof is how skoolies are built);
  `VehicleExterior.checks`: two items on one face overlap (a `rack` is
  mounted on, never an overlap), a side item across the side door or over
  a window; `VehicleInterior.checks`: seats ≥ sleepers (not trailers), a
  shower needs fresh + grey, loads need a house battery (an EV's pack
  counts), AC loads (`ac_load` types) need an inverter rated for them
  (`inverter_w`, the inverter type's `supply_w` 2 kW) or a shore inlet, a
  bed under `BED_MIN_M` 1.85, water days at CampProvisioning's 50 L
  (warn under a day, note under three), headroom `STAND_M` 1.85 (a stock
  school bus's 6' 2" — the plan's 1.9 flagged every unraised skoolie) warn
  / `CROUCH_M` 1.5 note, trailers included. Access: the cab walk-through
  is a `CAB_WALK_M` strip between a van's seats or beside a bus's driver
  (`cab_walk_x`); a step van has none — its curb-side cab door is its side
  door (`sliding_step`), an entry on the right only. `VehicleInterior
  .access` is cached on `d["access"]` (one flood per solve). Windows:
  `VehicleDesign.window_spans` is the ONE window rule — bus / band runs,
  and a "few" body gets a pane over each bed, dinette, sofa or bench on
  the wall it stands against (a bed across the box looks out both sides),
  trimmed back from the side door and from tall fixtures, capped at
  `WINDOW_MAX_M`, merged when touching, one mid-box pane each side with
  nothing to look out from; the builder draws them, the side-item checks
  read them. `_cargo` and the builder's rear door read `door_spans`.
  Geometry: wheel arches (`_wheel_arches`, a dark fender box + lip at
  each outer wheel under the cab's and the shell's panels, `ARCH_CLEAR_M`),
  lugs by weight class (`lug_count`: 5 under 5 t, 8 under 12 t, else 10),
  ONE wheel ArrayMesh per (r, w, side) shared by every wheel of that size,
  a dually pair `DUAL_GAP_M` 0.05 apart and pushed inside the body
  together, a grille with slats on van / cutaway noses, headlamps 30 × 16
  cm in a 6 cm bezel, tail lamps 12 × 34 cm, a `BUS_STEP_M` tread under a
  bus door and a running board under a van's, the Class A windshield from
  `y0 + 0.9` (the real 1.6 m), a trailer's propane on the tongue (drawn by
  `_chassis` from `propane_lb`, not inside). The look gate is
  `tools/diag/vehicle_preset_grid_diag.gd`. ⚠ A multi-line lambda body
  inside call arguments needs its expression in parentheses
  (`func(w): return (a\n and b)`), or GDScript reads the second line as a
  stray argument.
- **Transport lifecycle (polish Phase 3, 2026-11-02).** Vehicles leave,
  crates go back in, and every place that moves cargo uses ONE rule:
  - **Leaving.** A record's `departure` = {start_h, route [spot, the
    pull-out point `APPROACH_M` ahead, the road, the gate, outside], park,
    out: true, by}: PARKED before `start_h`, DRIVING (creeping out first),
    then AWAY. `VehicleDrive.make_out` / `pose_of(rec, h)` / `pose_for(arr,
    dep, h, ...)` / `parked_at` / `leave_h` / `gone_h`; plans are cached,
    oldest dropped past `PLAN_CACHE_MAX` 64. `VehicleDriveRuntime` draws
    both legs; a hitched trailer follows its tow vehicle's arrival AND
    departure. `TerrainLoader.schedule_vehicle_departures(start, spacing,
    by)` (the one nearest the gate LAST, no sooner than it parked) /
    `_auto` / `clear_vehicle_departures(by)`. A Pack-up event whose crews
    finish schedules them (`SiteDeployDirector.DEPART_AFTER_H` 2 min,
    `by` = the event id); scrubbing back past that event takes them back.
    Camps panel: "Drive out" beside "Drive in"; "Already here" clears both.
    `vehicle_arrivals()` lists every scheduled drive with park_h (−INF =
    here from the start), leave_h / gone_h (INF = staying) and `camp_id`;
    the bridge's camp is home while any of its scheduled vehicles stands
    on site, away before the first parks and after the last is gone. Both
    legs were already billed (`VehicleEnergy.trip` is a round trip).
  - **One host model** (`VehicleCargo`): `is_host` / `host_bay(rec)` (a
    container's interior in the same solver frame as a vehicle's bay) /
    `door_xz(rec)` (THE door rule; `UnpackScenario.door_xz` delegates; a
    container's door is local +Z, 1 m out) / `host_ready(rec, h,
    drive_rec)` (not packed, the vehicle — or a trailer's tow vehicle —
    parked) / `door_near(records, pos, reach, h)` returns {x, z,
    host_id}, skipping a packed, away or driving vehicle.
  - **One spawn path**: `VehicleCargo.spawn_into(layer, scenario, host_id,
    h)`; `UnpackScenario.spawn` places the container then calls it,
    `spawn_in_vehicle` too. Every stowed crate carries `stow_local`
    [x, y, z, yaw_rel]; staging is sized from the crates (`staging_xz`:
    `STAGE_GAP_M` 2.5 past the door, rows a crate + `STAGE_AISLE_M`
    apart), overflow beside the door (`overflow_xz`). The old door-stack
    constants are gone.
  - **One stowed-crate rule**: `place_stowed(host_rec, crate_rec)`
    (records) and `place_stowed_node(node, host_ground, host_yaw, crate)`
    (nodes). PlacedVehicle (its own bay and the trailer it tows), the drive
    runtime and a hand move of any host (`PlacedPropService._reseat_cargo`
    from `update_prop_record`) all use them. `move_prop_at` clears
    `stow_local` with `stowed_in`.
  - **Pack-up stows crates back**: `door_near`'s `host_id` becomes the
    load-out effect's `stow_in`; `SiteProjectEffects` then calls
    `TerrainLoader.stow_prop_in(pid, host)`, which packs the whole load
    again with the new crate (`VehicleCargo.restow_patches`; what does not
    fit stays at the door). The next deploy takes a stowed kit that has a
    `deploy_home` back out once its host is parked. The pack-up inventory
    skips the forklift and every living vehicle (they drive out).
  - **Unloads are gated and retried** (`_tick_vehicle_logistics`, 1 Hz):
    a delivery is `unload_pending` on the host's `delivery` blob until the
    host stands in its spot (a vehicle still driving in holds its crates),
    a board too full to take it is asked again every `UNLOAD_RETRY_S` 5 s,
    and a vehicle's crew is the camp nearest the camp it belongs to
    (`camp_of_vehicle`: the painted camp it stands in, else the nearest
    camp middle within 300 m; stored as `camp_id`). A clock before the
    host's (or its tow's) arrival cancels the unload and re-stows every
    crate still a crate (`_rewind_unload`).
  - **Forks and a vehicle's bay**: the forks cannot drive in. A heavy
    crate in a vehicle gets a "Slide to the door" row (2–4 people) the
    fork trip waits for, picked up at the door on the ground;
    `SiteProject.fork_fits_door` refuses the forklift when the door is
    narrower than max(forks, load) + 0.1 m.
  - **One handling table**: `PackKitter.HANDLING` (hand ≤ 23 kg, team ≤ 60,
    forklift beyond; `label`, `labour_scale` — the forklift class's lifting
    labour is halved, an estimate). `NpcHaulModel.SOLO_LIFT_KG`,
    `crate_needs_forklift`, `ForkliftRig.liftable`, PackingList labels and
    `SiteDeployPlanner.labour_hours` all read it.
  - **Hygiene**: deleting a host sets its crates down beside its door
    (un-stowed, collision on), unhitches a partner (`PlacedVehicle
    .unhitch_prop` now clears the records when no live runtime holds the
    hitch), empties a forklift whose load is deleted; a duplicate drops
    delivery / towing / hitched_to / arrival / departure / fork_load_id /
    stow keys / camp_id. A vehicle somebody is driving is not scheduled.
    The forklift saves its load's place on the forks (`fork_load_off`) and
    writes null, never "", for an empty fork. A vehicle bay's packing-list
    labels are `V1-…`.
  - Gates: `vehiclelab_selftest` `_test_transport_lifecycle` (740),
    `site_deploy_selftest` (85), and with real input on Walton:
    `vehicle_cargo_check` (22: rewind restow, load-out stow, drive out,
    camp away, scrub back), `vehicle_arrival_check` (28: a cargo trailer
    following both ways), `forklift_unload_check` (22: the box-truck bay
    phase), new `vehicle_delete_check` (9).
- **UX (polish Phase 4, 2026-11-02).**
  - **Designer:** the summary and checks lead the right column, and the
    header's badge ("2 problems to fix" / "1 warning" / "Checks pass",
    `DesignerShell.set_badge`, a click scrolls to them) counts them. Paint
    and "Your vehicle's model" start folded. Wheelbase is a choice of the
    chassis' factory wheelbases (`VehicleCatalog.WHEELBASES_IN`, only the
    published ones; one = disabled, an older design's own number stays
    choosable); Fuel is read-only from the chassis. Words, not ids
    (`VehicleExterior.face_word`, `FUEL_WORDS`, "another type's" chassis).
    Save design is in the footer (reachable at 720 without the flyout); a
    name clash asks "Replace?"; Forget and Apply toast; Place is disabled
    with a reason on a scene with no loader; type buttons say they start
    over (Ctrl+Z undoes); shortcuts ride the tooltips (undo / redo, Remove
    = Del / Backspace, Shift-click keeps a tool, R turns). The roof / side
    palette is grouped (`VehicleExterior.TOOL_GROUPS`: Power / Comfort /

  - **One units setting** (`UnitsPref`, core/units_pref.gd, ui_prefs.cfg

    and fuel. Toggle: the designer's trip section.
  - **Transport surfaces:** the Packing Lab with a vehicle's bay picked
    reads "Load into <vehicle>" and stows the kit there
    (`deliver_kit_in_vehicle`); Deliver and Load keep the Lab open and
    toast. Deploy chip menu → Vehicles: drive in / drive out / simply here
    (with the gate rule in the separator); the Site Projects deploy header
    has Drive in / Drive out. The camps panel's arrival line has its own
    wrapped row and a "place a Site gate" hint; each camp lists its
    vehicles as chips with Look and a "Getting here" line
    (`vehicles_by_camp` now carries ids and positions). The ride dashboard
    has a hint line (`PlacedVehicle.dashboard_hint`: a trailer within 20 m
    to back onto, the fork keys on a forklift). The prop editor shows

    (`SystemGraphView.fuel_store_near`) and "Hitch nearest trailer"

    "[E] Drive <name> · [Click] Edit". The forks are InputMap actions
    `fork_raise` / `fork_lower` (PgUp / PgDn, rebindable), and the F1
    overlay lists drive / hitch / refuel / forks / load.
  - **Packing Lab on the kit:** `ui_modal` meta (the modal audit sees it:
    0 errors at 1080 and 720), Lucide icons instead of emoji, `CoordToken`
    site keys (the old "%.4f" keys are still read), empty states, "4
    people: bucket brigade", Empty asks first. NOT done: its own orbit →
    `StudioViewport` (and the intermodal designer's) — a larger refactor
    left for later.
  - Vocabulary: Vehicle designer · Deliver (a kit arrives) · Load / Unload
    (crates into / out of a bay) · Pack up / Unpack (a prop's shipping
    form); the Pack-up button's tooltip says one verb.
  - Tour stop `40a_arrive_at_camp` (Walton): a box truck with a kit in its
    bay drives in through a site gate, parks, and the crew unloads it.
  - Gates: `vehiclelab_designer_check` 66/0 at 1080 and 720 (the new
    order, the badge, factory wheelbases, a REAL click on the units box, a
    REAL click on "Load into" in the Packing Lab), `--capture=modals` at
    both sizes, the tour stop PASS.
- **Performance (polish Phase 5, 2026-11-02).** Measured with
  `tools/bench/vehicle_site_bench.gd` (Walton, festival mode, 40 vehicles
  with kits stowed, idle / 1x / 60x / 450x through an arrival window;
  `VSB_QUICK=1` stops after idle) and two probes,
  `tools/diag/vehicle_place_cost_probe.gd` (what a placement costs, step by
  step) and `tools/diag/ac_shed_cost_probe.gd` (each AC-bus listener timed).
  What it found, largest first:
  - **Every placement took 2.5 s in the graph sync.**
    `sync_vehicle_system` / `remove_vehicle_system` set `_history_suppress`
    but not `_sim_bulk_update`, so each of the dozen items and wires the
    realize / make_unique wrote ran the view's whole change cascade. Both
    now write in bulk mode and fire ONE `_on_model_changed`. Result: 137 ms
    a vehicle; 40 vehicles + kits placed in 11 s instead of 276 s.
  - **A 47 s stall whenever the site's AC shed.** The vehicles' own loads
    counted toward the SITE inverter (`GraphAcLoad` seeded from every
    controller, the vehicles' own included), so 40 vehicles tripped its
    overload, and the shed made ~180 `GraphSimLoad` proxies each write their
    own `update_item` (one full cascade per load, ~130 ms each). Now
    `GraphAcLoad.vehicle_scopes` keeps a vehicle's controller out of the
    site's reachability (its loads run off its own house battery), and
    `GraphSimLoadHost` hears the AC bus ONCE and fans the change out in one
    bulk write (`fan_ac_available`); proxies under the host no longer hook
    the bus themselves. One flip now costs one refresh.
  - **A vehicle's loads run on its own battery** (refinement pass,
    2026-11-03). `SystemGraphView._tick_vehicle_power` (ambient, inside the
    sim-write bracket, beside `_tick_camp_power`) steps each vehicle
    compound with `CampPowerModel.step` (pv = its panels' Wmp × the site's
    yield at the instant, battery = its house bank, inverter = its
    controller's overload watts, load = its appliances that are on), sets
    `set_scope_ac_available` per vehicle scope, writes the battery card's
    SOC (every 0.5 h or a 1 % move) and hands the per-scope AC to
    `GraphSimLoadHost.set_vehicle_ac`. The site's `fan_ac_available` skips
    proxies in vehicle scopes (`ac_for(item_id)` is the one answer). A
    scrub back or a > 6 h jump holds. `vehicle_power_states()` for probes.
    Gate: `tools\harness.ps1 -World walton -RunScript res://tools/checks/vehicle_power_doors_check.gd -Label vehicle_power_doors -Timeout 900`
    (13: site inverter down leaves the van's loads on, a flat van battery at
    night switches them off, a box truck's door open while unloading).
  - **`npc_population` was 40 ms per tick on the festival alone (133 with
    the vehicles)**, almost all in `_service_machine_chores`: every full-
    tier camp re-walked the whole graph with `GraphNesting.walk_items`, which
    called the linear `get_items_in_scope` once per scope. `walk_items` now
    groups items by scope in one pass (same order), and the bridge lists
    the waiting machines once per tick (`_waiting_machines`). 4.5 ms festival
    only, 6.5 ms with 40 vehicles; this predated the vehicles.
  - The plan's own items, all landed: the design cache is LRU on a hashed
    pre-key with a solve-miss counter and `solve_transient` for designer
    drags; `VehicleDriveRuntime` sleeps (`set_process(false)`) until an
    arrival / departure / hitch wakes it (group `vehicle_drive_runtimes`,
    `TerrainLoader._wake_drive_runtimes`), and its plan key is an Array
    hash; PlacedVehicle caches Main, checks the charger every 3 s, tests the
    trailer chassis prefix before any solve and saves once per move; the
    builder caches wheel refs, one-sided materials (weakref-checked) and
    part meshes by design key (`MESH_CACHE_MAX` 32) and can rebuild only
    Exterior or Interior (`rebuild_part`, the designer's drags); id indices
    on `PlacedPropLayer.find_by_id` and `PlacedPropRuntime.find_by_prop_id`;
    the director precomputes doors and the forklift once per inventory;
    `_show_props(ids)` replaces full prop rebuilds when a kit is delivered or
    an unload rewinds; `vehicle_arrivals()` is cached 500 ms. PerfSpan
    sections `vehicle_drive`, `vehicle_cargo`, `forklift`, `npc_beds`,
    `prop_rev`, `sui_solar` / `sui_load` / `sui_battery` / `sui_board` /
    `sui_over`.
  - `_prop_revision` never moved during the bench (0/s): the plan's premise
    that it churned while vehicles drive was wrong, so it was only measured.
  - Bench (Walton, before → after, frame median): festival only 78 → 51 ms;
    40 vehicles idle 98 → 69 ms; 1x 85 → 61; 450x 90 → 71. `vehicle_drive`
    0.02 ms idle, ~1.5 ms with 40 on the road. What remains is ~1300 more
    draw calls for 40 vehicles and the GPU.
- **Shuttle bodies (2026-11-03, from a SketchUp model of an Aerotech-class
  E-450 shuttle and the owner's photos of the Magic Tool Bus).**
  - Body keys (VehicleSpec.BODY_KEYS): `front_cap` + `cap_len_m` (the
    fiberglass wedge over a cutaway's cab, `_front_cap`), `end_r_m` (the
    box's vertical corners rounded in plan; the roof edge rounds down with
    them; a raked front is never rounded), `skirt_h_m` (side panels down to
    that height with real arches cut round the wheels and a dark well behind,
    `VehicleDesign.side_arches` / `_skirt`), `door_w_m` (the entry door),
    `lift_door` none | front | mid | rear + `lift_door_w_m` +
    `lift_door_at_m` (a typed front edge from the living box's front; the
    designer's position pick erases it).
  - `VehicleDesign.lift_door_span` is the ONE lift rule: the asked-for spot
    if it is clear, else the nearest spot clear of every wheel arch and of
    the entry door; {} when none fits. It is a side door span with
    `kind: "lift"` (every span now carries `kind`), so entries, the
    exterior checks and windows see it. The cargo bay loads through the
    WIDEST side door, and CargoDoors opens that same one.
  - A band of windows skips curb-side panes a door stands in, and panes a
    side-mounted solar array covers (blacked-out windows); each run of
    panes sits in a dark surround.
  - The van / cutaway nose is a loft (`_van_cab`) through rounded sections
    (`_rr_ring`), the arch cut into the sections' bottom; `_loft` is the
    generic helper (normals smoothed under ~53°, faces turned outward). The
    body is lofted too: stations along z, flat in the middle, a quarter
    circle at a rounded end. Its end caps fan from the profile's middle, NOT
    the ring centroid (the crown carries most points; a centroid fan cut
    through a Sprinter's cab, `_test_driver_view` caught it).
  - Liveries (`paint.livery` two_tone | transit + `livery_a` / `_b`):
    `VehicleBuilder.livery_image` paints an image column by column, laid on
    like a wrap. ⚠ Godot's triplanar already flips Y: `_triplanar_body`
    scales +1/H. Every wrap image had been drawn upside down before.
  - Bus doors draw as bifold glass leaves; the outside step only where the
    sill stands over 0.45 m (a skirted shuttle's stepwell is inside).
  - Preset `magic_tool_bus` (catalog `vehiclelab_magic_tool_bus`): 25 ft,
    176" E-450, ex-TriMet livery, lift doors behind the entry door, 4 ×
    400 W on the roof, 6 × 100 W (`rigid_100`, added) over the curb-side
    windows, a hitch. Its numbers come from the photos (the front tyre as
    scale) — `_test_shuttle_body` holds them.
- **Looks and walk-in (2026-11-08).** The bodies stopped being painted
  boxes with windows laid over them, and the player can open the doors and
  walk inside.
  - **Real openings.** `_body` skips the loft's flat side walls and underside
    and draws them through `_cut_panel(outline, holes, notches)`: the outline
    cut into strips at every hole's edges (so a hole only ever notches a
    strip: `Geometry2D` clips never return a polygon with a hole), minus
    windows, doors and wheel arches (`body_arches`: every body, not only
    skirted ones). The rear face and an integral body's windshield are cut the
    same way. Inside: a `liner` wall at the house width with the same holes,
    jambs between skin and liner, a headliner, a bulkhead liner.
  - **Nodes.** `PARTS` = Chassis / Cab / Shell / Glass / Exterior / Interior;
    `CUTAWAY_HIDES` = Shell, Glass, Exterior (and Doors). `Glass` holds every
    see-through pane (kit "pane", alpha, double-sided) and casts NO shadow, so
    the sun reaches the room. The old opaque "glass" kit stays for cabs that
    are not lofts (tractor) and the cab-over bunk's window.
  - **Doors are leaves** (`_door_leaves`, node `Doors/D<span>_<leaf>`): meshes
    in VEHICLE coordinates (a livery runs across them; shut = identity), meta
    `open_xf` / `door` (index in `VehicleDesign.door_spans`) / `where` /
    `kind`. Bus and lift doors are two leaves swinging out, a slider slides
    back, a hinged door swings forward, barn doors swing round, a roll-up
    scales to a strip at the header, a lift gate swings up.
    `VehicleBuilder.set_doors_open(model, door | -1, t)`.
  - **Cabs.** A van / cutaway nose (`_van_cab`) and a cab-over (`_cabover_cab`)
    are lofts of `_rr_ring` sections, which now carry a vertex each side at
    the belt line: the windshield (edges `RR_TOP_R/L` between the cowl and
    header stations) and the door glass (`RR_WIN_R/L`) are quads of the loft
    handed to the pane kit, so they are flush and see-through. A full van
    (`euro`) has a shorter, steeper nose (`nose_hood`), its loft is open at
    the back into the body, its door glass carries on in the body's wall
    (`cab_wins`), and the high roof is a cap lofted from the windshield header
    into the body's roof. A conventional hood (`_hood_loft`: school bus,
    tractor) tapers to a slatted grille with a fender band over each wheel.
    `_cab_interior` draws seats, dash and steering wheel behind the glass.
  - **Wheels** are lathed (`_K.lathe`: profile (axial, radius), outside on the
    left of its direction): rounded shoulders, tread grooves, a dished rim
    with hand holes, lug nuts on the "metal" surface.
  - **Paint** is `_paint` (clear coat, double-sided) for body / roof / door,
    wraps and liveries too.
  - **Walk-in collision.** Nothing drawn collides (`skip_prop_collision` on
    every part, wheel and leaf). `collision_boxes(d)` (pure) → the hidden
    `CollisionMesh`: floor, walls with the doorways left open
    (`door_gaps(d)`, at least `WALK_GAP_M` 0.9 wide), a roof never lower than
    `WALK_HEAD_M` 1.86 over the floor, the cab / hood, and furniture 0.26 m
    slimmer than drawn (aisles are sized for hips, the capsule is 0.7 m).
  - **`VehicleWalkIn`** (gameplay/, attached by PlacedPropRuntime beside
    PlacedVehicle, trailers too; group `vehicle_walk_in`): a StaticBody under
    the builder root with, per doorway, a BLOCKER (shut) and a RAMP from the
    ground to the sill (open: the player has no step-up); the leaf animation;
    `door_at(origin, dir)` = ray vs the leaves where they stand now; dome
    lights along the ceiling (no shadows, distance-faded: a player's world
    ambient can be ~0); `set_cargo_open` (CargoDoors delegates to it for
    living vehicles: an unload opens the real door; `CargoDoors.is_open`).
    It follows the prop's own collision: driven / towed / on the road in, the
    doors shut and the body leaves the world.
  - **Interact.** `InteractionFocus._update_door_focus` runs before the
    Ctrl-gated prop pick (no modifier): a door under the crosshair shows
    "[key] Open the sliding door" and Interact toggles it; the player's own
    proximity mount stands down while `has_door_focus()`. Anywhere else,
    Interact still drives. ⚠ The other focus clears blank the crosshair
    prompt: set the door prompt AFTER them.
  - Gates: `vehiclelab_selftest` `_test_walk_in` (872 checks in all),
    `tools/checks/vehicle_walkin_check.gd`, tour stop `18ja_walk_in_vehicle`.
    Look check: `vehicle_preset_grid_diag.gd --views=low,cab,rear`.

  - **Designer (same day).** Pictured "Start from" list (thumbnail, name,
    "24 ft · sleeps 2"; the type buttons folded under "By vehicle type"),

    Frame (`set_view(id)`), six headline tiles over "All the numbers", a

    ⚠ `rebuild_part` builds its own kit list: a kit added to the Interior or

- **Traps found:** Python `open(p, 'w')` on Windows writes CRLF — always
  `newline=''`, and some files here ARE CRLF (unified_library_modal.gd):
  match their endings; a bash heredoc collapses backslashes — write patch
  scripts with the Write tool and use raw strings for GDScript `\`
  continuations.

## Site deployment schedule — "set a time, everyone builds / packs" (2026-10-26)

Plan: `plans/DEPLOY_SCHEDULE_PLAN.md`. Deployable infrastructure as a game
mechanic: the timeline's **Deploy** chip (or the festival panel's "Deploy
from now" / "Pack up from now") puts a DEPLOY or PACK-UP event at the
playhead; when the clock crosses it, the camps' people build every packed
structure and pitch every struck camp (or take it all down and pack it),
and the site lives in it. Flags on the clips lane (drag to retime,
right-click, double-click to jump); the chip reads green while a crew is on
it. Everything rides the existing Site Projects pipeline; nothing was
duplicated.
- **`SiteDeploySchedule`** (pure): the per-world record (WorldPaths kind
  `deploy_schedule`, `TerrainLoader.deploy_schedule_path`) — events
  `{id, action deploy|packup, at_h}` and a `fired` stamp per event that
  carries what a reload needs (crews, items, pending, projects, done).
  `due(prev, now)` = forward crossings not yet fired; `rewound` = fired
  events the clock went back past; moving an event clears its stamp.
- **`SiteDeployPlanner`** (pure): inventory items (props with a packed spec,
  painted camps) → `pick_crews` (nearest camps to the work until
  `ALL_HANDS_MAX_PEOPLE` 320) → `assign` (nearest crew with board room: rows
  + one project slot; the rest wait) → `rows_for(item, action, roster)`:
  linkage = the rebuild / breakdown rows; pallet rack = unpack → raise
  frames (four) → decks → finish (unpack_prop); any other packable prop =
  lay out → assemble (ghost firming through `set_build_phase`) → finish;
  pack-up = take down (ghost) → pack (pack_prop); a camp = one pitch /
  strike row with the new `set_camp_built` effect. Labour is PERSON-HOURS
  from the packed mass (0.4 + kg/40, pack-up ×0.6) — estimates, tune there.
- **`SiteDeployDirector`** (SystemGraphView `site_deploy()`, ticked after
  the bridge): fires due events (toast + "tap to watch"), pins the picked
  crews as **ALL HANDS** (`NpcPopulationBridge.set_all_hands`: forced FULL
  tier after `CrowdFocus.decide`, ctx `all_hands` through `_make_ctx`, and
  in `NpcAgent._step_idle` the board beats every LEISURE block — a festival
  day is SOCIAL all afternoon and `_begin_social` always succeeds, so
  without this nobody ever reached the board), creates one project per item
  (kinds `site_deploy` / `site_packup`; `SiteProject.is_build_kind` /
  `is_breakdown_kind` drive the linkage ghost push), retries pending items
  every tick as boards free up, pushes a camp's live built fraction from
  the project rollup, releases the crews when all are done. A backward
  scrub past a fired event cancels its projects and puts every item back
  INSTANTLY (the fire's scrub rule, as far as a simulated crew allows);
  the chip's "Pack / Deploy everything now, no crew" does the same for
  setting up a before-state.
- **World reveal**: a packed prop with `build_state` that is not a linkage
  falls through to its REAL model, ghosted, with the kit crate beside it
  (`PlacedPropRuntime`, `packed_build`); the pack effect clears
  `build_state` + `build_run` (left on, the crate rendered as a ghost
  forever). `PalletRackBuildSite` gained LABOUR mode (progress × makespan,
  lanes only for people on site, NpcStandIns). Painted camps carry `built`
  (CampAreaLayer, default true); `CampAreaRuntime.set_built_fraction` hides
  household instances (`visible_instance_count`, prefix per class batch),
  their lights, and the shelters / shades / solids people use (entries carry
  `ix` / `n` in their batch), so a struck camp offers no beds and its people
  sleep on the ground until it is pitched.
- Caps raised: `SiteProjectStore.MAX_PROJECTS` 8 → 48 (one project per
  structure). Boards stay at 160 chores; the planner spreads items over the
  nearest crews and the rest wait.
- **Per-part staging (`gameplay/assembly_build_site.gd`, `AssemblyBuildSite`,
  second pass the same day).** Every non-linkage, non-rack prop a crew
  builds or packs gets a labour-mode site (`build_run = {mode: "labour",
  action, iid, project_id}`, attached by PlacedPropRuntime beside the
  generic ghost, which it hides while it owns the picture). It reads the
  project's PER-TASK fractions (`SiteProject.task_fractions`, carried by
  `linkage_build_status` as `tasks`) through the pure `stage_state`:
  deploy = `lay_out` lays the parts in a yard beside the crate, `assemble`
  seats them one at a time bottom up (`part_seat`); pack-up = `strip`
  takes them down to the yard, `pack` takes them into the crate. Two ways
  of cutting a structure into parts: the designer builders with an
  `assembly` build option (dome & zome, toroid, flat-pack) are REBUILT at a
  quantised fraction (`BUILDER_STEPS` 24, their own ring / part drop-in);
  everything else (a GLB, a gantry) is instantiated once through the shared
  `PlacedPropRuntime.model_extras` and SPLIT into its mesh instances (one
  mesh of several surfaces splits per surface), sorted bottom up, each part
  gliding from its yard spot to its seat with a lift. The real people on
  the chore stand at the prop in their work poses; the site draws no crew
  of its own.
- **One structure at a time**: the prop editor's "Crew: build" / "Crew:
  pack up" (every packable thing but a linkage, which keeps its own pair)
  go through `SiteDeployDirector.queue_item(kind, id, action)` — the same
  rows and staging, the nearest crew with board room, pinned ALL HANDS if
  it has no board yet, waiting under the record's `manual` stamp that the
  tick services like an event's. A pack-up near a cargo container (200 m)
  ends with the crate carried to its door (`item.loadout` → the `load_out`
  row; the linkage breakdown rows take the same).
- Polish: the Site Projects panel heads its list with the live deployment
  line, a progress bar and **Watch** (the settlement view over the busiest
  work site); the active flag's tag on the timeline fills with the crews'
  progress; the chip's no-crew actions ask first (ConfirmationDialog naming
  what they will swap).
- **No twin, no ghost (2026-10-27, Tool Camp 26).** The "full rack standing
  where they build it" was the PLAN crashing: a pitched roof's
  `ply:roof:i,j` sheets hit the deck pass (`bits[2]` out of bounds), the
  script error aborted the module, and 244 of 557 build units got no job —
  `_apply_units` never touched them, so they stood finished from frame one.
  `PalletRackBuildPlan` now splits a rack into `_plan_racking` (frames +
  beams, every joined rack in turn) and `_plan_fitout` (decks, the pitched
  roof — packing, rafters in fives, sheets in sixes — steps, walls,
  elements), and EVERY fit-out job waits for ALL the racking. Any new unit
  id family must land in a bucket there, or it will stand finished again
  (the selftest pins "every Tool Camp piece planned").
  Both staging sites (`PalletRackBuildSite`, `AssemblyBuildSite`) never show
  the prop's own model while it is `under_construction` (that model IS the
  ghost): suspended / finished / disposed fall back to the kit crate
  (`_show_model`), and the rack site holds its last frame until the prop
  is rebuilt for real. The rack site hides the KitCrate while its yard is
  out, plays a PACK-UP backwards (`(1 − progress) × makespan`), and moves
  its work loops off the clock's own steps when the clock is held but moving
  (the video export). Gate: `tools\harness.ps1 -World walton -RunScript
  res://tools/checks/tool_camp_build_video.gd -Label tool_camp_build`
  (`TCV_VIDEO=0` checks only; with the video it films a second rack into
  the user's Videos folder; `TCV_SPAN_H` 4.5 fits the build). ⚠ The
  project lives on ONE camp's board, so its roster is the crew: the
  sandbox's festival target (60 people = 2 a camp) made a 10 h build;
  the script resets the target to natural (1053 on Walton, crew 12,
  ~3 sim-h) and starts at noon (Walton's valley fog hides the morning).
  The rack site hides its progress label while the 🎬 export or preview
  holds the clock. Offline: `tools/diag/rack_build_order_diag.gd
  -- --preset=<id>` prints the job order and what is up at 0/10/…/100 %.
- **Every structure, piece by piece (2026-10-27).** A scheduled deploy or
  pack-up of ANY prop — dome / zome, toroid, Linkage Lab frame, gantry,
  flat-pack, a GLB — runs on the same crew site as a rack
  (`PalletRackBuildSite`; `is_schedule_run` = labour mode with an
  `action`, stamped by the director for every model with `crew_n`):
  - `StructureUnits` (`core/assembly/structure_units.gd`) cuts the REAL
    model into pieces: each MultiMesh instance (poses from the builder's
    `instance_transforms()` when it has one — the linkage builder; a
    headless MultiMesh keeps no transforms), each MeshInstance3D surface
    split into welded connected components; bits under `SMALL_M` ride with
    the nearest piece; > `MAX_UNITS` gathered on a grid; one surface per
    material (`_concat`, the 256-surface cap). Pile kind from the flat frame
    (frames / beams / sheets / parts), `stage` = 1.2 m height band × 4 +
    kind rank. Scale baked in, `ground_shift` = the lowest piece; the site
    stands at the ModelRoot's rotation + that shift (`_site_xf`). Cut cached
    by `look_key` (cost: 25–600 ms, the 216-plate corten zome 2.7 s, once).
  - `PalletRackBuildPlan.plan_units` schedules stage after stage, small
    bundles round the structure, carried and fitted one by one (`PIECE_*`
    tables); same timeline as the rack, no visitor.
  - A linkage frame is cut and built FOLDED (effective min fold); the
    finish unpacks it and the deploy sweep raises it. A linkage pack-up
    stows first (`_stow_then_stamp`, the stamp deferred a frame — stamping
    inside `deploy_state_changed` frees the emitting runtime: native crash).
  - The planner's rows lost their `set_build_phase` ghost stamps (only the
    finish unpacks, only the pack packs); the linkage rebuild / breakdown
    rows are the Lab / Site Projects path's now. The unpack effect KEEPS a
    schedule run so the finished prop's site draws the last pieces (they
    trail the labour), carrying the drawn time across the rebuild (`_carry`)
    and clearing the run itself when done (`_finish_run`). The read and the
